## Second-pass notes

**N401.1 — scan 401 — implication not pursued (second pass).**
The "pas extérieurs !" of the equivalence fits a Birman-type picture: once a hole is filled, its point can serve as a base point, so the result is a genuine group of type (g,ν−1) rather than an exterior one. On that reading the functor needs a chosen hole on the source side, which the sentence leaves implicit. Confidence medium; the page does not state the mechanism.

**N403.1 — scan 403 — claim without proof (second pass).**
The parenthesis reads "(ce qui trivialt. (or moralt.) revient à se donner une clôture alg. Q̄ de Q …)". For G = Gal(Q̄/Q), G-torsors correspond to algebraic closures Ω of Q, via P ≅ Isom(Q̄, Ω). For a torsor under 𝕀Γ_{g,ν} this presupposes 𝕀Γ_{g,ν} ≅ Gal(Q̄/Q), the identification the whole construction is aiming at. So whichever adverb the ink holds, the equivalence is heuristic; the witnesses' "moralement" says so outright.

**N403.2 — scan 403 — implication not pursued (second pass).**
A plausible reason for the (0,3) exception: M_{0,3} is a point over Q, so the π_1 of M_{0,3,Q̄} is trivial and compactification conditions have nothing to act on. For (1,1) the geometric π_1 is the profinite completion of SL_2(Z), so such conditions can bite. This is my gloss, not a reason stated by the author.

**N404.1 — scan 404, margin — claim without proof (second pass).**
"Le cas où P est le torseur trivial, est celui des π ext (?) munis d'une prédiscrétification orientée α (d'où une suite exacte 1 → T̂_α → 𝒩_α → 𝕀Γ_α → 1)". Neither the identification of a trivialised torsor with an oriented prediscretification nor the exactness is argued. Exactness in the middle is the analogue for α of 𝒩_{g,ν}/T̂_{g,ν} = 𝕀Γ_{g,ν}. 𝒩_α must first be defined from α; I assume it is the subgroup of 𝒩_a compatible with α, which the note does not say.

**N405.1 — scan 405 — claim without proof (second pass).**
"Or ceci revient exactement à ⓖ". This assumes, as the surrounding text suggests, that compatibility with the arithmetisations means differing by an element of 𝒩_{g,ν}.
- *ⓖ suffices.* Let u_0 be compatible and u another isomorphism of the stated kind. Then g = u u_0^{−1} normalises T̂_{g,ν} and transports the open subgroup u_0(Γ′·Σ) of 𝒩_{g,ν} into 𝒩_{g,ν}, so ⓖ gives g ∈ 𝒩_{g,ν}.
- *The converse needs a splitting.* Since such g normalise T̂_{g,ν}, ⓖ need only be checked for open 𝒩′ ⊇ T̂_{g,ν}. Recovering it from the stated condition needs each such 𝒩′ to be of the form u_0(Γ′·Σ) with Γ′ ∩ Σ = (1), i.e. a splitting of 𝒩′ → 𝒩′/T̂_{g,ν}. So "exactement" holds only given such quasi-sections.

**N407.1 — scan 407 — textual and mathematical point (second pass).**
The ink reads "on aura un hom canonique T̂(π) → T̂(π′)" with one hat on each T. The double-hatted T̂̂ of 401, 404 (19) and 405 shows two clearly stacked hats. Since 𝒩_a ⊂ T̂̂(π) (404 (19), 405) and 𝒩_a is larger than T̂_a, a map defined only on T̂(π) cannot induce the top row 𝒩_a → 𝒩_{a′} of (22). So T̂̂(π) → T̂̂(π′) is meant, as CSG and IUT print it; the single hats are probably a slip of the pen, and the transcription keeps the ink.

**N408.1 — scan 408 — own idea: proof sketch (second pass).**
Read "quasi-section of 𝒩_{a′} over 𝕀Γ_{a′}" as a closed subgroup that meets T̂_{a′} trivially and maps onto an open subgroup of 𝕀Γ_{a′}, and take Γ ⊂ 𝒩_a to be one over 𝕀Γ_a. Then (23) follows formally from (21)–(22).
1. Since (21) gives 𝕀Γ_a ⥲ 𝕀Γ_{a′} and (22) is compatible with the quotient maps, an element of Γ whose image lies in T̂_{a′} (in particular is 1) has trivial image in 𝕀Γ_a.
2. Such an element therefore lies in Γ ∩ T̂_a = 1, so the composite is injective and its image meets T̂_{a′} trivially; its image in 𝕀Γ_{a′} is open.

Confidence high for that reading of "quasi-section", which these pages do not define.

**N409.1 — scan 409 — claim without proof / notation (second pass).**
(24) is written Γ → π′(i′), yet it is said to "relever son action extérieure". A lift of the outer action Γ → Out(π′) is naturally a homomorphism to Aut(π′(i′)), the automorphisms of the vertex group at the Γ-fixed object i′, or a section of the corresponding extension; it is not a map into π′(i′) itself. The display probably abbreviates one of these. As written, its target does not match the sentence.

**N410.1 — scan 410 — implication not pursued (second pass).**
The margin "il faut pour ceci les restrictions anabéliennes habituelles" presumably requires both types, (g,ν) and (g, ν − Card I′), to stay anabelian, i.e. 2g − 2 + ν > 0 before and after filling. Otherwise π′ is abelian or trivial, and the condition π′^Γ = 1 and the sets Pts(π′, α′, Γ) change character. The exact restrictions are not stated on the page.

**N410.2 — scans 409–410 — own idea: proof sketch (second pass).**
For a fixed π′, the reduction to two points is formal on the groupoid side of 409. Whether i′ and j′ give the same π′-conjugacy class of liftings depends only on the full subgroupoid on {i′, j′}. That subgroupoid is Γ-stable, since Γ fixes both objects, and still describes π′, since any nonempty set of objects does. If "Card I′ = 2" instead means filling only two holes, the reduction also needs the point maps to be compatible with filling the remaining holes, a passage that can merge points; so the groupoid reading is the one under which the reduction holds as stated. Confidence medium.

# LM_P042 — cote 140-2, scans 411–420  [source: second_pass\LM_P042_notes_checked.md]

# LM_P042 (scans 411–420): research notes, checked against the corrected text

Each first-pass note (numbered as in `answers/unzipped/LM_P042/LM_P042_notes.md`, section 5) is kept, corrected or dropped against `LM_P042_checked.tex`. Notes added in the second pass are labelled **(second pass, own)**. Quotations are from the corrected transcription; π/Π doubts are resolved to π and Γ^♮ is read as a natural sign throughout.

## First-pass notes

1. **Scan 412, condition ① — question. KEEP.** « tt sous-groupe ouvert aussi (et inversement ?) »: the converse, admissibility of Γ deduced from that of an open subgroup, is asked, with a question mark that the witnesses drop.
2. **Scan 412, condition ② — claim stated as axiom. KEEP.** Under « On suppose », bouching a Γ-invariant part I′ gives an admissible operation of Γ on π′. It is a requirement on the notion of admissibility, not a theorem.
3. **Scan 412, lower margin — claim without proof. CORRECT.** The note reads « Il suffit de la poser pour card I′=1, i.e. bouchage d'un trou — du moins si on sait que la condition d'admissibilité ne dépend que de l'action des noyaux des groupes » (tail doubtful). The reduction of ② to one hole is therefore explicitly conditional on that hypothesis, which is nowhere stated or proved on these pages.
4. **Scan 412, ①–② — own idea (first pass). KEEP, reworded.** Testing the one-hole reduction separately for a Γ-fixed hole and for a Γ-orbit of holes is still useful; the corrected margin shows that the author's own reduction rests on a hypothesis about kernels, which is what such a test should probe.
5. **Scan 413, equivalence of systems — claim without proof. KEEP.** « On trouve ainsi une équivalence » between systems (π,a,Γ,ψ,i) of type (g,ν+1) with an admissible exterior operation and a Γ-stable i, and systems (π′,a′,Γ,ψ′) of type (g,ν) with a « vraie » admissible action. No functors on morphisms or natural isomorphisms are given.
6. **Scan 413, pathological lifts — conjecture. KEEP, wording corrected.** « il y aura des relèvements "pathologiques" d'une action cat./ext. admissible donnée… »: the inverse implication is expected to fail; no example is given. The abbreviation before « admissible » is doubtful (cat. or ext.).
7. **Scan 413, condition ③ — claim stated as axiom. KEEP.** If Γ operates effectively and admissibly on π, then π^Γ = (1). Introduced by « On suppose de plus ».
8. **Scan 413, rigidity — implication not proved. KEEP.** « Cela implique que la catégorie des Γ-Pts de π, ou … des sections de B_{π,Γ} (≃ B_u) sur B_Γ, est rigide »: automorphisms of a section are π-elements fixed by Γ, so ③ gives rigidity once every section is shown to come from an admissible effective action.
9. **Scan 413, existence vs rigidity — own idea (first pass). KEEP.** ③ controls automorphisms only; non-emptiness of the category of sections is a separate question, answered on 415 by axiom ④ only after passing to an open subgroup.
10. **Scan 411, opening — explicit doubt. CORRECT.** The margin « pour les isom » (CSG: « [pour les isomorphismes] ») restricts the claimed equivalence of categories to isomorphisms; the author then writes « ce n'est pas du tout évident ».
11. **Scan 411, axiomatic set-up — claim. CORRECT.** The « condition essentielle » is that the ψ_i : T̂̂_{g,ν} → Ŝ̂_{g,ν−1} (script capital G or S) induce M_{g,ν} ⥲ M_{g,ν−1}; the first pass read the ψ without index and left N/M open. This, with closed subgroups N_{g,ν} ⊂ T̂̂_{g,ν} normalising T̂_{g,ν}, is said to suffice to define arithmetisations and the bouchage/forage theory; no verification is given.
12. **Scan 411, inverse functor — own idea (first pass). KEEP.** Comparing « forer des trous » at invariant points with passage to a smaller Γ′ remains a sensible check; the author's own doubt follows immediately.
13. **Scan 414, discreteness — claim without proof. KEEP.** The inductive-limit category of sections of B_{π,Γ} ≃ B_u over the B_{Γ′} « est discrète et correspond à l'ens » Pt_ad(B_{π,Γ^♮}) ≃ lim Pt_ad(B_{π,Γ′}).
14. **Scan 414, groupoid description — claim without proof. CORRECT.** Corrected statement: if Pt(B_{π,Γ}) ≠ ∅, then, because π^{Γ′} = (1) for every open subgroup, « le gr. cat. π peut être décrit can.(?) par un groupoïde profini P̲t̲(B_{π,Γ^♮}) ayant Pt(B_{π,Γ}) comme ens d'objet, lié(s) par le groupe cat. π, sur lequel Γ opère en sens strict, avec le stabilisateur Γ_P de ∀ pt étant ouvert, et Γ_P → Aut(P) (≃ π mod autom. int.) étant continue ». A proof must build the arrows from π, the strict action, and continuity.
15. **Scan 414, NB margin — implication not pursued. KEEP.** The point groupoid « à opérateurs stricts » « dépend fonctoriellement de (π,Γ), pour des morphismes ext. … »; the rest is illegible (CSG: « [??] »), so the class of morphisms is not fixed.
16. **Scan 415, bijection — claim without proof. CORRECT.** The sentence reads « On a ici si à ∀ P ∈ Pt(B_{π,Γ}) on associe la classe d'isom. de sections de B_{π,Γ} sur B_Γ, on trouve une bijection — ce qui caractérise le Γ-groupoïde en question à isom unique près »; it is an assertion, not a definition (the first pass read « par déf. »).
17. **Scan 415, ④ — axiom. KEEP, wording corrected.** An admissible operation of Γ on (π,a) has, on some open Γ′, its « op. cat. » lifted to an effective admissible operation, i.e. Pt_ad(B_{Γ,π}) ≠ ∅.
18. **Scans 415–416, canonical homomorphism of extensions — claim. CORRECT (consequential).** The text says the homomorphism of extensions coming from the exterior action and from p_i « n'est pas la composée » Ŝ̂(π)_i → T̂̂(π)_i →ψ_i Ŝ̂(π′_i); the first pass read the opposite (« qui vient par la composée »). The insertion on 416 also requires the p_i : π → π′_i to commute with the exterior actions of T̂̂(π).
19. **Scan 416, general construction — claim. CORRECT.** It is said to exist whenever a group Γ (here T̂̂(π)) acts exteriorly on two exterior groups π, π′ with a Γ-compatible homomorphism π → π′ such that « le centre de π et le centralisateur de son image(?) dans π′ soient triviaux »; the cancelled « de centre trivial » after « qui » was replaced by this sharper condition. Existence and uniqueness are not separated in the text.
20. **Scan 416, forgotten axiom (g) — claim. CORRECT.** « On a oublié de préciser : (g) L'hom canonique (Ŝ̂_{g,ν})_i → Ŝ̂_{g,ν−1} associé à i ∈ [0, ν−1], envoie (M_{g,ν})_i dans M_{g,ν−1} donc il s'insère dans un hom.(?) de suites exactes » (26). The label is (g) or 9, not 7/2; CSG and IUT misprint the target as M_{g,ν}.
21. **Scan 415, ④ — own idea (first pass). KEEP.** Testing the lifting axiom on finite quotients is reasonable; nothing on the page makes the finite-level choices compatible.
22. **Scan 416, centraliser hypothesis — own idea (first pass). KEEP.** The difference of two candidate extension maps should land in the centraliser of the image of π in π′, so dropping triviality of that centraliser is the natural toy test.
23. **Scan 417, admissibility transported by φ_i — claim. KEEP.** « On conclut aisément de ② que si le premier est admissible, le deuxième l'est »: the argument is not written out.
24. **Scan 417, (27)–(29) — claim. KEEP.** Passing to the limit gives a map of Γ-sets (28) and a homomorphism of Γ-groupoids (29); the transition maps and the action on arrows are not specified.
25. **Scan 417, canonical point P — implication not pursued. KEEP.** P ∈ Pt_ad(B_{π′_i,Γ}) = (Pt_ad(B_{π′_i,Γ^♮}))^Γ is « le pt canonique », presumably the class of the canonical hom Γ → M_{a′}(π′_i) of 418 a).
26. **Scan 418, ⑤ — requirement. KEEP.** « On demande » that (27) induce a bijection onto Pt_ad(B_{π′_i,Γ}) ∖ {P}, and in the limit a bijection of Γ-sets.
27. **Scan 418, a) — claim. KEEP.** The canonical hom Γ → M_{a′}(π′_i) is not π′_i-conjugate to any φ_i∘λ with λ admissible; no obstruction is given.
28. **Scan 418, b) — claim. KEEP.** The target of φ_i∘λ, φ_i∘μ is written M_a(π) without primes (also in CSG); one expects M_{a′}(π′_i).
29. **Scan 418, c) — own idea (first pass). KEEP.** c) states no exception for P; read with a), the canonical class is simply not admissible-in-image, so c) concerns admissible lifts of Γ → N_{a′}(π′_i), which presumably excludes P by definition. Whether the canonical lift counts as « admissible » is the point to settle.
30. **Scans 417–418 — own idea (first pass). KEEP.** Splitting ⑤ into a) exclusion of P, b) injectivity, c) surjectivity matches the author's « Ceci signifie trois choses ».
31. **Scan 418, Γ-sets — own idea (first pass). KEEP.** A bijection of Γ-sets in the limit needs compatibility over all open Γ′, not only Γ-fixed points.
32. **Scan 419, points — claim. CORRECT.** The equivalence « se précise de façon parfaite au niveau des points : les Points Γ-rationnels de B_π(,Γ^♮?) s'identifient à l'un(?) des pts Γ-rationnels de B_{π′}, distincts de P ». With « l'un » each point corresponds to one point ≠ P; the set-level statement is ⑤.
33. **Scan 419, (30) — claim without proof. KEEP.** Extension to many points (« ce qui n'était pas faisable dans le contexte discret ! »): systems with Γ fixing each point of I′ ⊂ I(π) ↔ systems (π′, α′, I′, Γ, θ′) with I′ ⊂ Pt_ad(B_{π′,Γ})^Γ.
34. **Scan 419, margin — restriction. KEEP.** « avec 2g + (ν − card I′) ≥ 3 », ν′ = ν − card I′, keeps (g,ν′) anabelian.
35. **Scan 419, quasi-inverse — claim. KEEP.** « On a donc un foncteur quasi-inverse : forage de trous en I′ ! » (the doubt on « forage » is removed).
36. **Scan 419, many holes vs successive holes — own idea (first pass). KEEP.**
37. **Scan 420, restriction — claim. CORRECT.** The restriction is to I′ ⊂ I(π) « non seulement stable par Γ, mais ⊂ I^Γ », equivalently I′ ⊂ Pt(B_{π′,Γ^♮}) « non seulement stable par Γ, mais m̄ [même] ⊂ Pt(B_{π′,Γ^♮})^Γ »; removing it is reduced to ⑥, without proof.
38. **Scan 420, ⑥ — claim. CORRECT.** For (π,a) « groupe à lacets cat. profini arithmétisé » (not a groupoid), Γ′ open in Γ acting admissibly (written Γ → N_a(π), no prime), I′ stable: a lift of the action of Γ′ to an admissible action of Γ on N_{a′} invariant on I′ should extend uniquely to an admissible action of Γ (or Γ′, doubtful) on (π,a) inducing the given one on π′. Existence and uniqueness are both open here; the next page (CSG l. 8371) starts on uniqueness.
39. **Scan 420, ⑥ — own idea (first pass). KEEP.** Passing to an open normal subgroup fixing I′ pointwise is exactly the author's next move (« On peut supposer Γ′ invariant dans Γ », next package).

## Notes added in the second pass

40. **(second pass, own) Scan 416, why the extension map is not the composite — own idea, high confidence.** The composite Ŝ̂(π)_i → T̂̂(π)_i → Ŝ̂(π′_i) kills π (π is the kernel of Ŝ̂(π)_i → T̂̂(π)_i), while the left square of the diagram forces φ_i|π = p_i. So φ_i equals the composite only if p_i is trivial: the corrected reading « n'est pas la composée » is the mathematically necessary one.
41. **(second pass, own) Scan 417, diagram (26) — implication not pursued.** The annotations « non comm.? » (left triangle, with φ_i) and « comm. » (right triangle) say that the dashed lift N_a(π)_i → M_{a′}(π′_i) makes the lower-right triangle commute but not, apparently, the upper-left one. Whether the left triangle commutes up to π′_i-conjugation is the question behind a) and b) on 418.
42. **(second pass, own) Scan 413, which axiom is invoked — open point.** The inserted sentence cites « La condition (1) » (ink), but the inference « si Γ opère effectivement, de façon admissible, alors l'action extérieure déduite est admissible » follows from ② applied to (π°,a°) and the new hole, not from ① (open subgroups). The witnesses print (2). Either the author slipped or the ink is (2); the mathematics needs ②.
43. **(second pass, own) Scan 412, admissibility of the arithmetic groups — implication not pursued.** The admissible acting groups may be open subgroups of 𝕀Γ_g, « valeur commune des 𝕀Γ_{g,ν} », or of 𝕀Γ_a for an arithmetisation a. That 𝕀Γ_{g,ν} does not depend on ν is asserted in passing; it is what makes forage/bouchage compatible with the acting group.
44. **(second pass, own) Scan 416, transport of structure — claim.** The extension homomorphism is identified (« C'est aussi ici ») with the transport-of-structure map sending every automorphism à lacets u of π to the corresponding automorphism of π′_i. This identification is asserted, not checked; it presupposes that u preserves the hole i.
45. **(second pass, own) Scan 420, (6) as a splitting problem — own idea, medium confidence.** With E the extension of Γ by L = Ker((N_a)_{I′} → N_{a′}), ⑥ asks that the partial splitting over Γ′ extend uniquely to Γ; uniqueness follows if L^{Γ′} = 1, a generalisation of ③ (this is the author's own continuation, CSG ll. 8371–8383). Existence amounts to Norm_E(Γ′) → Γ being onto.

# LM_P043 — cote 140-2, scans 421–430  [source: second_pass\LM_P043_notes_checked.md]

# LM_P043 (scans 421–430): research notes, checked against the corrected text

Each first-pass note (numbered as in `LM_P043_notes.md`, section 5) is kept, corrected or dropped, with the reason. Notes added in this pass are labelled "second pass (own)". Source: Grothendieck, *La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois* (1981), Montpellier cote 140-2, scans 421–430.

## First-pass notes

1. **Scan 421: question. Keep.** "L'unicité est-elle de ttes façons claire ?" asks whether the partial splitting over Γ′ extends uniquely to Γ. The corrected text puts the splitting over *the* subgroup Γ′ ("du sous-groupe Γ′"), not over subgroups in general.

2. **Scan 421: conjecture. Keep, with the doubt removed.** "je présume qu'on doit avoir L^{Γ′}=1" is now a secure reading. The condition is said to generalise condition ③ of an earlier page.

3. **Scan 421: unproved claim. Keep, corrected.** The kernel is L = Ker((N_a)_{I′} → N_a), and the extension of Γ is pulled back from the extension (N_a)_{I′} of N_{a′} by L along Γ → N_{a′}. The first pass had N_0, N_{0′}. Identity (31), Norm_𝓔(Γ′) ∩ L = L^{Γ′}, is called "évident". The claim that L^{Γ′}=1 gives uniqueness (Γ̃ = Norm_𝓔(Γ′)), and that existence means Norm_𝓔(Γ′) → Γ is onto, is stated without proof.

4. **Scan 421: own idea (first pass). Correct.** The worry about continuity of an inverse does not arise in the profinite setting of these pages. A continuous bijective homomorphism between compact Hausdorff groups is a homeomorphism, so "épi (donc iso…)" holds once the map is continuous. The remaining point is the injectivity, which comes from L^{Γ′}=1 via (31).

5. **Scans 421–422: proposed investigation. Correct.** The text reads "dans certains contextes (au moins celui des actions arithmétiquement fidèles, i.e. Γ → 𝚪_a injectif — qui correspond normalement au cas de courbes alg. définies sur des ext. algébriques de ℚ)". The first pass had "(on visera alors des …", "arithmétiques" and "Π_a". So the arithmetically faithful case is the minimal context in which "admissible" is to be made precise. Returning to curves and finite coverings, which also gives a way to vary g, remains a plan.

6. **Scan 422: expectation. Correct.** He wants to take up "le formalisme précédent" (not "le problème") under another, perhaps more general, aspect. It is expected to apply also to *discrete* groups with loops (the formalism of the U!). Keep the separation of the discrete and profinite cases.

7. **Scan 423: unpursued implication. Keep.** Strict transitivity is demanded: a covariant functor from the category of cofinite parts U (with inclusions) to groupoids, over the evident functor on objects. Strictness versus coherence up to isomorphism is not discussed here.

8. **Scan 423: unpursued implication. Keep, wording corrected.** The local maps Π_{D_i^*} → Π_{U_I} are to be compatible with the "morphismes de transition" Π_{U_I} → Π_{U_J} (I ⊃ J). For fixed I they make Π_{U_I} a groupoid with loops through Π_{D_I^*} = ∐_{i∈I} Π_{D_i^*} → Π_{U_I}.

9. **Scan 423, margin: own idea (first pass). Correct.** The margin is now mostly read. If 𝒳 is finite and I = 𝒳, Π_∅ is not to be the empty groupoid but a groupoid "qui s'envoie dans les précédents…". Strict transitivity cannot then be required, and "il faudra(it) peut-être … hyp. anabéliennes sur Π_{U_I} dans ce cas". The finite case is thus explicitly set aside from strictness, and anabelian hypotheses are suggested for it.

10. **Scan 424: unproved claim. Keep.** The composite Π_{D_i^*} → Π_{U_J} → Π_{U_I} (i ∈ J∖I, J ⊃ I) is "constant", so that Π_{U_I} is deduced from Π_{U_J} by "bouchage des trous". Constancy alone does not say that Π_{U_I} is the universal such quotient; that would have to be imposed or proved.

11. **Scan 424: unproved claim. Correct.** The model "pouvait se visualiser" with a topological orientable surface X and a part 𝒳 meeting every connected component. For 𝒳 = I (𝒳 finite), the exceptional groupoid is the fundamental groupoid of X∖I = X∖{𝒳}, that is X minus the whole finite set 𝒳; the first pass had "X∖{x}". The text says one will have trouble mapping it into the others with strict transitivity, "qu'à cela ne tienne !". This agrees with the margin of scan 423 (note 9).

12. **Scan 424: own idea (first pass). Keep.** Comparing strict transition maps with maps defined up to natural isomorphism is a sensible test. The text itself only notes the difficulty in the exceptional case.

13. **Scan 425: unpursued implication. Keep.** Γ acts strictly on 𝒳, on the Π_{U_I} and on the Π_{D_i^*}, which it permutes ("N.B. qu'il permute entre eux"), commuting with all transition and local maps. The struck margin copy of "(qu'il permute entre eux)" shows that the phrase was added afterwards.

14. **Scan 425: unproved claim. Keep.** "On aura des difficultés, si 𝒳 est fini … pour la commutation stricte … mais passons" defers the finite case again.

15. **Scan 425: own idea (first pass). Keep.** The axiom read now is "si Γ′ est admissible alors tt ss-groupe Γ″ ⊃ Γ′ aussi" (upward closure), with admissible subgroups ≠ 1. Nothing is said about intersections, so testing closure under finite intersections remains a fair question.

16. **Scan 425: canceled draft. Keep.** The canceled conditions defined admissibility of Γ′ by 𝒳^{Γ′} meeting every connected component of 𝒳 = U_∅. They also considered the operation of Γ_P on π₁(U_I, P). This is abandoned material and not an assumption.

17. **Scan 426: conjecture / aim. Keep.** "Nous voulons des conditions qui assurent que 𝒳 et les Π_{U_I} etc. [peuvent|puissent] se reconstruire à isom. can. près" from the bare ("nues") groupoid or topos data with Γ-operators. This states an aim, not a theorem.

18. **Scan 426: conjecture / aim. Keep, notation corrected.** The single datum is the operation of Γ on the outer group with loops π₁(Π_{U_I}) attached to I (lower-case π₁; the first pass had Π₁). The data to be recovered are the Π_V for V ⊃ U_I, the Π_{D_i^*} (i ∈ I) and the action of Γ.

19. **Scan 426: own idea (first pass). Keep.** Test cases with different stabiliser patterns under condition 1° (Γ_P ≠ {1} of finite index) are a reasonable probe.

20. **Scan 427: unproved claim. Keep.** The direct direction is "immédiat, par l'opération de forage des trous". The task is the converse ("en sens inverse"): rebuilding Π_{U_I} and the action from Π_𝒳 (or rather the topos B_{Π_𝒳}).

21. **Scan 427: conjecture. Keep.** "sous réserve d'anabélianité, disons de Π_𝒳, on peut ± réconstituer Π_{U_I} et l'action de Γ dessus …". The sign after "anabélianité" is still unread.

22. **Scan 427: unproved claim. Correct.** The text reads "On veut au moins une description intrinsèque des éléments de 𝒳, et de l'action de Γ dessus, via cette action « molle »". The first pass had "On veut en avoir une" and "visible". So the minimal aim is to recover the points of 𝒳 with their Γ-action from the *soft* (outer) action alone. For 𝒳 connected this is an outer action of Γ on a group "à lacets (sans lacets !)".

23. **Scans 427–428: unproved claim. Correct.** The continuation reads "du moins si 𝒳 est infini donc qu'on puisse prendre I de cardinal arbitrairement grand". The infinitude of 𝒳 is given as what allows I to be taken arbitrarily large, hence π(I) anabelian for I "assez grand". The size threshold and the precise anabelian property are not stated.

24. **Scan 428: unpursued implication. Keep.** Condition 2°: the evident map U_I → Pt(B_{π(I),Γ♮}) ≅ {classes of π(I)-conjugacy of germs of splittings of the extension 𝓔(I) of Γ by π(I)} should be injective and Γ-compatible. Injectivity separates points but does not identify the image.

25. **Scan 428: open question. Keep.** "il faudrait pouvoir donner une caractérisation de l'image".

26. **Scan 428: unproved claim. Correct.** Compatible arithmetisations on the π(I), compatible with the hole-filling homomorphisms and the Γ-action, give "un hom canonique de Γ dans le groupe commun 𝚪 des autom. arithmétiquement (ext. de ces arithmétisations". The group is the bold 𝚪 (first pass: Π). Making this precise needs the definition of that common group and independence of the choices of representatives.

27. **Scan 428: unproved claim. Correct.** The parenthesis is "(et même Γ → M_{π(∅)=π}, — qui est déjà une donnée nettement plus forte)"; the first pass had "(cad = …" and "chose". The stronger datum is a homomorphism of Γ to M of π = π(∅) itself, compared with the homomorphism to the common group 𝚪. Grothendieck calls it markedly stronger without argument.

28. **Scan 428: own idea (first pass). Keep.** Restriction to open subgroups (germs) and π(I)-conjugation should be kept as separate equivalences when testing injectivity. The written words "germes de scindages" are secure.

29. **Scans 427–428: own idea (first pass). Keep.** A two-step diagram I ⊂ J tests how the point maps and the filling homomorphisms commute.

30. **Scan 428: own idea (first pass). Keep, with 𝚪 for Π.** Model the common group 𝚪 first on a short diagram of puncture sets and compare it with the group at I = ∅.

31. **Scan 429: proposed criterion. Correct.** One may suppose given a notion of admissible lifting making the map a bijection U_I = 𝒳∖I ≅ Pt_ad(B_{π(I)},Γ♮). "Ceci signifie … que *la notion d'admissibilité* satisfait aux conditions 1°) : 6°) vues ci-dessus" (first pass: "ce critère"). The conditions 1°–6° belong to earlier pages.

32. **Scan 429: conjecture. Keep.** What is to be called an admissible operation of Γ on an outer profinite group with loops "reste pour le moment conjectural".

33. **Scans 429–430: conjecture. Correct.** The experimental definition reads: an action Γ → 𝒯̂̂(π) (first pass: 𝓔̂̂) respecting an arithmetisation a, i.e. factoring through N_a, such that the image of Γ → N_a/𝒯̂_a = 𝚪_a is open (first pass: "= Π_a"), together with the non-normalisation conditions on scan 430. CSG elsewhere writes 𝒯̂̂(π) for Autextlac(π) (its line 6359). Whether this definition has the bijection property of note 31 is left open.

34. **Scan 430: unpursued implication. Keep.** For each hole-filling homomorphism π → π′_i, N(π)_i → M(π′_i), neither the corresponding image of Γ_i nor that of any open subgroup Γ′ of Γ_i may normalise an L′_j (j ∈ I(π′_i) = I∖{i}). Requiring this for all open subgroups makes it a condition on germs.

35. **Scan 430: conjecture. Keep, reading secured.** "peut-être même faudrait-il imposer π^{(Γ′+)} = (1), où Γ′+ est le noyau de Γ′ → Ẑ* (χ)". Then "on s'attend que l'on ait alors π^{Γ′} = (1), et si ce n'était le cas, il faudrait l'introduire dans la définition". This is to hold for each relative filling (I′ ⊂ I(π), i ∈ I′) defining Γ_{(I′,i)} → M(π(I′)).

36. **Scan 430, upper margin: conjecture. Correct.** The note is cancelled: long strokes cross it, and no witness carries it while all carry the lower note. It is an abandoned alternative. The condition just stated is perhaps superfluous and premature, and it might be that the subgroup K of M(π) normalising L_i and, modulo Ker(π → π′_i), L_j is "trop petit": its image in 𝚪 (or Π) = M(π)/𝒯̂(π) (letters doubtful) would not be of finite index. Treat it as a cancelled idea.

37. **Scan 430, lower margin: unproved claim. Correct.** CSG prints this note as footnote 118. It reads: "Plus généralement, pour i ∈ I′ ⊂ I = I(π), on impose que la vraie action de Γ_{I′,i} sur π(I′) correspondante [à i] ne normalise aucun sous-groupe L_j (j ∈ I∖I′) — on est ramené pour ceci au cas où I′ = I∖{j}, donc où π(I′) n'a (qu'une) seule classe [de] lacets… (si g ≥ 1)". The reduction to one remaining hole is asserted without proof. The genus condition is now read as g ≥ 1 (si|et still open).

38. **Scan 430: unproved claim. Correct.** The sentence ends "et qu'" and continues on scan 431: "il en est de même pour l'action induite sur chaque π(I′) …" (P044). A true action lifting a given admissible action is itself admissible (defines an admissible action on a π′ of type (g, ν+1)) iff the action, or rather its germ, normalises no L_i, and the same holds for the induced actions.

39. **Scan 430: own idea (first pass). Keep.** Γ′+ ⊂ Γ′ gives π^{Γ′} ⊂ π^{Γ′+}, so the imposed condition π^{(Γ′+)} = (1) implies π^{Γ′} = (1). Grothendieck's "on s'attend que l'on ait alors π^{Γ′} = (1)" must therefore mean "from admissibility" rather than "from the stronger condition", for which it would be trivial.

40. **Scan 430: own idea (first pass). Keep.** Compare one filling with two successive fillings, tracking normalisers of a remaining L_j and images of open subgroups. This tests the reduction claimed in the lower margin (note 37).

## Notes added in the second pass (own)

41. **Scan 421: own idea.** In the ink the kernel's target is N_a without a prime, while the extension is "de N_{a′} par L" and the map is Γ → N_{a′}. For L to be the kernel of the extension (N_a)_{I′} → N_{a′}, the target must be N_{a′}. The unprimed N_a in Ker(…) looks like a slip of the pen; the transcription keeps the ink.

42. **Scans 422 and 429: own idea.** With Γ profinite, "arithmétiquement fidèle" (Γ → 𝚪_a injective) makes Γ isomorphic to a closed subgroup of 𝚪_a. Adding the open-image condition of the experimental definition, the arithmetically faithful admissible actions are exactly those where Γ maps isomorphically onto an open subgroup of 𝚪_a. In that case condition 2° compares points of 𝒳 with sections over open subgroups of the arithmetic group, which is the setting of the section conjecture.

43. **Scan 424: own idea.** For I = 𝒳 the object set U_I = 𝒳∖I is empty, so restricting the fundamental groupoid of X∖I to U_I, as in the general case, would give the empty groupoid. That is what the margin of 423 excludes ("pas le groupoïde vide"). Grothendieck therefore takes the whole fundamental groupoid of X∖I = X∖𝒳, written "X∖{𝒳}" (the braces are a notational slip), whose objects are points outside 𝒳. Its object set is not U_∅ = ∅, so the maps from it cannot be inclusions on objects. This is exactly why strict transitivity fails in this case.

44. **Scan 428: own idea.** The step from "Γ → 𝚪" (exterior, arithmetic) to "Γ → M_{π}" (the stronger datum) is a lifting problem along M_π → 𝚪, whose kernel is of the type 𝒯̂(π). A lift exists iff the extension of Γ pulled back from M_π → 𝚪 splits. This is the same kind of splitting question as on scan 421. The comparison "nettement plus forte" is therefore measured by such a nonabelian obstruction, which the text does not discuss.

45. **Scan 427: own idea.** The word "molle" is the key term. The reconstruction is to use only the soft (outer) action of Γ on π, not a true action. This matches the later criterion on scan 430, where a true action lifting an admissible outer one is examined separately ("Notons qu'une vraie action …").

The second-pass notes that follow are labelled *Claude, second pass*. Scan numbers are file scans (manuscript pages 218–222). Quotations follow the corrected transcription.

The acting group is now read Γ♮; this is no longer ♮ or ♯. A proof would have to follow the normalisers of the loop subgroups through the hole-filling passages π′ → π′(I) and π(I) → π′(I).

Its relation to the infinitude of germs of splittings in 432 c) is still to be compared.

The first pass read the margin beside the heading as "Corrigé". It reads "Canulé cf plus bas…": the author himself withdraws this provisional conjecture, and the reason follows on 433–434.

The author links this, with "⟺?", to the absence of étale multisections of U_{g,ν} over M_{g,ν}. The letter forms and the word after "germes de" are still unsettled. The CSG's "(g,ν) = (0,3)" contradicts the ink's ≠.

In c) the quotient action is on π′♮; the superscript is the same sign as in Γ♮. "= R(i)" or "= π(i)" is unresolved, and the right-hand letter differs from the π of b), so the target of c) should not be identified with π(i) from the witnesses alone.

The next page gives the reason: for Γ = π₁(S) of a parameter scheme S, "il est manifeste que la surjectivité déconne", because two distinct sections need not be disjoint.

- **433 d) — own idea (first pass) — keep, with a note.** Keeping injectivity and the description of the image as separate problems is sound. The failure of the image description, however, is not left open on these pages: the author names its mechanism on 434, non-disjoint sections over a positive-dimensional base. The first pass's "missing admissible lifts" is a different mechanism, which the text does not support.

An admissible exterior action of π₁(S) on π corresponds "morally" to a family of curves of type (g,ν) parametrised by S. This is a heuristic dictionary, not an asserted equivalence. The first pass left the adverb as "maintenant|manifestement".

The ink says "la surjectivité déconne": surjectivity onto the complement of {P} fails. The author asserts, without proof, that condition c) holds for instance when U comes from a curve over the base field, and that surjectivity then visibly fails.

- **434 — implication not pursued — keep.** "deux sections distinctes de U sur S peuvent ne pas être disjointes !" Equality of sections and meeting in some fibre are different notions over a base of positive dimension.

- **434 — own idea (first pass): coincidence locus of two sections — keep.** It fits the corrected text exactly. The locus where two sections meet is what "pas disjointes" refers to.

- **435 — implication not pursued — keep (updated).** "Strictly distinct" sections are to be detected by comparing splittings with the admissible germs of splittings "sur ℾ′ ⊂ ℾ de Γ (en tant qu'extension de ℾ_Q par une partie géométrique)". Both letters are now read as double-struck Γ, not Π. Only a low dot after the prime is uncertain.

Injectivity of Γ → ℾ_a is offered as an example of arithmetical faithfulness ("p.e."), not as its definition (the first pass read "i.e."). The condition is wanted only up to passing to an open subgroup.

- **436 — assessment — correct (quotation).** He writes "semble raisonnable, ou du moins pas nécessairement déconnante", not "vraisemblable". This is a provisional assessment, not evidence.

This is an explicit programme for the non-compact case, which the author sets aside ("Finalement je ne regarde que les surfaces compactes"). The first pass treated it as a fragment that could not be recovered.

- **437 — unproved claims (compactification, extension of homeomorphisms, orientations, antiinvolutions) — keep (updated).** The parenthesis reads "(supposée orientée)": U is assumed oriented, which is what the notion of antiinvolution needs. The first-pass reading "supp. non orienté" is dropped. Homeomorphisms "U sur lui-m̄" extend to X and preserve S; no proof is given.

- **437 — unproved equivalence (U,σ) ↔ (Y,T) — keep.** "On trouve alors une équivalence" between the two categories, together with the inserted claim that the "double orienté" is a compact oriented surface. The morphisms are not specified.

- **437 — own idea (first pass): fixed versus interchanged punctures — keep.** See also the second-pass note on 437 below.

- **438 — unproved claim — keep.** The general case "se ramènera" to ν = 0.

- **438 — claim and the author's own correction — keep.** The text says "il faut que Y soit connexe, et non orientable"; the margin says this holds only when X^σ = ∅. A complete classification must allow orientable quotients.

- **438 — construction of (1) — keep (sharpened).** The margin beside (1), "Y surface compacte connexe sans bord non orientable de genre γ", fixes the convention. A closed non-orientable Y "of genus γ" is ℝP² with γ discs replaced by Möbius bands, so χ = 1 − γ: γ is the cross-cap number minus one. Removing μ open discs gives χ(Y) = 1 − (γ + μ). In the first display the sign before μ is still marked uncertain in the ink, but (1) requires −.

- **438 — unproved claim: X^σ is a union of circles — keep.** It is used to remove the fixed locus without changing χ.

- **439 — Proposition and left margin — keep.** The Proposition claims an equivalence with compact non-orientable bordered surfaces of type (γ,μ) with γ + μ = g. The margin restricts this to "une sous-catégorie pleine" and adds the orientation doubles Y ∐_{∂Y} Y of orientable compact Y with non-empty boundary.

- **439 — left margin, g = 2γ + μ − 1 — keep (reading adjusted).** It reads "X est de genre g avec g = 2γ + μ − 1 (où γ ≥ 0, μ ≥ 1)". Here γ is the ordinary genus of the orientable Y, a different convention from 438.

- **439 — Corollaire and right margin — keep.** The count "exactement g+1 classes … 0 ≤ μ ≤ g" holds only for (X,σ) with X/σ non-orientable ("Ça ne marche qu'en se limitant …").

- **439 — inverted cancelled block — keep.** "Nous ~~admettrons~~ savons qu'elles sont classifiées, mod isomorphisme près, par les systèmes" breaks off and is cancelled. It must not be completed.

- **439 — own idea (first pass): small-genus inventory — keep.** It is carried out in the second-pass note on 439–440 below.

- **440 — unproved claim — keep.** There are "exactement g+1 classes de conjugaison" in A_g = Aut(X_g) satisfying (4), which give classes in A_g/A_g° = 𝒯_g. By the 439 margins this is the count for non-orientable quotients only.

- **440 — conjecture — keep.** "Nous montrerons (on l'espère!)" that these classes stay distinct in 𝒯_g, and that every σ ∈ 𝒯_g satisfying (4) lies in one of them. These are a separation problem and a realisation problem.

- **440 — assumed lemma — keep (updated).** Every antiinvolution of the unit disc, with an inserted "(cas de ℂ)" or "(ou de ℂ)" that is still uncertain, is conjugate to z ↦ z̄. Its fixed set is therefore homeomorphic to ℝ, hence connected. It is assumed ("On admettra"), not proved.

- **440 — theorem set-up — keep.** An oriented surface U not isomorphic to S², an antiinvolution σ, the universal covering Ũ, π = Aut(Ũ/U), and an extension E of ℤ/2 by π, "formée" (now read); the statement continues past the package.

- **440 — own idea (first pass): split into lifting and conjugacy problems — keep.**

- **440, display (4) — own idea (first pass): check the definition of sg — keep.** The ink, and every witness, has sg(σ) = +1. For an orientation-reversing involution the orientation character would be −1. Either "sg" is defined otherwise earlier in the manuscript, or this is a slip; check before using (4).

- **436 — literature: Belyi — keep.** Relevant as a benchmark. The correction to "p.e." does not affect it.

- **440 — literature: Kerckhoff, Nielsen realisation — keep.** It is a retrospective comparison only.

## Second-pass notes (Claude)

- **431–434 — the author's withdrawal and its reason — implication made explicit (Claude, second pass).** The "Conjecture provisoire profinie" is marked "Canulé" in the margin, and 433–434 give the reason. Take Γ = π₁(S) for a parameter scheme S of positive dimension. A section of the filled family U(i) → S that meets the section P given by the hole i over some, but not all, points of S is neither a section of U nor equal to P. So the complement of the image of Pt_ad(B_{π,Γ♮}) → Pt_ad(B_{π′,Γ♮}) is larger than {P}: this is "la surjectivité déconne", while injectivity is untouched.

- **431, margin — implication not pursued (Claude, second pass).** The reduction to subsets I′ = I ∖ {j} is qualified "du moins si g ≠ 0" (ink ≠; the CSG prints "= 0"). For genus 0, whether the induced conditions on all π(I′) follow from those on the I ∖ {j} is left open.

- **432 — a slip in a definition (Claude, second pass).** "Une action effective de Γ sur π est dite effective, si l'action ext. est effective, et si elle ne normalise aucun ss-groupe à lacets" is circular as written. The next clause, "Si Γ opère effectivement de façon admissible", shows that "admissible" is meant in both places. The ink says "effective" twice, and the transcription keeps it.

- **435 — conjecture: the section conjecture in germ (Claude, second pass).** Points of S, over finite extensions of the ground field, are said to correspond to germs of splittings of Γ = π₁(S) over open subgroups ℾ′ of ℾ, with Γ seen as an extension of ℾ_Q by its geometric part. This is stated without proof, and is the content Grothendieck later stated as the section conjecture (letter to Faltings, 1983). Here it is used to define "admissible" germs, and that is the circularity he points out.

- **436 — implication (Claude, second pass).** With "p.e." restored, "arithmétiquement fidèle" is wider than injectivity of Γ → ℾ_a, and is wanted only "modulo tt au moins passage à un ss-groupe ouvert". The dimension-0 step of the proposed induction therefore covers every Γ that is faithful on some open subgroup. A definition of faithfulness is still missing on these pages.

- **437 margin and 440 theorem — own idea, medium confidence (Claude, second pass).** The marginal aim, recovering how the points at infinity lie on the components of X^σ from the order-2 outer automorphism, fits the theorem begun on 440. There each component of U^σ should give a π-conjugacy class of order-2 elements of E outside π. A real puncture lying on a component Z_i should then appear as a cusp (loop) subgroup normalised by the corresponding involution σ_i. The distribution of the punctures could be read off from which loop subgroups each σ_i normalises; the pages do not state this, and it needs proof.

- **439–440 — checking the count (Claude, second pass).** The two marginal corrections together give the full count of conjugacy classes of antiinvolutions on a closed oriented surface of genus g.
  - Non-orientable quotient: (γ,μ) with γ, μ ≥ 0 and γ + μ = g, giving g + 1 classes.
  - Orientable quotient: γ ≥ 0, μ ≥ 1 and 2γ + μ − 1 = g, giving ⌊g/2⌋ + 1 classes.

  The total is ⌊3g/2⌋ + 2, the classical number of topological types of real structures in genus g (Weichold, 1883). Harnack's bound μ ≤ g + 1 is reached only in the orientable case with γ = 0. The "exactement g+1" of the Corollaire and of 440 is therefore the non-orientable count alone, as the right margin of 439 says. (Check: g = 1 gives 3 = 2 + 1: Klein bottle, Möbius band, annulus.)

- **433 c) — open question (Claude, second pass).** In c) the target is written π′♮ = R(i)|π(i), with a letter unlike the π of b) and a ♮ exponent that no witness keeps. How π′♮ relates to π′ = π(i) of b) ("par passage au quotient") is not explained on these pages. Settle it before using c) in d).

# LM_P045 — cote 140-2, scans 441–450  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P045\LM_P045_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — separate from the transcription

These notes concern only what is stated, invoked, or suggested in the supplied extract. “Unproved claim” includes a step invoked without a proof here; it does not mean that the full manuscript or the literature lacks a proof. Several arguments are completed later within these same ten images, and the notes identify that where relevant. A wholly canceled claim is discussed as a discarded formulation. Brief quotations are finding aids; uncertain details remain governed by the diplomatic transcription and the doubt table.

No securely readable explicit mathematical conjecture is identified in the surviving text of this extract. The author’s wish to construct a simultaneous geometric figure on scan 449 is recorded under the requested conjecture/expectation category, with its status as a construction aim stated explicitly. “Own idea” marks an editorial proposal for further investigation; none is asserted to be established or new. Manuscript locations below refer to Grothendieck (1981), using the filename-based scan numbers in Section 1.

### R01. Scan 441 — 5–6, a)

**Kind:** unproved claim.

**Manuscript cue:** « (Pour mémoire) ... sous-variété fermée ... de dim 1 ».

The fixed-locus assertion is recalled without a proof on this page. Checking it requires the hypotheses on U and its involution from the preceding pages, plus the appropriate local fixed-point model; these ten supplied images do not contain the beginning of the theorem.

### R02. Scan 441 — 8–18, b), equations (5)–(6)

**Kind:** own idea.

**Manuscript cue:** « Cette application se factorise en une bijection ».

Compare the component-to-splitting map with the cocycle description of splittings of a group extension by Z/2. This comparison would require a fixed choice of one splitting and careful tracking of the conjugation convention; it is an interpretive direction, not an additional formula attributed to the manuscript. The subsequent supplied pages contain the manuscript's geometric argument for the displayed bijection.

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** The page visibly identifies conjugacy classes of splittings with order-two elements outside the kernel, but does not introduce cocycles or choose a reference splitting here.

### R03. Scan 441 — 19–24, c)–d)

**Kind:** unpursued implication.

**Manuscript cue:** « π^{σ_i}={1} ... Z_i≃R ».

The asserted contrast between the line and circle cases suggests that fixed subgroups can detect the compactness of individual fixed components. Before using this as a reconstruction statement, one must verify the ambient hypotheses, the converse in (7), and the conjugacy choices in d), whose statement continues onto scan442.

### R04. Scan 442 — 6–8

**Kind:** unpursued implication.

**Manuscript cue:** « quitte à remplacer g_i par un conjugué ».

The conjugacy qualification suggests isolating a formulation independent of the selected representative and basepoint. The comparison between the geometric component and the fixed subgroup should keep track of which lift of the involution is being used.

### R05. Scan 442 — 21–22

**Kind:** unproved claim.

**Manuscript cue:** « Comme par le lemme … est non vide et connexe ».

This is a dependency on an invoked lemma, not a claim that the full manuscript lacks a proof. Before transferring the classification to another surface or involution, one should check exactly which hypotheses guarantee nonemptiness and connectedness of the fixed locus in the universal cover.

### R06. Scan 443 — 1–17

**Kind:** unpursued implication.

**Manuscript cue:** « l’application déduite (6) est bijective ».

The argument separates a connected-image statement from the stronger assertion that the image fills a fixed component. The latter uses the universal-cover construction on this page; any generalization should identify a replacement for that step rather than rely only on connectedness.

### R07. Scan 444 — top and diagonal marginal insertion, (10)

**Kind:** unproved claim.

**Manuscript cue:** « un rev. étale de son image ».

The marginal revision strengthens the canceled equality of images to an isomorphism from the universal cover of the component to the lifted fixed locus. The local covering assertion is compressed: a detailed verification should specify the local homeomorphism and explain the one-sheeted conclusion from simple connectedness of the target.

### R08. Scan 444 — (11)–(12)

**Kind:** own idea.

test the covering argument explicitly for a line component and for a circular component, retaining the chosen lifted involution throughout. This is a verification exercise that may clarify which step changes when the component ceases to be simply connected; it is not a claim of novelty.

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** The two cases are suggested by the manuscript’s contrast between the trivial fixed subgroup and the subsequent deck-transformation group T_i, but an explicit model has not been worked out here.

### R09. Scan 445 — 6–10

**Kind:** unproved claim.

**Manuscript cue:** « Il est clair ... commute à l'hom injectif ».

The equivariance needed to induce T_i→π_i^{σ_i} is asserted by appeal to transport of structure. A full check should specify the lifted involution on the chosen universal cover and verify that the map on deck groups is equivariant for exactly that choice; the subsequent surjectivity argument is present on this page.

### R10. Scan 445 — margin beside Corollaire 1

**Kind:** unpursued implication.

**Manuscript cue:** « et X_g/σ non orientable.... ».

This marginal qualification may restrict the scope of Corollaire 1, but no caret securely locates its insertion in the statement. Any later use of the corollary should check whether nonorientability of the quotient is an explicit standing hypothesis; the note has not been silently incorporated into the theorem text.

### R11. Scan 446 — 1–4, together with scan 445 margin

**Kind:** own idea.

Compare involutions with the same number of fixed components but different orientability of the quotient, asking whether the conjugacy classes of lifts or the embedded cyclic fixed subgroups distinguish them. This is a proposed comparison, not a claim that such examples occur under all the present hypotheses.

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** Part (a) singles out the component count, whereas the margin records an additional topological qualification that the count alone may not encode.

### R12. Scan 446 — 16

**Kind:** own idea.

**Manuscript cue:** « Soit Y_{g,i}=X_g^{σ_i} ».

Check the literal superscript notation against the surrounding definitions before using this as an identification of spaces. The same paragraph calls Y a connected nonorientable surface with boundary, while the earlier superscript notation refers to a fixed locus; the transcription preserves the visible formula without deciding whether this is a slip or a local notational convention.

**Confidence:** high. **Reason:** The sigma is visibly superscripted and no quotient slash is visible, but the intended mathematical interpretation is not settled by this local reading.

### R13. Scan 446 — 18–19; continuing scan 447, lines 1–3

**Kind:** unproved claim.

**Manuscript cue:** « il est bien connu, et immédiat ».

Transitivity on boundary components is invoked for the automorphism group of the connected nonorientable surface, and then lifted to the pair (X_g,σ_i). A proof should construct homeomorphisms exchanging the required boundary circles and verify the permitted category and compatibility of their lifts with the involution.

The passage from Π-conjugacy to equality in (15) is condensed into a modification of h. An explicit verification should write the inner conjugating element and check that multiplying the chosen lift by it preserves the required positive subgroup and the projected class commuting with σ_i.

The text literally describes an index of the automorphism centralizer in the outer centralizer, without the words 'image de'. Before formalizing Corollaire 2, distinguish that homomorphism from its image: the displayed kernel T suggests that the intended finite index concerns the image subgroup, but no such repair is inserted into the transcription.

**Confidence:** high. **Reason:** The diagram includes T as a kernel term, while the prose omits an explicit image operation; the note concerns interpretation rather than a correction to the ink.

The reduction from the full groups to the positive subgroups uses an index-two assertion for both centralizers. A proof should identify the relevant orientation characters and exhibit elements in the nonpositive cosets; the involutions themselves are natural candidates once their orientation behavior is fixed.

Audit the i=0 boundary case before treating the index formula as an unconditional statement. Corollaire 1(a) would provide no order-two lift in that case, so the parts that choose u_i, and hence the cyclic group T, should be read conditionally rather than as assigning a subgroup of index zero.

**Kind:** own idea.

For the image subgroup in the outer centralizer, determine its action on the cyclic kernel T and ask whether the resulting extension splits, beginning with i=1. This is a possible computation; the present pages do not exhibit a section or establish a splitting criterion.

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** Cyclicity of T and the proposed finite-index image give concrete extension data, but do not by themselves imply a splitting.

isolate the elementwise calculation ending in α⁻¹γ belonging to the centralizer as a general lifting criterion for an extension of groups. A separate proof could clarify exactly which quotient action is used and which stabilizer classes lift to actual commuting automorphisms. This is a proposed reformulation for study, not a claim of novelty or a correction of the manuscript.

**Confidence:** high. **Reason:** The visible proof explicitly passes from equality modulo inner conjugacy to membership in an actual centralizer.

**Kind:** unproved claim.

**Manuscript cue:** « Les éléments de torsion … sont d’ordre 2 ».

This assertion belongs to a wholly cancelled and locally revised passage, not to an accepted corollary on these pages. Its intended hypotheses and even part of the boundary condition remain illegible. Assessing or proving the discarded formulation would require recovering the relevant meaning of Π and the earlier conventions; ordinary surface fundamental groups must not simply be substituted for that missing context.

**Kind:** conjecture / authorial expectation (construction aim).

Construction aim or expectation, not a mathematical conjecture: Grothendieck wants one geometric figure to exhibit the topological anti-involutions giving the σ_i and the various associated u_i. He begins such a construction on this and the following page. The supplied pages do not by themselves complete the promised simultaneous description of all the associated automorphisms.

A proof would need the precise meaning of the doubling construction, the admissible range of g and i, and the classification or existence statement being invoked. The overwritten surface subscript is a transcription issue and has not been repaired to support that interpretation.

# LM_P047 — cote 140-2, scans 461–470  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P047\LM_P047_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

All manuscript quotations and attributions below refer to Grothendieck (1981), with the supplied scan identifiers and local equation or line anchors. “Conjecture” also covers the author's questions, expectations, and proposed programme; a question may be answered on the very next supplied page, which is stated where relevant. An “unproved claim” means that proof details are not given at the cited location, not that the assertion is false or unproved elsewhere. The proposed implications and own ideas are research leads scoped to these pages; they have not been checked for priority, later treatment in the manuscript, or resolution in the literature.

### 461-R1 — Unproved claim — semidirect-product normal form (approximately ll. 9–11)

“Ainsi G apparaît comme le produit semi-direct” uses both the inversion relation and the identification `H≃Z^I`. The displayed calculation establishes the conjugation action locally, but this excerpt does not itself prove independence of the generators of H or uniqueness of the asserted normal form. A complete proof would have to import those previously established facts or verify them for the supported cylinder transformations.

### 461-R2 — Unpursued implication — the negative coset consists of involutions (approximately ll. 12–14)

The assertion “est une anti-involution !” following `(τρ)^2=1` suggests studying the full family indexed by H before imposing geometric equivalence. The inversion action makes the distinction between enumerating involutions and classifying their conjugacy classes particularly important; the latter is taken up explicitly in scan 463. This observation is a consequence to check within the stated group structure, not a claim of novelty.

### 461-R3 — Unproved claim — additivity of the fixed-set index (approximately ll. 15–20)

“il suffit de prendre la somme des” reduces the global index to the cylinder contributions continued on scan 462. To make the reduction fully explicit, one should verify that the fixed set avoids V₀, that cylinder boundary identifications do not join distinct fixed components, and that all fixed components are accounted for by the local models. The present lines indicate the argument but leave these topological details implicit.

### 462-R1 — Unpursued implication — parity patterns versus the numerical index ((45)–(46))

The condition “n_j est impair” makes the numerical index depend on the cardinality of the odd-exponent set. Equal cardinalities need not record which cylinders carry the odd exponents; the numerical index therefore supplies less information than the entire parity pattern before further conjugacies are considered. A useful next comparison is between these patterns and the actions of the larger symmetry groups introduced later in the supplied sequence.

### 462-R2 — Unproved claim — geometric conjugacy of the involutions (after (46))

“Il est visible” is supplemented by “par des raisons générales” before a conjugacy assertion involving `u` and `τ_{I'}`. An explicit conjugator and a precise statement of its orientation behavior would clarify the assertion, particularly because the inserted parenthesis concerning `A_g^+` and the extensively canceled continuation are not fully legible. The canceled argument is not treated here as a valid theorem or as the author's final formulation.

### 463-R1 — Unpursued implication — a square-quotient parametrization (approximately ll. 1–8)

The criterion “ρ′ρ″^{-1}∈H²” identifies H-conjugacy of the displayed involutions with equality in the quotient H/H². Under the asserted finite-rank identification `H≃Z^I`, this gives a parity-vector indexing set with `2^{|I|}` elements. The passage does not at this point determine how many such classes become identified by additional surface symmetries.

### 463-R2 — Conjecture (expectation) — the richest simple symmetry arrangement (approximately ll. 9–13)

“La façon la plus riche en symétries simples … me semble la suivante” expresses a tentative geometric preference for the dihedral arrangement of the antipodal holes. It is not accompanied here by a defined extremal invariant or a maximality proof. Any attempt to formulate it as a theorem would first need to specify what counts as a simple symmetry and which competing configurations are admitted.

### 463-R3 — Unproved claim — passing from the spherical action to the punctured and attached surface (approximately ll. 9–25)

The instruction “on prend l'action type du groupe dihédral” gives formulas for the sphere action, while the choice of antipodal holes is described as part of the construction. To justify the later induced surface action, one needs equivariant choices of disks and compatibility of their attaching maps with the cylinder models. This is a construction problem suggested by the page, rather than an assertion that the supplied segment contains no later treatment of it.

### 463-R4 — Own idea — classify the parity vectors under the explicit finite symmetries (after (48))

Compute the action of the transformations `u_{ζ,α}` on the cylinder labels, then study its orbits on the quotient H/H² from the preceding criterion. **Confidence: high as a feasible research step**, because both the local transformation formulas and the square criterion are explicitly present; a full orbit computation and the comparison with geometric conjugacy still require work. This is a proposed calculation, not an established result or a claim of novelty.

### 463-R5 — Own idea — examine the smallest genera separately (following the dihedral construction)

Work out the configurations with one and two antipodal pairs, recording separately the action on the sphere, on the holes, and on the set of paired cylinders. **Confidence: medium**, because the explicit formulas make the examples accessible, but possible kernels or coincidences in these small cases have not been computed here. This check could expose qualifications needed in a general presentation without altering any manuscript reading.
