# LM_P051 — cote 140-2, scans 501–510  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P051\LM_P051_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

Every item refers to the supplied scan number. Brief quotations identify manuscript evidence; an uncertain quoted reading retains its qualification. Suggested proofs, calculations and consequences have not been fed back into the transcription. “Unproved claim” means that the claim is not proved in the cited passage, not that it is false, new, or unknown in the literature.

### Scans 501–503

1. **Scan 501, lines 15–20 — unproved claim.** “J'admets que ces groupes sont ≃ Ẑ” is followed by the inserted justification “c'est d'ailleurs trivial en passant à π_ab”. A detailed proof would need to identify the images of the displayed generators in the abelianization and check that their continuous procyclic parameterizations have trivial kernel; the manuscript supplies only this indication.
2. **Scan 501, lines 20–22, (4) — unproved claim.** “et qu'on a, en analogie avec (2)” introduces the centralizer identities for powers of the closed subgroups Λ_i and Λ′_i. The condition on the exponent is graphically uncertain, so any attempt at a proof must first settle that reading and then distinguish the injectivity of a procyclic parameterization from the stronger centralizer assertion.
3. **Scan 501, lines 13–15 — unproved claim.** The parenthesis “Ils sont d'ailleurs tous conjugués sous Aut(π)” is stated without an argument on this page. A proof would have to realize the needed permutations of the displayed closed cyclic subgroups by automorphisms respecting the relation (3).
4. **Scan 502, lines 2–13 — conjecture / expectation.** “Le résultat le plus fort de fidélité … serait le suivant” proposes faithful outer action for an anabelian curve over a finite extension of Q. The formulation is conditional and prospective; neither the passage's group-letter ambiguities nor the sentence's confidence should be silently converted into a proved theorem.
5. **Scan 502, lines 13–19 — conjecture / expectation.** “mais même l'homomorphisme composé … devrait être injectif” asks for faithfulness after passing to the displayed quotient by the hatted script subgroup. A proof would need to exclude nontrivial Galois elements whose action lies in that subgroup, a stronger issue than faithfulness before the quotient.
6. **Scan 502, lines 17–20 — unproved claim.** “puisqu'il est surjectif par construction même” asserts surjectivity of the quotient map and explains why its hoped-for injectivity would give an isomorphism. The relevant definitions are outside these pages, so this construction-dependent claim cannot be verified from the present extract alone.
7. **Scan 503, lines 1–7 — conjecture / expectation.** “semblent indiquer que ce serait le cas au moins lorsque V est un revêtement étale” limits the heuristic to covers of the displayed U. He explicitly calls the preceding heuristic “moins convainquants sans doute”, so the wording records qualified expectation rather than a completed proof.
8. **Scan 503, lines 9–16 — unproved claim / conditional reduction.** “Si on pouvait montrer que” introduces injectivity of the map from the group indexed by π₀ to the one indexed by π′. A proof would need the actual definitions of these quotient groups, the functoriality of passage to a characteristic open subgroup, and control of the quotient map's kernel; faithfulness of a related automorphism restriction alone would not automatically settle the quotient statement.
9. **Scan 503, lines 16–18 — unpursued implication.** “Donc modulo cette hypothèse … et utilisant [Белый]” makes the ensuing conclusion explicitly dependent on the profinite-group hypothesis. This is a useful place to track which later statements retain that dependency; the name's reading is itself marked doubtful in the transcription.
10. **Scans 502–503, quotient and diagram — own idea.** As a checking strategy, write the proposed kernel as the intersection of the arithmetic image with the subgroup being quotiented out, and then track this intersection under each diagram map. **Confidence: medium**, because this would isolate the additional faithfulness requirement visible in the passage, but the absent definitions may obstruct or change the proposed comparison; this is a suggested analysis, not an established result or a novelty claim.

### Scans 504–506

#### 504-R1 — Scan 504, lines 1–4 — unproved claim

The continuation states that for every algebraic curve there is a nonempty open `V'` for which the displayed `\Gamma \to \mathbb{\Gamma}_{\pi'}` is injective (“pour toute courbe algébrique … ∃ V' … soit injectif”). This is a conditional conclusion carried over from the preceding page, not an independent proof on this page. Its hypotheses and dependence on the proposed profinite-group argument must be retained when assessing it.

#### 504-R2 — Scan 504, lines 4–11 — conjecture / question

Grothendieck asks whether injectivity already holds before shrinking, and singles out `\Gamma \to \mathbb{\Gamma}_g` for `g ≥ 2` and `\Gamma \to \mathbb{\Gamma}_{1,1}`. His stated uncertainty is strong: “je n'ai pas de raison heuristique plausible … peut-être est-ce tout à fait faux ?” This should be recorded as an open question with an explicit doubt, rather than as an asserted faithfulness theorem.

#### 504-R3 — Scan 504, lines 12–19 — unproved claim

The earlier argument, “à supposer qu'on arrive à le justifier,” is said to propagate injectivity from one `π` to its open subgroups `π'`. A proof would need to specify the restriction map on the relevant outer-action quotients and show that its kernel cannot kill the image of the Galois group. The text itself qualifies this deduction rather than claiming that the needed argument has already been established.

#### 504-R4 — Scan 504, lines 16–18 — unpursued implication

The parenthesis “ce qui ne dépend que de son type `(g,ν)`” asserts independence from the chosen curve within the indicated type for the injectivity property under discussion. This raises a separate naturality issue: an identification of geometric fundamental groups alone need not, without further argument, identify arithmetic actions. A later check should distinguish which object or quotient is asserted here to depend only on the topological type.

#### 505-R1 — Scan 505, lines 1–5 — unproved claim / expectation

The preceding knowledge claim is qualified by “modulo peu de chose” and limited to types `(0,ν)`, `ν ≥ 3`. Grothendieck then suggests “on pourrait peut-être le déduire” for types obtained from these by finite covering. A proof would need the precise covering hypotheses and the injectivity-preservation argument discussed on scan 504.

#### 505-R2 — Scan 505, lines 6–9 — unproved claim

He says that the proposed method does not yield `(g,0)` with `g ≥ 2`, or any `(g,ν)` with `g ≥ 1` and `ν ∈ {0,1,2}` (“C'est dire qu'on est loin du compte”). The page gives the numerical exclusion but no calculation establishing it. A check should identify the permitted covering maps and count the preimages of the punctures, with their ramification constraints.

#### 505-R3 — Scan 505, lines 10–17 — conjecture / question

The “premier cas bien intéressant” is type `(1,1)`, annotated “tore à un trou !”. The question is whether the arithmetic action, described as an outer action modulo `\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^+_{1,1} \simeq Sl(2,ℤ)^∧`, is faithful: “est-elle fidèle ?” The qualifier “mod” is underlined and should remain central when comparing this question to an ordinary outer-action faithfulness statement.

#### 505-R4 — Scan 505, lines 11–13 — unproved claim

The page writes the displayed identification of the completed Teichmüller-type group with `Sl(2,ℤ)^∧` and calls the acted-on fundamental group a “groupe libre à deux générateurs”. The precise completion, topology on the acting group, and passage from a discrete action to this completed outer action are not proved on this page. A later verification should keep these issues separate from the faithfulness question itself.

#### 505-R5 — Scan 505, lines 6–8 — own idea

An explicit numerical test of the method's limitation could compare Euler characteristics and the number of punctures for finite covers of a genus-zero punctured curve. Confidence: medium, because the written exclusions suggest a covering-theoretic obstruction, but the exact meaning of “revêtement fini” and the admissible ramification have not yet been settled from these pages. This is a proposed check, not a claim that those numerical conditions already prove the asserted exclusions.

#### 506-R1 — Scan 506, heading — unproved claim / announced objective

The heading announces “L'isomorphisme” between the two displayed Galois-type groups and “l'injectivité” of a map to an outer-automorphism group of the completed type `(1,1)` group. The small subscripts on the two outer-automorphism expressions are illegible, so the precise category of automorphisms must not be supplied from expectation. These announced conclusions are not established within this page alone.

#### 506-R2 — Scan 506, upper-left marginal note — unproved claim / deferred treatment

The margin says the present section's reflections, described as “un peu cahin-caha”, “seront reprises” in the following section. The adjective after “moins” is uncertain, but the deferral itself is legible. Subsequent treatment should therefore be checked before treating this section's formulations as final.

#### 506-R3 — Scan 506, lines 3–11 — unproved claim

The quotient with relations `l_1² = l_∞³ = 1` is identified as a cartographic group, and its finite sets are said to correspond to oriented finite maps whose faces are triangles or mono-angles. A complete proof would construct the two assignments and check the treatment of what is tentatively read as “bords aplatis” (alternatively “boucles aplaties”). The interlinear qualifier about triangular structures is part of this assertion, although its final word remains uncertain in the transcription.

#### 506-R4 — Scan 506, lines 11–14 — unproved claim

The arithmetic outer action is said to descend through the quotient, “mais non celle de” the displayed symmetric-group symbol. A proof needs invariance, under the arithmetic action, of the closed normal subgroup generated by the two stated relations; the symmetric-group failure should be checked against the distinct chosen orders 2 and 3. No replacement of the manuscript's quotient or generators is justified by this observation.

#### 506-R5 — Scan 506, lines 16–17 — unproved claim

The underlined proposition asserts: “L'action extérieure … est fidèle” for the completed quotient group. The following paragraph starts a proof, but on this page only announces a compatible finite-index embedding and its completed version. Completing the argument requires both the compatibility and control of how inner automorphisms in the larger group act on the embedded subgroup.

#### 506-R6 — Scan 506, lines 18–22 — unproved claim

The proposed proof will “plonger” the original group into its quotient as a subgroup of finite index, and obtain an analogous injection after completion that is “compatible avec l'action ext.” The use of a quotient group as an ambient group is mathematically substantive; the quotient map itself is not the displayed injection. A proof must construct the separate embedding, justify injectivity on completions, and make its outer equivariance precise.

#### 506-R7 — Scan 506, equation (1) and lines 18–22 — own idea

One concrete check is to construct an explicit finite permutation quotient with generators of the indicated orders and compare the kernel with the proposed embedded group. Confidence: medium, because the relations suggest a manageable finite coset calculation, but the required arithmetic compatibility cannot be inferred from that calculation alone. This is a verification strategy, not an assertion that a particular permutation representation already supplies the manuscript's embedding.

### Scans 507–508

1. **Scan 507, lines 7–11 — unproved claim.** Grothendieck writes, “On sait que Y est une droite projective”, followed by the three marked rational points and the identification with `P^1_Q`. A self-contained justification would need to establish the structure and field of definition of the quotient, then explain why the specified marking determines the identification used for `f`; the page invokes this rather than proving it.

2. **Scan 507, lines 17–20 — unproved claim.** The quotient is called “galoisien”, and its ramification indices are listed as “2, 2, 3”. A proof at this point would require checking the three displayed orbits, their stabilizers, and the local degrees of the normalized quotient map, including how the three orbit labels match the ordered list of indices.

3. **Scan 507, deleted parenthesis after (3) — unproved claim, explicitly canceled.** The canceled text says that `f` “peut se définir comme morphisme” between two projective lines over `Z`. This must not be treated as a retained assertion: a separate investigation would need an integral model of the actual normalized map and a check for common zeros of its defining homogeneous forms in every residue characteristic.

4. **Scan 507, displayed trajectories and (3) — own idea.** As an explicit candidate to test, try `f(x)=27x^2(x-1)^2/[4(x^2-x+1)^3]` against the three labeled fibres, then check its invariance under the transformations generating the displayed permutation action and compute its local degrees. **Confidence: medium**, because the candidate is motivated by the visible orbit sets and normalization, while neither its formula nor the required checks appear on these pages. It is a suggested calculation, not a claimed result or novelty.

5. **Scan 507, canceled integral-extension sentence — own idea.** Once an explicit quotient formula has been verified, reduce its homogeneous numerator and denominator at 2 and 3 as a first test of the deleted assertion over `Z`. **Confidence: medium**, because these primes are suggested by the written ramification indices and occur in the preceding candidate formula; a genuine obstruction would still require proving that it cannot be removed by a permissible choice of integral presentation.

6. **Scan 508, lines 7–10 — unproved claim.** The sentence beginning “Tout revêtement” says that an étale topological cover on the `X` side gives a cover on the `Y` side with the stated ramification at 1 and infinity. A direct proof would need the local behavior of the quotient map and an explanation of how composition preserves the required unramified condition upstairs while producing the specified ramification downstairs.

7. **Scan 508, lines 11–13 — unpursued implication.** The insertion identifies the functor as “oubli” “(de la pondération)”. This invites an explicit description of which marking or weighting data are forgotten on objects, and of the corresponding change in automorphism groups; the identification is asserted in the prose but not developed here.

8. **Scan 508, large display (4) — unproved claim.** The correction replaces “hom. de groupes extérieurs” with “équiv. de catégories”, and the displayed target is a category over the object represented by `X \setminus {0,1,∞}`, or by `E` in the permutation-set version. A proof should specify the morphisms, the meaning of the ramification bound “sub. à”, and the functors in both directions; it should also account for the slice object rather than merely compare the unpointed groups.

9. **Scan 508, display (4), lower right — own idea.** Choose a point of the displayed set `E`, compute the monodromy of the quotient on its fibre, and compare its stabilizer with the group on the left of (4). **Confidence: medium**, because the two permutation categories and the object `E` are written explicitly, but the point, generators, and corresponding stabilizer calculation are not supplied on this page. This is a proposed route for making the equivalence concrete, not an assertion that it has been established here.

10. **Scan 508, ramification sentence versus display (4) — own idea.** Check carefully the distinction between the prose’s “3 exactt” (reading uncertain) and the diagram’s “ramification sub. à” the signature `2{1}+3{∞}`. **Confidence: medium**, because the two formulations are visible and may refer to different classes of objects; a worked example could determine whether the slice over `E` supplies the missing restriction. No inconsistency is asserted.

### Scans 509–510

1. **Scan 509, display (6) — unproved claim / unfinished calculation.** The three generator images are specified only as elements of orders 2, 2, and 3, with the explicit instruction “à calculer !”. A completion would require concrete images compatible with the chosen loops and their relations, together with a verification of the kernel used immediately above. The uncertainty in the target group's handwritten alphabet should be settled before attaching a more specific interpretation.

2. **Scan 509, middle paragraph beginning “On choisit” — unproved claim.** Grothendieck states that the slice category “s'identifie, par le foncteur” taking a fibre at `Q_0`, with the category of sets carrying the kernel-group action. A proof would need to construct the inverse operation and check that changing the chosen point of the homogeneous space gives the claimed equivalence, including the action conventions.

3. **Scan 509, final paragraph — unproved claim.** The resulting equivalence is said to be “décrite par un bitorseur” and, up to a nonunique isomorphism, by an isomorphism of the two groups. The needed verification is that the two commuting actions are free and transitive and that choosing an origin gives precisely the stated group isomorphism. The following scan discusses the ambiguity, but does not spell out these verifications.

4. **Scan 510, first paragraph — unproved claim.** The isomorphisms from varying origins are asserted to form “exactement une classe de conjugaison”; allowing `Q_0` to vary is then said to give an exterior homomorphism into the larger group. One should verify both the source of the inner conjugations and the compatibility of the composite with the different choices of `Q_0`.

5. **Scan 510, paragraph beginning “J'ai beaucoup…” — unproved claim / missing framework.** The phrase “à défaut d'avoir écrit” explicitly points to elementary functoriality for the quoted fundamental groups with ramification that has not been developed here. The subsequent path description of `I` would require precise objects, admissible paths, and composition laws, along with a proof that these recover the earlier categorical construction; the disputed word “bifoncteur”/“bitorseur” should remain unresolved at the transcription level.

6. **Scan 510, last paragraph and (7) — conjecture / methodological expectation.** “Il serait peut-être plus commode” introduces the proposal to construct the functor in the inverse direction, by inverse image followed by the underlined “normalisation”. A full treatment would need to define the allowed ramification in the source category, prove that the resulting normalized pullback is an étale covering of the indicated punctured `X`, and compare it with the preceding functor. This excerpt stops before those checks are supplied.

7. **Scan 509, (6) — own idea; confidence: medium.** If the curled target symbol is indeed the symmetric group on three letters, one could test two explicit transpositions and the inverse of their product as the proposed generator images, then compare the resulting kernel with the covering in the manuscript. The reason for considering this test is the visible order pattern 2, 2, 3; the confidence is conditional because the loop conventions and the target glyph still need checking. This is a suggested calculation, not a claim of novelty or a completed proof.

8. **Scan 510, (7) — own idea; confidence: medium.** Test the proposed normalization construction first on local cyclic covers over the two points appearing in the signature `2{1}+3{∞}`. This could reveal whether pullback removes exactly the ramification permitted in the source category and which hypotheses the functor needs. The reason for the suggestion is the explicit signature and the final underlining of “normalisation”; no global equivalence is asserted by this local test.

9. **Scan 510, first paragraph and discussion of paths — own idea; confidence: medium.** A formulation with fundamental groupoids and path torsors might make the change-of-origin and change-of-`Q_0` operations visible before choosing group identifications. The reason is that the page itself attributes the ambiguity to those two choices and then describes `I` using paths. This would be a way to organize a verification of the manuscript's claims, not an additional theorem extracted from the text.

# LM_P052 — cote 140-2, scans 511–520  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P052\LM_P052_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English

These items record the author's expressed expectations, assertions whose proofs are not supplied here, consequences worth checking, and explicitly labelled proposals by the transcriber. They are not a literature review or a claim that an issue remained unresolved later. Each heading is a locator for the primary-source citation, Grothendieck (1981); a brief quotation identifies the relevant wording. An **own idea** is a proposed investigation with its confidence and reason, not an asserted result or a claim of novelty.

### R01 — Scan 511, (7 bis) and following paragraph — unproved claim

« a les propriétés d'exactitude » and « est donc défini par un … ens. » assert the passage from a functor between categories of group actions to a right torsor with a second group action. A proof should specify the precise ramification-bounded covering categories, verify the exactness conditions, and establish the claimed torsor property; these details are not supplied on this page.

### R02 — Scan 511, middle paragraph — unpursued implication

« Le choix d'une origine pour ce torseur » points to a dependence on an auxiliary choice when the homomorphism is extracted. It is worth tracking explicitly how changing that origin changes the homomorphism and how this relates to the inner-conjugacy ambiguity stated on scan 512; this is a question about the manuscript's construction, not a correction to its text.

### R03 — Scan 512, (9) — unproved claim

« Les raisonnements précédents s'étendent à ce cadre » (beginning on scan 511) asserts an arithmetic version yielding a morphism of extensions. A proof would need to construct the functor over the base field and check both the maps on geometric kernels and the identity on the arithmetic quotient, including the stated ambiguity « modulo conjugaison ».

### R04 — Scan 512, definition of `K` through « lui-m̄ est fini » — unproved claim

« On voit alors que … se fait par un groupe fini » is the key reduction before invoking « le th. 1 du § précédent ». To assess the argument, one needs the preceding theorem's actual hypotheses and a proof that the restricted outer action factors through the displayed finite quotient; the present extract does not include that theorem.

### R05 — Scan 512, last paragraph — unproved claim

« Donc par Artin » and « comme χ(τ) = −1 » condense two external ingredients in the proof of triviality of the kernel. A reconstruction should identify the precise Artin result being invoked, explain its applicability to `K`, and verify the induced action on the indicated quotient or abelianization without relying on the uncertain final insertion.

### R06 — Scan 513, opening paragraph — conjecture / expectation

« J'ai envie maintenant d'interpréter » announces the intended identification with a central quotient and asks that it be « compatible à l'action extérieure de Γ ». The discrete identifications below it do not themselves supply this arithmetic compatibility; scans 515–520 should be read as attempts to construct the comparison geometrically.

### R07 — Scan 513, (10)–(13) — unproved claim

« pour mémoire » introduces isomorphisms obtained by « bouchage du trou » and the action on the fundamental group, followed by the description of the centre. A proof must fix the exact marking and orientation conventions of the Teichmüller groups, since those conventions determine the filling map and the distinction between the two linear groups.

### R08 — Scan 513, (14)–(15) — unproved claim

« Il est connu » states a presentation by elements of orders three and two, while « Sauf erreur » expressly qualifies their lifting to elements of orders six and four. One should verify the lifts, their exact orders, and the common central element; the next page discusses the additional relation rather than giving explicit matrices here.

### R09 — Scan 514, ll. 3–7 — unproved claim

An “élément d'ordre fini” is said to be conjugate to a power of one of the two displayed generators. A proof would have to classify finite-order elements of the written integral linear group and state precisely the roles of conjugacy and inversion; those qualifications occur just above the claim.

### R10 — Scan 514, ll. 8–10 — unproved claim

The cyclic subgroups of orders 4 and 6 are identified with the automorphism groups of the “deux courbes elliptiques exceptionnelles” in characteristic zero (the abbreviation read as `autom.` is uncertain). A verification would require identifying the curves and explaining which point or origin their automorphisms preserve; neither identification is supplied on this page.

### R11 — Scan 514, ll. 11–17 — conjecture / expressed doubt

The author says that he has no formula to “placer” the generators and adds “sans doute” about generation of the full group from generation modulo its centre. He immediately warns about “la relation supplémentaire”, so the uncertainty and subsequent relation should be studied together rather than treating the tentative implication as an unqualified assertion.

### R12 — Scan 514, equation (16) — own idea (high confidence as a verification plan, not as a historical or novelty claim)

Check the tentative lifting argument directly from the displayed relation `u_4^2=u_6^3` and the next line's identification with the central element `-1`. The reason for confidence in this plan is that the manuscript itself singles out precisely the central element that the argument would need to recover.

### R13 — Scan 515, ll. 12–16 / equation (20) — conjecture / expectation

“Je veux maintenant me convaincre” introduces the desired compatibility of the completed homomorphism with the outer action of `Γ=Π_Q`. This is stated as a goal here; a verification would have to specify how the two outer actions are compared, including their indeterminacy by inner automorphisms.

### R14 — Scan 515, ll. 17–21 / equation (21) — conjecture / expectation

“J'ai envie de définir directement” and “et m̄ de le relever” describe a proposed direct construction and a lift from the quotient by `±1` to the full completed group. The page does not yet establish that this stronger construction respects the indicated arithmetic action.

### R15 — Scan 515, equations (19)–(21) — own idea (medium confidence as a research plan)

Separate the existence of a lift across the central quotient by `±1` from compatibility of that lift with the outer arithmetic action. The reason to try this separation is the author's explicit move from the quotient in (20) to the larger target in (21); it may expose an obstruction that would be hidden by checking the displayed generator relations alone.

### R16 — Scan 516, equation (22) and following relators — unproved claim

The target “s'identifie au quotient” by the invariant subgroup generated by the three displayed relators. A proof would have to show that these relators give the whole kernel, not merely that their images are trivial; the page records the assertion without a separate proof.

### R17 — Scan 516, ll. 11–13 and diagonal margin — unproved claim

“Peut s'interpréter comme un groupe de Teichmüller” is supported by a short extension statement in the margin and the equality `T^{!+}_{0,3}=(1)`. Checking the assertion requires fixing exactly what the `!` and `+` decorations mean and verifying the exceptional cases covered by the partly uncertain “non ab.” condition.

### R18 — Scan 516, between (23) and (24) — conjecture

“Dont je soupçonne qu'il se prolonge en un hom” explicitly proposes an extension from the groups decorated by `+` to the groups displayed in (24). A proof would need to specify the image of the extra coset and verify the relations connecting it to the subgroup in (23).

### R19 — Scan 516, annotation below (24) — unproved claim

The domain is described as an “ext. de {1,τ} par Π_{0,3}” and identified with a “groupe cartographique” bearing two uncertain adjectives. The extension structure and the cartographic interpretation merit independent verification; the adjacent marginal “pas encore défini” has an uncertain attachment and should not be assigned a more precise referent without further manuscript evidence.

### R20 — Scan 516, final two lines — unpursued implication

“J'interprète le premier mb de (23)” as the “Π_1 ‘géométrique transcendant’ du topos modulaire” shifts the proposed group map toward a moduli-theoretic construction. The sentence continues on the following scan, so its interpretation should be checked together with that continuation before concluding which moduli object is intended.

### R21 — Scan 516, equation (24) — own idea (medium confidence as a verification plan)

Given a candidate image for the nontrivial element of the displayed two-element quotient, calculate its conjugation action on the two chosen generators and compare it with the domain extension. This is a concrete test of the stated expectation; confidence is only medium because the page does not completely spell out the extension action or fix the generator matrices.

### R22 — Scan 517, lines 6–10 and (25) — kind: conjecture (expressed expectation)

Grothendieck writes “On devrait donc pouvoir définir …” a morphism of modular multiplicities over `Q` that “donnerait naissance à (23).” The open task at this point is to give a geometric construction and then verify that its induced map is the previously written homomorphism, including the treatment of stabilizers. The heavily overwritten superscript of the target in (25) prevents a confident statement here about the precise version of the target.

### R23 — Scan 517, (26) and following paragraph — kind: unproved claim

The asserted identification `M_{0,4}^{!} ≃ U_{0,3}` turns the requested datum into “une famille de courbes elliptiques sur U_{0,3}.” A proof at the stated moduli level would need to track the ordering of all four marked points and the descent of the normalization of three of them; identifying point sets alone would not settle the assertion for families.

### R24 — Scan 518, lines 1–6, continuing scan 517 — kind: unproved claim

The branched quadratic covering is said to give “une courbe elliptique,” with the point over `0` chosen as origin and the other points becoming “les trois points d'ordre 2.” A verification would need to establish smoothness and genus one for the covering and identify its covering involution with inversion relative to that origin. The choice of origin and the order of the branch labels should be checked explicitly against the notation used later.

### R25 — Scan 518, lines 7–15 — kind: unproved claim

The construction is extended to a base scheme with `2` invertible and to systems `(E,α,β)` in which the sections form a basis of `{}_2E`. One should verify that the construction and basis condition are preserved by base change, and explain the local constancy property inserted into the text. The manuscript's many revisions in this sentence make the intended source category a point requiring special care in any reconstruction.

### R26 — Scan 518, lines 15–18 — kind: unpursued implication

The third section `γ=α+β` appears “comme un troisième larron,” with other ordered pairs asserted to be bases as well. This suggests comparing the permutations of the three nonzero sections with permutations of the corresponding three nonzero branch labels, keeping the origin separate. The damaged canceled ordered pair should not be used as evidence for a particular permutation formula.

### R27 — Scan 518, lines 19–23 — kind: unproved claim

The functor is described by “en associant à E le quotient E/±1,” equipped with the four image sections. A proof would need to show that this quotient is a relative projective line in the intended sense and that the four image sections remain pairwise disjoint over every base point. It would also have to specify the behavior on isomorphisms, which is not worked out in these lines.

### R28 — Scan 518, quotient construction — kind: own idea. Confidence: medium; reason: the displayed quotient forgets a visible involution, but the precise categorical conventions are not settled by this page alone

Test the construction on an elliptic curve with a chosen basis of its 2-torsion and compare its automorphisms with those of the marked quotient projective line. This is a concrete way to locate any loss of faithfulness before trying to prove that the construction is an equivalence; it is a proposed check, not a claim of novelty or an established result in these notes.

### R29 — Scan 519, left margin — Unproved claim / proposed simplification

“Les pages qui suivent sont inutilement compliquées” introduces a proposed simplification using a directly specified elliptic family over `U_{0,3}` and a map to `M_{1,1}`. The readable phrase “il suffit d'y aller” and the final “cf plus bas” leave the construction and its comparison with the primed moduli objects to be checked elsewhere. A proof would have to identify the resulting morphism and compare its induced geometric and arithmetic fundamental-group maps; the marginal equation itself first requires independent confirmation of its transcription.

### R30 — Scan 519, main ll. 1–13 — Unproved claim

The functor is described as “presque une équivalence”, with the elliptic involution acting trivially on the quotient object, and the proposed repair replaces isomorphisms by their quotient under `±1` before passing to an associated champ. A proof would need full faithfulness after that quotient, local essential surjectivity, and effective descent for the resulting objects. The manuscript's passage from the crossed-out “catégorie fibrée” to the inserted “champ” makes the descent step a substantive part of the construction.

### R31 — Scan 519, main ll. 13–21, (27) — Unproved claim

The resulting champ is said to be “représentable par une multiplicité modulaire”, with the displayed completed modular group modulo `±1` as geometric fundamental group. The finite-level presentation in (27) points toward a proof but does not supply compatibility between the level presentations or the fundamental-group calculation on this page. Those comparisons would need to preserve the distinction between a quotient presentation and an ordinary quotient space.

### R32 — Scan 519, main ll. 22–25 — Unproved claim

The insertion “le ss-groupe central” modifies the assertion that `±1` “opère” trivially on the level-moduli object. Verification requires the exact moduli functor and the meaning of the group action, including whether equality means equality of marked objects or equality of their isomorphism classes. This is the step used to replace the finite linear group by its primed quotient.

### R33 — Scan 520, immediately after (28) — Unproved claim

The presentation is said to “ne dépend pas du choix” of the level, in the written range with lower bound 2. A proof would require compatible comparison morphisms between presentations at different levels and a check of the endpoint of that range. The compressed adverb preceding this assertion is uncertain in the transcription; the independence assertion itself is legible.

### R34 — Scan 520, (29)–(30) — Unproved claim

The morphism from the four-pointed genus-zero moduli object is asserted to be “un rev. galoisien” with the indicated three-letter permutation group, more precisely the level-2 object over `M'_{11}`. A proof would need to recover the relevant level-2 data from the labelled branch points, account for automorphisms, and identify the full deck group with the displayed finite linear group. The additional small signs attached to the moduli notation remain palaeographically unresolved.

### R35 — Scan 520, paragraph following (30) — Unproved claim

The geometric fundamental group of the level-2 object is described as “isomorphe au noyau” of the displayed reduction map. A proof would need the connectedness of the finite cover and the compatibility of its geometric fundamental group with the profinite topology on the corresponding finite-index subgroup. Keeping the central quotient and completion operations explicit is necessary to justify the stated factorization.

### R36 — Scan 520, (31) — Unpursued implication

The “suites exactes” diagram supplies a possible route to the compatibility of the geometric map with the outer Galois actions. These pages end with the diagram, without an explicit base-point comparison or a statement of the ambiguity under inner conjugation. Recording those choices would be needed before using the diagram to identify a particular earlier group homomorphism.

### R37 — Scans 519–520, central quotient and (29)–(30) — Own idea

Compare the inertia groups before and after quotienting the elliptic involution, especially at elliptic objects with additional automorphisms, before interpreting the morphism as a cover of ordinary spaces. **Confidence: medium**, because the manuscript explicitly removes a central involution and then presents a nontrivial finite Galois cover; the proposed local check is motivated by those two operations, but its outcome is not asserted here. This is a suggested verification, not an established conclusion or a claim of novelty.

### R38 — Scan 520, (29)–(31), compared with (17), (22), and (23) in the supplied earlier scans — Own idea

Compute the index of the image of the geometric fundamental-group map associated with the asserted finite cover and compare it with the earlier generator-defined map. **Confidence: medium**, because the cover and finite group in (30) make an index test concrete, while identifying the two maps requires choices and comparisons not made on this page. A mismatch would be evidence to distinguish the constructions, not grounds to alter the manuscript or declare a contradiction without further investigation.

# LM_P053 — cote 140-2, scans 521–530  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P053\LM_P053_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

Each item identifies its scan location and one of the requested kinds. “Conjecture” includes explicit questions, doubts, and expectations; “unproved claim” includes deferred work and claims whose local justification is only a sketch. A point may be reconsidered or resolved later in the supplied sequence or elsewhere in the manuscript: it remains recorded at the place where it is raised. These notes do not establish novelty or the state of the later literature. **Own ideas** are proposed checks or constructions, with confidence and reasons; none changes the transcription. All source references are to Grothendieck (1981), using the scan numbering specified in the task.

1. **Scan 521, ll. 15–21 — unproved claim.** “cet hom. (27) n'a rien d'injectif, par contre il est surjectif” reverses an apparent expectation about the earlier map; the number 27 is itself a marked reading. A proof would first require recovering that map from the preceding manuscript pages, then computing its kernel and image with the distinction between `Sl(2,Z)` and its quotient by ±1 maintained. The local passage supplies an assertion and a correction of viewpoint, not those computations. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 521).

2. **Scans 521–522, page transition — conjecture.** “Il faudra donc que je revienne encore sur une façon de donner un sens arithmético-géométrique …” records an explicit intention to revisit the earlier construction. The doubtful adjective at the start of scan 522 is not settled from the argument; what is clear is the wish to supply a geometric interpretation and an extension to profinite groups. (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 521–522).

3. **Scan 522, ll. 5–10, (34) — unproved claim.** “les arguments faits dans le cadre schématique, marchent aussi dans le cas transcendant” asserts transport of the earlier argument to the complex setting. Verification would require specifying the objects and comparison maps and checking that kernels and the central quotient are respected. The literal label under the first T in (34) differs from the corresponding label in (35), so a proof must first distinguish a manuscript notation issue from a substantive assertion without altering the diplomatic record. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 522).

4. **Scan 522, ll. 15–19 — conjecture.** “On aimerait interpréter (35) et (33) …” and “J'y reviendrai …” defer the proposed identification with the exact sequences associated with the earlier diagram, read tentatively as (9). The missing earlier diagram is essential to testing whether the proposed identifications commute with all maps and with completion. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 522).

5. **Scans 522–523, final remark and opening — conjecture.** “On peut se demander si l'hom … se remonte (de façon plus ou moins naturelle)” asks for a lift through the quotient by ±1, in both profinite and discrete forms. The upper margin of scan 523 answers that a lift is possible and “plus ou moins trivial”; the body immediately separates mere existence from compatibility with Γ. (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 522–523).

6. **Scan 523, ll. 5–9 — unproved claim.** Freeness “avec deux gén” is invoked to assert “d'exactement quatre façons” to lift, and the parenthesis claims compatibility with the discrete objects inside the profinite setting. A proof would need to specify the equivalence relation on lifts, select the two generators, and check whether their independent central signs exhaust the choices. The word transcribed as “niveaux” in that parenthesis is uncertain, so its precise comparison claim should be verified before formalization. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 523).

7. **Scan 523, ll. 10–14 — conjecture.** “Mais peut-on le faire en respectant les op. de Γ?” asks for arithmetic equivariance after the elementary lifting observation. The proposed sufficient condition is a lift of the map from `U_{0,3}` to the elliptic moduli object across the `Z/2`-gerbe. Testing sufficiency requires retaining the arithmetic fundamental-group extensions and the effect of basepoint choices, rather than only a map of geometric groups. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 523).

8. **Scan 523, ll. 14–19 and lower margin — conjecture.** “je suspecte … que l'inverse doit être vrai” proposes an anabelian converse: a Γ-compatible group-theoretic lift should arise from a geometric lift. The marginal “pas tout à fait … pour une formulation plus raisonnable” qualifies that expectation and directs attention to the next page. Any investigation should record this qualification and specify whether maps are actual homomorphisms or outer homomorphisms. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 523).

9. **Scan 523, ll. 19–22 — unproved claim.** The existence of the geometric lift “signifierait [exactement] l'existence d'une famille de courbes elliptiques …”. The inserted adverb is doubtful. A proof should identify the moduli functor, the level structure continued on the next page, and the residual automorphisms so that the equivalence is stated at the appropriate groupoid level. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 523).

10. **Scan 523, “quatre façons” and Γ-question — own idea.** Treat the four lifts, conditional on the manuscript's count, as a finite Γ-set and compare its fixed points with sections of the arithmetic lifting problem. This could isolate the difference between the existence of an invariant geometric lifting class and a homomorphism of the full arithmetic extensions. **Confidence: medium**: the finite action is suggested directly by the four choices and the equivariance question, but the precise action and equivalence relation still require construction; this is an investigation, not a claim of novelty or a proved result.

11. **Scan 524, lines 1–6 — conjecture.** Grothendieck writes, “Je doute qu'il en existe une,” about the proposed rigidification, and adds that he doubts the corresponding lift in profinite groups with operations can be made. The preceding page must be retained when specifying exactly which rigidification and compatibility conditions are meant; this is a recorded expectation, not a nonexistence argument (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 524).

# LM_P054 — cote 140-2, scans 531–540  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P054\LM_P054_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

“Unproved claim” means that the required argument is not supplied in these ten scans; it does not mean that the assertion is false, novel, or unproved elsewhere. Each location below cites the supplied manuscript directly (Grothendieck, 1981). Own ideas are proposed checks or comparisons, with their confidence and reasons stated. They do not alter the transcription. No explicit conjecture has been inferred merely from a doubtful punctuation mark.

### 5.1. Questions, assertions, implications, and proposed checks

1. **Scan 531, approximately lines 9–17 — unproved claim / authorial question.** Grothendieck writes “de s'assurer qu'il en est bien ainsi” before requiring the homomorphism just used to agree, through a suitable isomorphism, with the other displayed homomorphism and its exterior actions. A proof would have to construct the comparison, specify its dependence on basepoints or paths, and verify compatibility with the exterior actions; a match between abstract group presentations would not by itself establish the intended compatibility. This records a comparison problem, not a claim that it has already been solved here.

2. **Scan 532, approximately lines 5–9 — authorial doubt / correction.** The “naturel” homomorphism is said to be “pas du tout celui qu'on avait en vue,” followed by “il me faut revenir à la charge.” This explicitly reopens the construction at the preceding page boundary. The statement should be checked against the eventual replacement construction before attributing a completed comparison proof to this passage.

3. **Scan 533, approximately lines 10–15 — unproved claim.** The parenthesis says that the two faithfulness conditions are “équivalentes” and concludes that each stabilizer is “un groupe cyclique.” A proof needs to use the actual hypotheses on the properly acting discrete group and the local surface action, including orientation preservation, and to clarify whether the global/local faithfulness comparison needs connectedness or an effectiveness assumption on each component.

4. **Scan 533, approximately lines 15–22 — unproved claim.** The quotient is asserted to be a paracompact surface, while the locus of nontrivial stabilizers and its image are called “partie discrète.” One should supply local quotient charts, a justification for discreteness under the stated action hypotheses, and the relation between the ramification index and the stabilizer order. These are proof obligations suggested by the written proposition, rather than silent additions to its hypotheses.

5. **Scan 533, diagonal margin — unproved claim.** The “Variante” asserts equivalences for equivariant covering categories and their fundamental groups after passage through a normal subgroup. Its exact ornamental group symbols and some wording remain uncertain, so a proof should only be formulated after checking the marginal transcription; it would need to define the quotient action and track the residual group in the covering-category construction.

6. **Scan 533, diagonal margin, `Application` — unpursued implication.** The marginal application links a group with subscript `(0,3)` to the primed T-like group with subscript `(1,1)` and writes a further extension by `\Pi_{0,3}`. This invites an explicit comparison of the extension and the displayed linear group, but the first linear-group letter is uncertain between `Gl` and `Sl`, so the transcription cannot settle which comparison is intended.

7. **Scans 531–533 — own idea (confidence: medium).** Compare the failed and proposed homomorphisms through their induced actions on a chosen covering category, with basepoint-change paths recorded explicitly. This may expose whether the discrepancy is in the abstract homomorphism, the identification of source/target, or the exterior-action compatibility; the reason for trying it is Grothendieck's own transition from a failed “natural” map to the covering-category formulation. This is a proposed investigation, not an established or claimed new result.

8. **Scan 534, (a)–(b), equation (1) — unproved claim.** The page asserts an “équivalence de catégories” between equivariant covers and covers subordinate to a ramification signature. A proof would need the local ramification model at nonfree orbits, reconstruction of the equivariant cover, and verification that morphisms descend and lift; those details are not supplied here.

9. **Scan 534, NB, approximately lines 6–15 — unproved claim.** “On peut expliciter un foncteur quasi-inverse” is followed by the prescription of a “normalisé” fibre product, with “un sens topologique facile à expliciter.” The missing construction should define that topological normalization at the branch locus and establish the two inverse equivalences; the scheme version likewise requires checking the hypotheses under which normalization gives the claimed cover.

10. **Scan 534, corollary, equation (2) — unproved claim.** The text gives an “isom canonique” of fundamental groups from the categorical comparison. Establishing its canonicity requires matching the fibre functors at the selected points, in addition to the categorical equivalence; the doubtful left basepoint in the manuscript remains a transcription issue.

11. **Scan 535, equation (3) — unproved claim.** For connected X, the page writes a “suite exacte canonique.” A proof must identify the kernel with the ordinary fundamental group of X and obtain the surjection to G from equivariant-cover monodromy; the circled correction makes the distinction between ordinary and equivariant fundamental groups especially worth checking.

12. **Scan 535, NB, approximately lines 4–12 — unproved claim / authorial expectation.** After claiming an analogous scheme-theoretic corollary, Grothendieck writes “il faudrait (si j'en ai besoin) faire un peu attention” when passing to relative smooth curves. His statement is explicitly left to be formulated more carefully; a proof would first need precise base, ramification, and connectedness hypotheses. The isolated mark after “On a” may itself be a question mark, but that reading is uncertain.

13. **Scan 535, example, equation (4) — unproved claim.** The quotient is specified by the three orbit rows and ramification indices “d₀=2”, “d₁=2”, and “d∞=3.” Verifying the example requires the actual action and quotient map, checking every exceptional stabilizer and confirming the stated image of each orbit; the deleted quotient identification should not be reconstructed from those expectations in the transcription.

### 5.2. Literature comparisons proposed for further study

These comparisons were added after the readings were made. Their terminology does not replace the manuscript's own terminology or settle a doubtful symbol.

1. **Scans 533–537, covering-category comparison and exact sequences — own idea (literature comparison; confidence: medium).** Recast the proposed equivariant covering category through the quotient stack `[X/G]`, then compare its fibre functor and inertia with Noohi's covering-space Galois theory (2005, §§18.2–18.3, especially Theorem 18.19). The reason for this comparison is the close match between the manuscript's categorical and fundamental-group assertions and the modern covering-stack formulation, but the local path-connectedness and semilocal simple-connectedness hypotheses must be checked before applying that theorem. This offers a proof-organizing framework, not a claim that the two formulations have already been identified.

2. **Scans 539–540, the `Gl` margin, level structures, and (11) — own idea (literature comparison; confidence: medium).** Compare the unrestricted level-basis problem written here with Hain's pairing-normalized level structures and congruence-subgroup description (2014, §4.2). The reason is that the choice of a pairing value can affect which change-of-basis group and which geometric component are being considered, so the conventions must be aligned before comparing connectedness statements. The comparison does not authorize replacing the manuscript's `Gl` by `Sl`, or changing either torsion display.

3. **Scans 535 and 537–539, relative curves, representability, and the base with the level inverted — own idea (literature comparison; confidence: medium).** Use Deligne and Rapoport's *Les schémas de modules de courbes elliptiques* (1973) as a primary comparison source for the proposed relative and integral formulations. The reason is that the manuscript changes base and level conventions while leaving several representability assertions unproved here; a useful next step is to build a statement-by-statement comparison specifying the level functor, base, stabilizers, and quotient universal property. This is a research lead, not an assertion that an unspecified theorem there proves all the statements on these pages.

## 5. Research notes — separate from the transcription

These English notes distinguish manuscript assertions from proposed checks. “Unproved claim” means that a proof is not written out at the cited locus; it does not mean that Grothendieck lacked a proof or that the claim remains open. Some points are developed later within this ten-page extract, as indicated, and others may be addressed elsewhere in the manuscript or literature. These notes make no claim of novelty and have not been used to repair the transcription. Parenthetical APA references identify the supplied primary source; no survey of later literature is implied.

1. **Scan 541, (13)–(14) — unproved claim.** “On récupère les” introduces the level-change formula and its expression as a quotient by a kernel. A proof would need to identify the level-change functor, the action conventions in the contracted product, and the base over which the quotient has the asserted meaning; equations (9)–(10), cited later, are outside this extract. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 541.)

(Grothendieck, 1981, scan 541.)

(Grothendieck, 1981, scan 542.)

# LM_P056 — cote 140-2, scans 551–560  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P056\LM_P056_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English

These are reading notes and proposed checks, not a literature review or claims of novelty. “Unproved claim” means a statement or step not justified in detail at the cited location; it does not assert that the entire manuscript lacks a proof. Where the supplied pages themselves return to an earlier question, that is identified. The required label “conjecture” also covers an author's explicitly recorded question or expectation, with that distinction stated. Own ideas are marked as such and include confidence and reasons. Uncertain source readings remain uncertain when quoted here.

### Scans 551–554

- **Scan 551, approximately lines 3–9, (33) — unproved claim.** The text identifies the elements attached to partitions with the “permutations paires d'ordre 2” and says that they and the identity form `V(I)`. A proof within this four-element setting would list the three unordered partitions into pairs, compute the products of their associated permutations, and check compatibility with relabelling; these checks would justify the displayed bijection without adding anything to its transcription (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 551).
- **Scan 551, approximately lines 12–20, (34)–(36) — unproved claim.** “Cette bijection étant compatible avec le transport des structures” is used to identify the induced symmetric-group isomorphism with the displayed composite. A complete verification would check the action of a permutation fixing `i` on the partition determined by `{i,j}`, then verify the stated composite on every `j` (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 551).
- **Scan 551, last two lines — own idea (high confidence; reason: the manuscript explicitly has a four-element indexing set and the stabilizers in (36)).** The phrase “d'indice 3” deserves a textual and mathematical check against the surrounding manuscript. For the ordinary symmetric group on four elements, a stabilizer of one element has index four by the orbit–stabilizer calculation; the transcription therefore preserves `3` while the notes flag the discrepancy rather than silently repairing it (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 551).

1. **Scan 552, upper third, approximately lines 5–13 — unproved claim.** The comparison maps are said to form a “syst. transitif d'isom.” after the correction replacing the identity on the two common elements by “la transposition”. A proof should track the maps through the common three-element partition set and verify the cocycle identity for three omitted indices, including the precise bijection on their common elements (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 552).

2. **Scan 552, proposition, approximately lines 17–22 — unproved claim.** The proposition states that the action of the subgroup consisting of the identity and even involutions “est triviale” on the indicated four-point moduli object, hence factors through the symmetric group of the partition set. Proving this in the indicated moduli setting requires an automorphism implementing each double transposition and a check that the construction is compatible with families, rather than only a calculation on individual geometric points. The corollary and coordinate proof on supplied scan 556 return to this statement (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 552, 556).

3. **Scan 552, corollary, final three lines — unpursued implication.** The assertion that each point-stabilizer action “est déduite de celle de” the quotient group suggests that choosing different distinguished points should lead to compatibly identified effective actions. It is useful to distinguish the canonical identification through the partition set from an identification obtained by simply matching the common labels, because the preceding correction shows those bijections need not coincide (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 552).

4. **Scan 553, final paragraph, approximately lines 17–23 — conjecture (explicit question and tentative expectation).** Grothendieck asks “comment passer d'une de ces” actions to the other and adds “On a envie de penser que ce sont les” abbreviated *mêmes*. This should be treated as a request to identify the two actions with the relevant labeling conventions, not as an already proved assertion of literal equality; the exact parenthetical characterization of the question is partly uncertain in the transcription. The explicit comparison in (38)–(40), on supplied scans 555–556, returns to this question (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 553, 555–556).

5. **Scan 553, approximately lines 7–16 — own idea.** The two indicated copies of the three-letter symmetric group could be compared explicitly on the three partitions into pairs, keeping the chosen bijections of their label sets visible throughout. **Confidence: high as a check to perform**, because the text specifies both subgroup embeddings and the finite partition set, so every action can be enumerated without importing additional moduli conventions.

6. **Scan 553, approximately line 16 — own idea.** The visible phrase “qui fixe les trois premiers éléments” deserves an independent mathematical audit against its immediate subgroup notation: pointwise fixation of three labels would be incompatible with a nontrivial three-letter symmetric group acting on those labels, whereas setwise preservation would be a different statement. **Confidence: high in the need for this audit**, because the phrase and the displayed embedding are readable; the observation does not authorize changing `fixe` or the numeral in the transcription.

7. **Scan 554, after (32), approximately lines 7–12 — unproved claim.** The map on the three partitions “est surjectif” and its kernel is described as a two-dimensional vector space over the two-element field; its action makes the original four-element set a torsor. A direct proof would enumerate the kernel permutations and check that each nonidentity element is fixed-point-free, which is the additional condition needed for simple transitivity (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 554).

8. **Scan 554, approximately lines 12–19 — unproved claim.** The text asserts that the four-element set has “1 et 1 seule structure de plan affine” over the two-element field and that every permutation is affine. A proof should specify the intrinsic affine structure, explain in what sense uniqueness is literal on the fixed underlying set, and verify that the group of translations is exactly the subgroup already defined (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 554).

9. **Scan 554, final four lines — unpursued implication.** The phrase “ce qui suggère d'interpréter” the three-element partition set as the nonzero translation vectors points to a canonical equivalence between a partition into pairs and the translation whose orbits are those pairs. This should be checked for equivariance under all permutations of the four-element set, so that the resulting interpretation also accounts for the asserted automorphism group. The explicit bijection (33) is on supplied scan 551, earlier in the supplied file order (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 551, 554).

10. **Scan 554, approximately lines 12–19 — own idea.** One way to test the affine-structure assertion is to define the ternary operation on three distinct labels by taking the fourth label, and to prescribe the value on repeated labels as suggested by the expression `x+y+z` in characteristic two. **Confidence: medium**, because the proposed construction is intrinsic and fits the four-point model, but the heap/affine identities and their compatibility with the manuscript's translation subgroup still require explicit checking.

### Scans 555–557

#### 555-R1 — Specified conjugacy of the two symmetric-group actions

**Scan/location:** 555, displays (38)–(39) and corollary, continuing into (40) on scan 556. **Kind:** unpursued implication. The phrase “via l'autom.” and the explicit permutation `1↦4, 2↦3, 3↦2` make the choice of identification of the two actions part of the statement, rather than merely an abstract identification of groups. It would be useful to track this particular relabelling when comparing subsequent basepoint choices or named inertia elements, because an unspecified identification with the same abstract symmetric group can hide that information (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 555–556).

#### 555-R2 — Removing the inner twist at the level of the comparison map

**Scan/location:** 555, corollary; 556, (40). **Kind:** own idea. With the left-action convention suggested by (40), test the modified map `ψ(x)=σ₁⁻¹·φ(x)` to see whether the comparison becomes strictly equivariant for the same labelled group. **Confidence:** high for this algebraic test, because substituting (40) cancels the two adjacent factors `σ₁⁻¹σ₁`; the handwritten `1/i` ambiguity and the precise action convention must first be settled from the manuscript (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 555–556).

#### 556-R1 — The earlier proposition and its reformulation

**Scan/location:** 556, lines approximately 2–11. **Kind:** unproved claim. Grothendieck writes “Il faut quand” followed by the sign for *même* and “démontrer la prop.”, then says that the statement “équivaut” to the four-section corollary. The corollary receives a coordinate argument on this page, but the exact earlier reference and the two directions of the claimed equivalence should be traced explicitly; the handwritten reference after `prop.` is uncertain (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 556).

#### 556-R2 — The normalization and uniqueness steps

**Scan/location:** 556, “évidemment unique” and proof beginning “OPS”, approximately lines 10–15. **Kind:** unproved claim. The proof compresses the passage to the normalized projective line into “OPS” and does not spell out the uniqueness argument. A complete verification over an arbitrary base would need to justify the local normalization and show that the locally constructed automorphisms agree on overlaps, using the effect on three disjoint sections; this is a request to supply the omitted details of the argument actually written here (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 556).

#### 556-R3 — The weakened disjointness condition

**Scan/location:** 556, final NB, approximately lines 18–21. **Kind:** unpursued implication. The observation “pas la peine que” the last two sections be mutually disjoint suggests studying the same formula on the locus where those two sections can coincide, while the two indicated triples remain disjoint. The page does not describe the resulting fixed locus or its behaviour over bases of different characteristics; the uncertain middle index of the second triple should be resolved before giving a formal moduli interpretation (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 556).

#### 556-R4 — A coordinate-free check through the projective matrix

**Scan/location:** 556, formula `u(z)=λ/z` and `λ=s₃s₄`. **Kind:** own idea. Test the construction with the matrix `[[0,ab],[1,0]]` for invertible sections `a,b`: its square is `ab` times the identity and its determinant is `−ab`, which gives a direct calculation to examine over a general base, including the allowed coincidence `a=b`. **Confidence:** high for the proposed matrix calculation, because these identities are formal; the application to the global relative curve still requires the normalization and gluing details noted above (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 556).

#### 557-R1 — Quotient presentations and the exceptional level two clause

**Scan/location:** 557, (41)–(42). **Kind:** unproved claim. “On part de” introduces the two quotient presentations, with the explicit replacement of `M₁,₁[2]` by its primed version when `n=2`. A detailed verification should identify the represented objects and their automorphisms, and explain precisely why the level two replacement is necessary before applying the fundamental-group construction; this page states those identifications without supplying that moduli argument (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 557).

#### 557-R2 — Connectedness, geometric connectedness, and the cyclotomic margin note

**Scan/location:** 557, prose between (42) and (43), with left marginal note. **Kind:** unproved claim. The manuscript uses “est connexe” while allowing “s'il n'est pas géom connexe” and links the point to cyclotomic irreducibility in the margin. To make that justification explicit, one would need to describe the geometric components of the level space, their arithmetic permutation, and the connection with the cited cyclotomic equation; the attribution and singular/plural wording of the margin remain transcription doubts (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 557).

#### 557-R3 — Recovering the extension by pullback

**Scan/location:** 557, (43) and following proposition. **Kind:** unproved claim. The phrase “par image inverse” is followed by the assertion that the unprimed fundamental group is an “extension centrale” of the primed one by `{±1}`. A complete argument should identify the upper middle group with the pullback of the lower extension along `Γₙ→Γₙ′`, and then verify the kernel and its centrality; the diagram records the structure of this argument but the verification is not written out (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 557).

#### 557-R4 — The extension class as a further invariant

**Scan/location:** 557, final proposition. **Kind:** own idea. Once the central extension is established, one could ask whether its class can be read from the finite-level pullback description, and whether restrictions to suitably specified subgroups split. **Confidence:** medium, because the page gives a concrete central extension and compatible finite quotients, but basepoint conventions, the relevant category of extensions, and any splitting behaviour have not been checked here (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 557).

### Scans 558–560

#### 558-R1 — Unpursued implication; scan 558, margin beside (45)

Grothendieck warns, “Attention ne pas confondre” the completion of `Sl(2,Z)` with `Sl(2,Z-hat)`. Together with the downward surjection in (47), this marks a distinction whose kernel and information loss deserve separate study; these pages do not describe that kernel. The precise location of the completion sign is therefore mathematically consequential as well as a transcription issue (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 558).

#### 558-R2 — Unproved claim; scan 558, introduction to (46)

The phrase “compatibilité essentielle … la commutativité” asserts compatibility of the arithmetic fundamental-group sequence with the level-n matrix-group sequence. A full verification would need the definitions of the level structures, transition maps, and determinant character, with the chosen identifications tracked; the diagram itself does not provide those checks. The statement may depend on arguments on earlier pages (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 558).

#### 558-R3 — Own idea; scan 558, determinant and cyclotomic-character square in (46)

One possible proof route is to formulate the level-n monodromy on torsion and use a pairing to relate its determinant to the displayed cyclotomic character. **Confidence: medium**: the labels `det` and “caractère cyclotomique” motivate this route, but the exact pairing conventions and the manuscript's definition of the moduli objects must be checked before this becomes an argument. This idea is not used to repair any symbol in the transcription (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 558).

#### 558-R4 — Unproved claim; scan 558, (47) and following line

“Passant à la limite sur n” produces (47), and he explicitly adds “diagramme sur lequel nous allons revenir.” The passage invites verification that the finite-level maps are compatible and that the inverse-limit sequence has the asserted exactness and surjectivity. That later return is outside the present set of pages (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 558).

#### 559-R1 — Unproved claim; scan 559, (48)–(49)

Grothendieck says that one obtains the extension isomorphism “de façon entièrement conceptuelle.” A proof written out from these pages would have to verify that the moduli identification and the inner automorphism `int(σ₁)` used in (48) induce the particular comparison of geometric kernels and arithmetic quotients in (49). The reference to the preceding section should be checked before treating the abbreviated argument as a gap in the manuscript as a whole (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 559).

#### 559-R2 — Unpursued implication; scan 559, (50)–(51)

The completed isomorphism “est associé à un isom” of discrete groups in (51), where two displayed relations are imposed. This suggests studying which choices of generators and orientation determine that discrete isomorphism and how much of it remains detectable after completion. The next scan explicitly asks for its formula, so the present note concerns the relation between the two levels rather than claiming the question is overlooked (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 559).

#### 560-R1 — Conjecture (author's request for an explicit construction); scan 560, approximately lines 4–9

“Il faudrait quand même expliciter l'hom (51)” identifies an unfinished task: compute formulas for a homomorphism so far defined conceptually. He explicitly states that it is defined only “modulo autom. intérieurs, a priori,” so any concrete answer must declare the choices that resolve that ambiguity. This is a request and expectation, not a conjectural truth statement in the usual sense (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 560).

#### 560-R2 — Conjecture (author's expectation about difficulty); scan 560, approximately lines 12–14

The computation is called “un calcul-clef,” with the insertion “sûrement instructif,” and he expects that it “ne devrait pas présenter de difficulté particulière.” This is his stated assessment; no calculation on this page establishes its feasibility or resolves the inner-automorphism ambiguity. It is worth checking where, if anywhere, he later carries it out (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 560).

#### 560-R3 — Own idea; scan 560, requested formula for (51)

A candidate computation could choose explicit order-two and order-three matrices modulo the central signs, then compare their geometric monodromies with the two generators in (51). **Confidence: medium**: the exponents visible in the quotient suggest this construction, but the exact loops, multiplication order, and action convention are not fixed on these pages. A bare abstract presentation is insufficient to identify Grothendieck's geometrically defined map (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 560).

#### 560-R4 — Unproved claim; scan 560, final paragraph

The author recalls “après avoir affirmé qu'il est” followed by the displayed affine-line-like identification, and “qu'il y a deux sections marquées.” The precise definition of the “schéma modulaire ‘grossier’” and its base must be recovered from earlier pages before one can justify this assertion, including its integral formulation. The exponent on the E is itself marked uncertain in the transcription and should not be used as secure evidence for a particular modern notation (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 560).

#### 560-R5 — Own idea; scan 560, final paragraph on the two marked sections

Check the behavior of those two sections in the fibers of characteristics 2 and 3, and distinguish the coarse moduli statement from stabilizer information carried by the preceding multiplicities. **Confidence: medium**: the integral base and the two special sections make these fibers a natural test, but the page ends mid-sentence and provides neither their coordinates nor a claim that they remain distinct in every fiber. This is a proposed check, not an asserted defect or a novelty claim (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 560).

# LM_P058 — cote 140-2, scans 571–575  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P058\LM_P058_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — separate from the transcription

These notes are in English and concern only what the supplied leaves state or leave open. “Conjecture” below includes an author's question, expectation, or proposed work program; it does not imply that he formulated a precise theorem. Own ideas are proposed investigations, not established results and not claims of novelty. Their confidence labels refer to the plausibility or usefulness of the proposed investigation.

### R1. Finite groups and the polyhedral table

**Location:** scans 571–572, (74)–(75). **Kind:** unproved claim.

The qualified “Sauf erreur” accompanies the tetrahedral and icosahedral identifications, followed by the four-row modular-curve/polyhedron table. A proof would have to recover the precise meanings of `SΓ′`, `GP`, and the prime on the level-2 curve, then verify the groups, covering actions, and orientation conventions; these leaves supply no such verification. The doubtful correction subscript in (74) remains a textual uncertainty and is not repaired by this proposed mathematical check (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 571–572).

### R2. Exhaustion of the rational congruence cases

**Location:** scan 571, approximately lines 13–15. **Kind:** unproved claim.

“Si je me rappelle bien” qualifies the assertion that the cases `n = 2, 3, 4, 5` exhaust the rational curves under discussion. Verification would need the exact moduli convention and a genus calculation, distinguishing the open curve from its compactification and checking what range of levels the surrounding discussion presupposes (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 571).

### R3. Why the realizations are congruence realizations

**Location:** scan 571, approximately lines 16–25. **Kind:** unproved claim.

The passage contrasts what was “clair” from the displayed group isomorphism with the further observation that the relevant subgroups are congruence subgroups. A proof would need to transport the combinatorial or covering objects through the stated isomorphism and separately identify their congruence kernels; the relation between these two steps is not worked out here (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 571).

### R4. The scope of the folded-edge exception

**Location:** scan 571, margin; scan 573, figure (76). **Kind:** unpursued implication.

The marginal “sauf un” directs the reader to the example with the tentatively read “arêtes repliées”. This makes it important to determine whether the asserted exhaustion concerns polyhedra in a restricted geometric sense or regular maps admitting the pictured edge behavior. The definitions and the exact status of this exception require comparison with the surrounding manuscript (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 571, 573).

### R5. Exhaustion by the listed proper quotients

**Location:** scan 572, quotient list a)–c) and the remark on d). **Kind:** unproved claim.

“On trouve comme quotients possibles” introduces an asserted complete list, with the exclusion of d) attributed to simplicity. A proof would enumerate the normal subgroups of the four displayed groups and then show why the resulting rational covers reduce to the two cases subsequently described. The uncertain source subscript in b) must be resolved textually before treating that particular written map as a reliable statement (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 572).

### R6. The quadratic cover and its drawn map

**Location:** scan 572, approximately lines 22–29. **Kind:** unproved claim.

The argument that the ramification index must “diviser 2 et 3” is followed by the equation `y = √(x(x−1))` and the one-vertex equatorial picture. A complete verification should specify the branch-point conventions, justify the unramified point, and recover the stated face and vertex indices from the cover. This would also clarify how the square-root expression is being used as a description of the covering curve (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 572).

### R7. The cubic quotient and figure (76)

**Location:** scan 572, final paragraph; scan 573, opening and (76). **Kind:** unproved claim.

The “rev. cyclique d'ordre 3” is described as ramified only at 0 and infinity and then associated with type `(3,3)`, folded edges, and a single triangular face. Reconstructing its monodromy and the corresponding cyclic ordering at the vertex would test the precise combinatorial interpretation of the picture. The unusual wording “une face triangulaires” remains a diplomatic reading, not a mathematical conclusion about the number of faces (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 572–573).

### R8. The proposed divisibility condition for rigidification
