### R13 — Scan 45, (63)

**Kind: unproved claim.** “Boucher le trou en i₀” is said to produce the group written as `π = L(π′)`. A proof should specify exactly which subgroup or conjugacy data are killed, recover the remaining lacet structure, and account for the distinction between “effectif” and “extérieur,” which the author’s revisions emphasize (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 45).

### R14 — Scan 45, last paragraph; scan 46, opening

**Kind: unpursued implication.** “Reprenant en sens inverse” introduces the reversal using the “foncteur ‘forage de trous’.” It remains to determine at what categorical level this is an inverse, which additional choices it requires, and whether the two composites come with canonical comparison maps (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 45–46).

### R15 — Scan 46, (64) and the invoked functor

**Kind: unproved claim.** The drilling functor is used to add a distinguished puncture and obtain the displayed decomposition of the index set. A full construction would specify its independence of presentations or coordinates and its action on exterior morphisms (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 46).

### R16 — Scan 46, (65)–(67)

**Kind: own idea.** Check the earlier convention for `T^{I(\widetilde π)}` before interpreting the displayed abelianization and coefficient-sum map; one can test the notation against an explicit peripheral presentation of the four-punctured sphere. **Confidence: high that the convention needs checking, low about any proposed correction**, because the full index set is visibly written, while the algebraic meaning of that superscript may have been fixed elsewhere. No augmentation relation, quotient, or reduced index set has been added to the transcription.

### R17 — Scan 46, (66)–(67) and following prose

**Kind: unproved claim.** The homomorphism is characterized by being “‘ramifié’ en tous les i,” and its kernel is assigned type `(1,4)`. Verification should show that the prescribed peripheral values respect all defining relations and should calculate the topological type of the associated two-sheeted cover (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 46).

### R18 — Scan 46, closing paragraph; scan 47, (68)–(69)

**Kind: unpursued implication.** “Ce n’est pas tout à fait un groupe extérieur” flags an ambiguity beyond inner automorphisms, attributed to the extra involution. The exact sequence and puncture-index comparison on scan 47 provide a place to track how this extra symmetry acts on representatives and on morphisms (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 46–47).

### R19 — Scan 47, closing paragraph; scan 48, opening

**Kind: unproved claim.** The requirement to have “‘choisi un noyau’” is described through a `(Z/2Z)`-gerbe and a connected groupoid with that fundamental group. A proof would construct this groupoid of choices explicitly and identify its automorphisms, then show how choosing an object supplies the stronger exterior-group datum sought in the preceding sentence (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 47–48).

### R20 — Scan 48, paragraph surrounding (70)

**Kind: conjecture / authorial expectation.** The qualification “il me semble” accompanies the assertion that the conceptual reflections prove a canonical isomorphism, with the parenthetical restriction read as “au moins mod autom intérieurs.” A fuller redaction should establish functoriality and state the residual inner ambiguity precisely; the right marginal qualification also needs its uncertain superscript resolved (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 48).

### R21 — Scan 48, after (70)

**Kind: unproved claim.** “Tout à fait indépendant, me semble-t-il” distinguishes the conceptual assertion from the claim that the displayed natural homomorphism to `Gl(2,Z)` is an isomorphism. To verify independence, one would audit the construction for hidden use of that identification or of a chosen identification of the two fundamental groups (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 48).

### R22 — Scan 48, closing paragraph; scan 49, opening

**Kind: unpursued implication.** The warning “plus sujet à caution” concerns identifying the target of (70) with the central quotient, while the next page permits that only “comme groupe extérieur.” This distinction suggests tracking the information lost when an actual homomorphism is replaced by its class up to inner automorphism, especially when composing such identifications (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 48–49).

### R23 — Scan 49, diagonal marginal note

**Kind: conjecture / authorial proposal.** “On pourrait inclure” introduces the suggested inclusion of complex conjugation so that (73) need not be restricted to the positive subgroups. To carry out the proposal, one would extend both the analytic construction and its group actions, then check compatibility with the involutions; several connecting words and the final abbreviation remain doubtful (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 49).

### R24 — Scan 49, (71)–(72)

**Kind: unproved claim.** A “morphisme canonique” of analytic modular objects is said to induce an isomorphism. Its construction, the significance of the primes, and its effect on the indicated fundamental groups require verification; the overwritten first target of (71) must be settled from the manuscript rather than silently reconciled with (72) (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 49).

### R25 — Scan 49, (73) and the following question

**Kind: conjecture / authorial question.** “Est-il possible de le préciser de façon utile, en un hom effectif, non seulement extérieur?” explicitly asks for a stronger version of the induced homomorphism. The proposed use of a canonical universal covering on the next lines should be checked for which choices it removes and which choices remain (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 49).

### R26 — Scan 50, (74)

**Kind: unproved claim.** The isomorphism is described as “pas seulement extérieur” and compared with (50) after restriction to an index-two subgroup. The proof obligations are to explain what the chosen universal-cover description fixes and to check the comparison with the earlier formula, which is outside the supplied excerpt (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 50).

### R27 — Scan 50, (75)–(76)

**Kind: unproved claim.** The “hom canonique” from `D` is asserted to be compatible with the displayed operator-group homomorphism. A verification would construct the map, prove the stated equivariance, and then establish the following universal-cover and mixed-fundamental-group identifications; the target group glyph is left explicitly doubtful in the transcription (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 50).

### R28 — Scan 50, annotation under (76)

**Kind: unproved claim / deferred reference.** The note says the isomorphism “est explicité dans” and leaves section/page references unfilled. The missing reference is an editorial task for comparison with the rest of the manuscript, not a number to be guessed or inserted here (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 50).

### R29 — Scan 50, final sentence

**Kind: unpursued implication.** “Pour pouvoir l’identifier” introduces an identification with a fundamental group at a written basepoint, but the excerpt stops at “il.” The next leaf should be checked for the required lift, path, or other datum and for how it interacts with the preceding canonicity claim; even the bar on the basepoint letter remains a marked reading issue (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 50).

### R30 — Scans 47–50, choice groupoid versus effective homomorphism

**Kind: own idea.** Formulate the groupoid of kernel choices and the groupoid of choices giving an effective version of (73), then test whether the construction supplies a functor between them or leaves an additional obstruction. **Confidence: medium**, because the manuscript explicitly juxtaposes a gerbe of kernel choices with the later effective-homomorphism question, but it does not identify those two choice problems on these pages.

# LM_P064 — cote 140-3, scans 51–60  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P064\LM_P064_notes.md]

## 4. Research notes — separate from the transcription

The categories distinguish the author's questions and expectations, unproved assertions, implications not pursued here, and proposed investigations of our own. A note classified as **conjecture** may record a tentative expectation or open question rather than a formally stated conjecture. Brief French quotations refer to the manuscript; an uncertain reading is identified where it affects interpretation. Own ideas carry confidence and reasons and are not attributed to Grothendieck as established results.


### Scans 51–53

1. **Scan 51, approximately lines 1–7 — Unproved claim.** The ambiguity in choosing the point is attributed to the displayed kernel, said to be « lui-\(\overline{\mathrm m}\) isomorphe à \(\Pi_{0,3}\) ». Checking this identification would require the preceding definitions of the prime on SL and of the pointed covering, as well as a precise comparison of the two group actions; those definitions are outside these supplied pages. The first SL digit remains a transcription doubt, not a mathematical emendation. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 51.)

2. **Scans 51–52, the three matrices and continuation — Unproved claim.** The passage lists « les trois éléments » taking \(j\) to \(-\bar j\), then infers that the two points are not congruent under the kernel modulo 2. A full verification should check each matrix action, establish that the displayed list is exhaustive in the precise quotient group being used, and then perform the reductions; merely checking the three reductions would not establish exhaustivity. Two lower-left matrix entries remain explicitly doubtful in the transcription. (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 51–52.)

3. **Scan 52, approximately lines 5–11 — Unproved claim.** Choosing the point above \(P\) to be a « racine de l'unité » is said to have « normalisé » the exterior homomorphism (73) into an effective one, and likewise (70). A proof should state exactly which inner-automorphism ambiguity the chosen lift removes and whether any residual stabilizer remains. The maps numbered (70) and (73) are referenced here but not defined within this batch. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 52, manuscript p. 314.)

4. **Scan 52, lower paragraph — Conjecture / expressed research intention.** « On aurait envie de reprendre les constructions précédentes dans le contexte des groupes profinis » is immediately qualified by « je manque des fondements nécessaires ». This identifies an intended profinite extension and a missing theory described by the tentatively read phrases « trouage » and « forage de trous »; it does not assert that such a theory has been constructed. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 52, manuscript p. 314.)

5. **Scan 53, approximately lines 1–10 — Conjecture / expectation.** « Pourtant on sent que c'est bien dans cette direction » introduces the hoped-for group-theoretic understanding of homomorphism (40), followed by « Ce devrait être une incitation ». A research task is to determine what data a purely group-theoretic description of that displayed homomorphism would require, especially which ingredients currently depend on the covering construction. The German adjective and the source-group alphabet are marked as uncertain in the transcription. (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 53.)

6. **Scan 53, lower paragraph, continued on scan 54 — Conjecture / question.** The inserted « la question s'il y a une » reframes the extension to the profinite context as a question, explicitly distinguishing it from introducing elements of « structure “arithmétique” ». The text makes that question depend on the status of the congruence relations discussed in the continuation. It should therefore be studied as a conditional problem, rather than read as an assertion that arbitrary suitable profinite automorphism groups already carry the desired construction. (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 53–54.)

7. **Scans 51–52 — Own idea. Confidence: high for the proposed check, low for any conclusion beyond it.** Once the uncertain entries and prime notation have been independently settled, a short table of the three fractional-linear actions and their reductions modulo 2 would provide an auditable local check of the orbit argument. The reason for confidence is that this is a finite calculation on the displayed matrices; it would still leave the completeness and covering-identification arguments to be proved. This is a verification proposal, not a claim of novelty or an established theorem.

8. **Scans 52–53 — Own idea. Confidence: low.** One possible way to formulate the missing profinite construction is to ask first for compatible constructions on every relevant finite quotient, then separately for preservation under the proposed arithmetic subgroup. The reason for low confidence is that compatibility, distinguished inertia data, and a universal property are not supplied here, so an inverse-limit formulation by itself would not establish existence. This separates two questions suggested by the passage without attributing this formulation to Grothendieck.

**Scan 60, approximate lines 15–20, (18) and final paragraph; kind: conjecture.** Grothendieck writes “On devrait avoir aussi la relation,” changes the displayed condition to “conjugué de,” and then says that it is not clear to him whether it follows from the conditions considered so far (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 60, (18) and final paragraph). **Scan 60, (18); kind: own idea; confidence: medium.** In a finite quotient with an element of order three representing `\rho`, one could compare the conjugacy class of the candidate image with the classes of the two nonidentity powers of `\rho`, using the relevant exponent modulo three. # LM_P066 — cote 140-3, scans 71–80  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P066\LM_P066_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

These notes identify questions for reconstruction and further study; they do not amend the diplomatic transcription. They use only the supplied extract, do not claim historical novelty, and do not establish whether a point is resolved elsewhere in the manuscript or literature. References below are to the supplied **scan numbers**, not the archive footer numbers. The provisional symbol $\xi$ in these notes does not resolve the transcription's $\xi/\zeta$ doubt, and no identification of the uncertain large group glyph is presupposed.

### 1. The normalizer statement behind the conjugator parameter

**Scan 71, (39)–(41), and scan 72, the calculation after (42). Kind: unproved claim.** The assertion that “$g_0$ est déterminé mod $L_0$” is accompanied by the use of a normalizer identity of the form $N_{\widehat{\Pi}_{0,3}}(L_1)=L_1$, which the following page invokes again without proving it in this extract. A reconstruction must identify the exact profinite subgroups and establish the required normalizer statement, keeping it distinct from a statement about the normalizer of one chosen element (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 71–72).

### 2. Independence from the representative of the right coset

**Scans 71–72, (40) and its following paragraph; scan 75, a), before (48). Kind: unproved claim.** The first passage calls $\gamma$ “bien déterminé” and says that $g$ “ne dépend en effet que de $g_0$ mod $L_0$”; the summary later describes the relation as “invariante par remplacement de $g_0$ par $g_0l_0^\lambda$.” These are related but distinct well-definedness checks: one concerns the reconstructed element and exponent, and the other concerns the equation imposed on a representative. They should be verified by substitution using the earlier action formulas, preserving the order of all factors and the side on which $l_0^\lambda$ acts (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 71–72, 75).

### 3. Inclusion, equality, and the exponent of a procyclic subgroup

**Scan 73, (43) and the surviving calculation below it; scans 74 and 79–80, the multiplier condition. Kind: own idea. Confidence: high as a conditional check; reason: the image of a procyclic generator under a power map is explicit.** The inclusion in (43), rather than an equality silently substituted for it, should be compared with the calculation giving the exponent $2\gamma+1$. If the indicated subgroup is isomorphic to $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, that power map has the entire subgroup as image precisely when the exponent is a unit, so the later requirement $p=2\gamma+1\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{*}$ should be tracked separately from the inclusion. This is a proposed consistency check on the formulation, not a correction to the canceled or surviving calculations (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 73–74, 79–80).

### 4. A condition declared redundant

**Scan 74, final sentence after (46). Kind: unproved claim.** The text says that an earlier condition is “superflue” and “automatiquement vérifiée,” but its handwritten reference remains uncertain between (9) and (7). Locating that exact earlier condition is therefore a prerequisite to proving the claimed redundancy. The proof must then derive it from the stated hypotheses without quietly adding a generation or automorphism assumption (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 74).

### 5. Uniqueness of the normalized lifting

**Scan 75, opening Théorème. Kind: unproved claim.** The theorem says that the exterior automorphism “se relève de façon unique” subject to the stated normalizations. A proof needs both existence of a representative with those normalizations and a determination of the inner automorphisms preserving them; the qualifier inserted after “autom. ext.” is itself a doubtful reading and must be settled before formalizing the theorem. This summary page does not supply that argument afresh (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 75).

### 6. The separate role of topological generation

**Scan 75, b), recalled (40), and the final NB. Kind: unpursued implication.** The requirement that $\sigma_\infty$ and $g\rho$ “engendrent top.” is stated separately from the three-factor relation. A reconstruction should accordingly distinguish preservation of a presentation, continuity of the resulting map, and the step that makes the map an automorphism. In particular, the exact structural hypothesis converting topological generation into the advertised automorphism conclusion should be made explicit (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 75).

### 7. The canceled corollary and its parameter relation

**Scan 76, canceled Corollaire, references (18), (21), and (38), and the adjacent lower margin. Kind: unproved claim in a canceled draft.** The corollary asserts an equivalence through “il f. et s.” and ends with “où nécessairement $\alpha=\beta+\gamma$”; the adjacent margin appears to assert that the parameters are uniquely determined. The whole corollary is crossed out, and its inserted commuting qualifier is uncertain between “extérieurement” and “strictement,” so it must be treated as an abandoned formulation, not cited as an accepted theorem. Verification would require resolving that qualifier and checking the equivalence, the exponent relation, and parameter uniqueness separately against the earlier definitions (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 76).

### 8. Freeness of the displayed twisted action

**Scan 77, (53)–(54) and the lower-right NB. Kind: unproved claim.** The note says that “$\lambda\mapsto{}^\lambda\xi$ est injectif” for the displayed action. A proof must show that a stabilizing element is trivial; under the displayed conjugation interpretation, this amounts to identifying the intersection of the kernel group with the centralizer of $\xi\rho$. The action formula is supplied, but that centralizer argument is not supplied on this page (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 77).

### 9. A nonabelian cocycle formulation

**Scan 77, (51)–(54). Kind: own idea. Confidence: high as a proposed formulation, not as a theorem about these groups; reason: both the norm equation and the twisted action are explicitly displayed.** The equation $\xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1$ and the transformation $\xi\mapsto\lambda\xi\rho(\lambda)^{-1}$ suggest organizing the solutions as nonabelian cocycles modulo their usual equivalence. Before identifying the orbit set with a continuous $H^1$ set, one must verify the precise acting group, its action and topology, and the convention relating cocycles to lifts of the quotient generator (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 77).

### 10. The expressly provisional two-class classification

**Scan 78, opening paragraph. Kind: conjecture / explicit provisional assumption.** Grothendieck writes “Admettons (quitte à le vérifier par la suite)” before asserting exactly two conjugacy classes. The subsequent representatives and formulas therefore rest on an assumption explicitly left for later verification in this passage. A proof needs both exhaustion of the classes and their distinction in the stated profinite setting; a classification in a discrete group would not by itself settle that task (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 78).

### 11. Comparing the two proposed orbit formulas

**Scan 78, (55)–(56) and the bracketed calculation following (56). Kind: unpursued implication.** Conditional on the preceding classification, the page describes the solutions by two formulas “de la forme” involving a twisted conjugation. The calculation moves between representatives involving $l_1^{-1}$ and $l_0^{-1}$, making it useful to check the exact conjugating element and whether the resulting two families are disjoint. That comparison must retain the source's uncertain small indices and canceled calculation rather than using the proposed classification to resolve their transcription (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 78).

### 12. Uniqueness for the equation defining $g_0$

**Scan 79, paragraph after (58) and left margin. Kind: unproved claim.** For fixed $h_0$, the text states that there is “au plus un seul $g_0$,” and the margin records $\widehat{\Pi}_{0,3}^{\sigma_\infty}=\{1\}$. If two solutions of $\sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1}g_0=h_0$ exist, their quotient is fixed by $\sigma_\infty$, so the marginal fixed-subgroup assertion gives the advertised uniqueness once that assertion is established. This concerns uniqueness only and does not establish existence (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 79).

### 13. Existence requires an additional norm-to-coboundary argument

**Scan 79, (58)–(59). Kind: unproved claim.** The same paragraph says that such a $g_0$ “existe ssi” the displayed norm-one condition holds. Necessity can be checked directly from the defining equation and the involution, whereas sufficiency requires every element satisfying the norm condition to arise as $\sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1}g_0$. That is an additional assertion, not a consequence of the trivial fixed subgroup used for uniqueness, and no proof of it is given on this page (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 79).

### 14. Uniqueness of the profinite exponent

**Scan 79, Corollaire following (60). Kind: unproved claim.** For fixed $\lambda$, and hence fixed $\xi$, the text asserts “il existe au plus un $\gamma$” satisfying $\sigma_\infty(\xi)=l_1^\gamma\xi^{-1}l_0^\gamma$. Proving this requires an explicit property of the two indicated procyclic subgroups or a suitable quotient calculation in which their images are known. The assertion should be kept distinct from the existence question: the page does not say that every prescribed $\lambda$ admits such an exponent (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 79).

### 15. Testing the inverse-multiplier notation

**Scan 79, last parenthesis. Kind: own idea. Confidence: high for the algebra and low for the doubtful asterisk in the handwriting; reason: the proposed inverse relation can be expanded directly.** The identity $(2\gamma+1)(2\gamma'+1)-1=2(2\gamma\gamma'+\gamma+\gamma')$ provides a direct check on the last displayed relation. In particular, the case $\gamma=0$ forces $\gamma'=0$ in the displayed equation $2\gamma\gamma'+\gamma+\gamma'=0$, so a possible extra unit requirement on $\gamma'$ itself deserves checking separately from the unit requirement on $2\gamma+1$. This diagnostic does not alter the explicitly doubtful transcription of the superscript (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 79).

### 16. Descent to a left-coset parameter

**Scan 80, opening NB. Kind: unpursued implication.** The substitution “$\lambda'=l_0^\alpha\lambda$” is accompanied by formulas for the corresponding changes of $\xi$, $h_0$, and $g_0$, and a statement that (60) remains equivalent. These formulas provide the mechanism for the left-coset parameter appearing in the preceding corollary. Checking the descent means verifying all the transformations with their stated sides of multiplication, including the earlier right-coset freedom of $g_0$, rather than identifying the two quotient conventions by notation alone (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 79–80).

### 17. What remains in the final parametrization procedure

**Scan 80, steps 1°–2° and (A)–(C). Kind: unproved claim / proposed parametrization.** The text calls the procedure “la démarche la plus claire”: choose a solution of (A), then require an exponent satisfying (C) and the unit condition on $2\gamma+1$. The selection ends with restrictions on which candidates are retained, rather than a criterion deciding their existence for every initial candidate. Completing the argument would require identifying the admissible candidates and establishing that reconstruction has every automorphism property asserted earlier (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 80).

### 18. Finite-quotient obstruction tests

**Scan 80, (A)–(C). Kind: own idea. Confidence: medium as a research strategy; reason: the two displayed equations can be pushed to finite quotients while keeping factor order.** One could first test the order-three norm equation and the involution-compatibility equation in finite quotients on which the relevant actions descend, retaining the same candidate data under transition maps. A failed finite test would obstruct that proposed candidate, but successful finite tests alone would not prove a coherent profinite solution, uniqueness, or the final automorphism assertion. This is a suggested diagnostic construction, not a claimed result (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 80).

### Reference

Grothendieck, A. (1981). *La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois* [Unpublished manuscript; Montpellier archive, cote 140-3, pages 293–650; supplied extract LM_P066, scans 71–80].

# LM_P070-071 — cote 140-3, scans 111–130  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_P070-071\LM_P070-071_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English

These notes are separate from the transcription. The source for manuscript statements is Grothendieck (1981), at the scan and location specified in each item. “Conjecture” is used as the requested category for explicit questions, expectations and doubts as well as conjectural statements; where the question is answered locally, that is stated. “Unproved claim” means that a proof or a necessary verification is not spelled out in the cited passage, not that no proof exists elsewhere in the manuscript or literature. Cancelled expectations are identified as cancelled.

The items labelled **Own idea** are suggestions for investigation, with confidence and reasons. They are not claimed to be established, original, or new. No survey of later manuscript material or of the external literature has been used to settle their status. Textual uncertainties constrain the mathematical interpretation throughout.

### R01. Scan 111 — Unproved claim

**Location:** item 2°, c. lines 9–18.

**Manuscript wording:** « peuvent varier d’un ℓ à un autre »; « 2, 1 et 0 paramètres »

The local cases are said to vary with the prime, and the three families are assigned parameter counts two, one and zero. On this sheet the justification is deferred to (86), outside this supplied range; checking it would require identifying the ambient coefficient rings and the parameter identifications in that earlier calculation. The ring after the local choice is visibly written with a hat over Z and is retained that way in the transcription.

### R02. Scan 111 — Conjecture

**Location:** item 3°, c. lines 19–25.

**Manuscript wording:** « J’ignore si »; « Je l’ignore … si on suppose g≡id (2) »

This is an explicit unresolved question, not an asserted conjectural theorem: does every indicated norm-one solution admit one of the written parametric forms? He says the uncertainty remains under the congruence-to-identity condition modulo 2 and suggests considering the local components separately. The precise group superscript and the second factor in the proposed parametrization are doubtful, so a mathematical reformulation must first resolve those readings.

### R03. Scan 112 — Conjecture

**Location:** cancelled paragraph, c. lines 6–11.

**Manuscript wording:** « Je présume »; « on sera dans le cas B) »

The cancelled passage predicts that the second parametrization belongs to case B and again has two parameters; it must be treated as a cancelled expectation, not as an active conclusion. A marginal « OK, cf. (…) ci-dessous » points to a later calculation, with the reference tentatively read as (99). Its relation to scans 116–117 deserves checking while preserving the lower-case c+d−b written in the cancelled sentence.

### R04. Scan 112 — Unpursued implication

**Location:** last paragraph and displayed matrix.

**Manuscript wording:** « Sans pouvoir néanmoins exclure le cas »

The surviving reservation introduces A+B=0 and a one-parameter matrix involving a primitive cube root. The exceptional family should be checked independently against the determinant and norm equations, particularly in the coefficient rings intended on the preceding page. The ordinal spelling and the word before paramètre are uncertain; no classification is established by this note.

### R05. Scan 113 — Own idea

**Location:** (*) and the subsequent (**).

The displayed reduction of the order-two norm equation to symmetry of h₀ suggests studying the solution set as symmetric determinant-one matrices, then testing how the later quotient by signs changes that description. This is a possible way to organize a verification of the written calculations; it is not a replacement for their entries, including the uncertain sign in (90).

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** The equivalence in (*) is explicit; how much of the desired parametrization survives the quotient and lift conditions still needs proof.

### R06. Scan 114 — Unpursued implication

**Location:** parenthesis following (93).

**Manuscript wording:** « mais le signe − impliquerait »

The page uses the diagonal entry and its congruence modulo 2 to exclude the negative symmetry sign for the lifts under consideration. It would be useful to isolate the precise lifting hypothesis under which this exclusion works, and to compare what happens when that hypothesis is removed. The overwritten name of the congruence subgroup is not securely read, so the subgroup should not be identified solely from this note.

### R07. Scan 115 — Unpursued implication

**Location:** (96)–(97) and the matrix-lift paragraph.

**Manuscript wording:** « le multiplicateur p s’obtient »; « ambiguïté de signe »

The multiplier is recovered as the inverse of the lower-right matrix entry after the stated choice of sign. The page also argues that changing the sign of the chosen parameter matrix does not change its twisted coboundary. A further check should separate this sign invariance from independence under other choices of the parameter; the latter is not supplied merely by the sign calculation.

### R08. Scan 115 — Own idea

**Location:** quadratic form in (96)–(97) and last paragraph.

One possible route to the later local representability question is the identity c²+cd+d²=(c−dω)(c−dω²) when ω²+ω+1=0. ## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

The source locators below refer to Grothendieck (1981), with the bibliography and limits of attribution given at the end. Authorial questions, assertions without a proof in the indicated passage, unpursued implications, and editorial proposals are labeled separately. A statement may be addressed elsewhere in the manuscript. None of these notes changes a reading in the LaTeX fragment.

The manuscript says, “Nous admettrons … que ces faits …” extend to elements of the profinite group. The criterion “il f. et s. que $\varepsilon'=0$” selects the positive subgroup among the choices in (41). The required check is the image of each ambiguity generator under the sign/orientation character; that computation is not given on this nearly blank page (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 132).

This is suggested by the reduction to a central sign, but no computation here has been performed and a finite test would not by itself establish the profinite claim (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 147).

### R38. Scan 148, opening paragraph — conjecture/question

The equivalence with the norm-one equation is explicitly followed by “que nous laissons en suspens pour le moment.” The positive-sign issue therefore remains open at this point, despite the subsequent table of formulas (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 148).

### R39. Scan 148, (45) — unproved claim

The displayed summary simultaneously records the corrective sign in the relation for the descending cocycle variable and in the threefold product of g. A verification should track the chosen lifts and the determinant restrictions inserted above the system, rather than assume that “signes arbitraires” makes every later identity sign-free (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 148).

### R40. Scan 148, left-margin note — unpursued implication

The legible opening proposes that it would be “plus pratique de définir g” by an alpha-coboundary so that the threefold product is one. This appears to relocate the corrective sign into another formula, but the note's closing clause is insufficiently legible to assert its full intended scope (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 148).

### R41. Scan 148, (46) — own idea (confidence: low)

A comparison of the proposed symmetric case with (45) could clarify which determinant and sign conditions survive interchange of the two actions. This is motivated by “De façon symétrique,” but the final equality is unfinished and the psi-definition has a doubtful first factor, so the missing calculation is not supplied here (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 148).

### R42. Scan 149, upper-left margin — unproved claim

In the “arithmétique” case the author states that alpha-zero and f are congruent to one modulo two and lists the resulting entrywise congruences. A proof would need the exact maps from the two indicated profinite groups to the matrix group and should preserve the distinction between the two groups rather than identify them from their congruence images alone (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 149).

### R43. Scan 149, upper-right margin — unproved claim

The note calls the change of signs in alpha-zero and f “inessentiel” (the word is not wholly secure). It invites an explicit verification of which coordinate expressions and compatibility relations are unchanged by each sign choice; the short stroke before f remains a transcription doubt (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 149).

### R44. Scan 149, (50)–(56) — unpursued implication

The author passes from group expressions to formulas in eight matrix entries and identifies the essential relation as the “relation du lacet.” This suggests a coordinate formulation over the profinite integers with determinant and parity restrictions, but the displayed sign epsilon still has to be tracked rather than absorbed by changing representatives (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 149).

### R45. Scan 149, (53)–(55) — unproved claim

“On aura les formules” introduces two displayed relations among matrix entries, of which S=T is legible and the operation between D and B in (54) is overwritten. A verification should begin by resolving that textual uncertainty or carry both candidate signs separately; the surrounding algebra should not be used to choose the transcription (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 149).

### R46. Scan 149, (48) and (52) — own idea (confidence: high as a textual observation; medium as a proposed check)

Equation (48) visibly reads ab-cd, despite the matrix placement of a,b,c,d in (47). A formal comparison of the literal polynomial identities could document where the subsequent relations depend on that written condition; this would be an editorial consistency check, not permission to replace it by the usual determinant expression in the transcription (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 149).

### Additional proposals arising from the combined reading

These are editorial proposals, not claims by Grothendieck, established results, or claims of novelty. They have not been used to alter the transcription.

1. **Scans 137–144, the two coboundary parametrizations and their changes of representative — own idea. Confidence: medium.** Define the two equivalence relations directly from the written transformations, one using the order-two action and the other the order-three action, and ask whether the compatibility formula describes a common set of orbits. Reason: the manuscript explicitly changes representatives and then specializes to `h=1` or `g=1`, but the uniqueness statements, the enlarged group allowed for alpha, and the left-coset ambiguity of f must all be accounted for before such an orbit description can be asserted (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 137–144).

2. **Scans 145–147, quotient lifts and the corrective sign — own idea. Confidence: medium.** Audit exactly which central subgroup is meant by the written quotient by `±1`, and test whether independent sign choices in reductions modulo coprime integers can occur among the permitted lifts. Reason: the later argument tracks one scalar sign, while the earlier notation passes between a completion of an integral group and a group of matrices over the profinite integers; an argument must state the image restrictions before treating all matrix lifts as equivalent (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 145–147).

3. **Scans 148–149, the component formulas and the revised convention for g — own idea. Confidence: medium.** Make two separately labeled symbolic checks: first use the formulas exactly as written, and then, in a separate exploratory calculation, test candidate readings of the doubtful signs and missing superscripts. Reason: the margin changes where the sign is carried, while the final scan contains the visible order `ab-cd` in (48); conflating a proposed intended identity with the diplomatic text would conceal which assumption makes a calculation work (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 148–149).

# LM_C3-150-168 — cote 140-3, scans 150–168  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_C3-150-168\LM_C3-150-168_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

These notes concern the supplied extract of Grothendieck (1981). Each scan and equation reference below is a locator in that primary source. Quotations are brief readings of the supplied handwriting; an unresolved reading is not promoted to established evidence. “Conjecture / expectation” includes working hopes and doubts that may be resolved elsewhere, including on a later supplied scan. “Unproved claim” means that a proof is not supplied at the cited location; it does not assert that the claim is unproved in the rest of the manuscript or the literature. Items labelled **own idea** are proposed checks or directions, with confidence and reasons, not claims of novelty or established results. No literature review is claimed.

### Scans 150–154

1. **Scan 151, paragraph following (62); kind: unproved claim / expectation.** Grothendieck writes “on doit pouvoir vérifier” that the scheme of solutions has relative dimension 3 and relative dimension 1 over either displayed factor; the margin says “non, il est de dim. rel totale 4.” A proof would need an exact independent equation set, a statement of the base and the projection under consideration, and an analysis of fibres, rather than merely subtracting the number of displayed equations from the number of variables. The marginal correction should be checked against subsequent discussion, without deleting the earlier claim from the diplomatic text.

2. **Scan 151, margin beside (61)–(62); kind: unproved claim.** The note says that the last relation is “conséquence des autres,” taking account of `C+D-B=1` and `AD-BC=1`; the last polynomial relation is likewise marked as a consequence. To validate the implication over the intended coefficient ring, one should make explicit where the invertibility derived from `\mu D=1` enters the elimination. This is especially relevant to the dimension count in the following paragraph.

3. **Scan 152, upper left margin; kind: conjecture / expectation.** “Ce serait le moment d'inclure … la relation `\mu\equiv\delta\ (3)`” records a proposed expository addition, not a new conjectural equality. Its suggested demonstration is only partly legible in the margin; the central text supplies the analogous calculation later on the same scan. The relation and the location of the proposed insertion are worth checking against the manuscript's later revisions.

4. **Scan 152, paragraph introducing the quadratic characters and (63); kind: own idea. Confidence: high for the elementary diagnostic, limited for the author's intended convention.** The literal square criterion at the prime 2 should be compared carefully with the mod-4 sign characterized in the preceding paragraph: `5` is `1` modulo 4 but cannot be a square modulo 8. Thus a direct identification of the sign in (63) with the indicator of membership in `(\mathbb Z_2^*)^2` requires clarification of the intended character or additional hypotheses. This is a research/checking note only; the transcription retains the written criterion.

5. **Scan 152, last paragraph and (63); kind: unpursued implication.** The words “la connaissance de … équivaut à celle de `\mu` mod …” connect the two signs with small-modulus data, while the adjacent margin displays the product of unit groups modulo 4 and 3. A useful later check is whether the combined mod-12 datum is used merely to determine the two signs or to impose stronger conditions on the admissible multipliers. The first modulus in the final prose line is visually uncertain and should not be treated as settled evidence until the image is re-examined.

6. **Scan 153, (65) and the paragraph below it; kind: unpursued implication.** Grothendieck remarks that “`g` s'exprime simplement en termes de `f`,” whereas expressing `\alpha` requires both sets of variables. The displayed matrix (65) appears to depend only on `t,u,\mu`, so the effect of changing the top row of `f` is worth making explicit. Any proposed invariance must be checked using the manuscript's precise change-of-choice convention and admissibility equations.

7. **Scan 153, left marginal note; kind: unproved claim.** The clearly readable part asserts that the relevant quantity is “déterminé sans ambiguïté (au signe près)” by an automorphism, while contrasting it with the choices entering `f`. A proof would have to specify the equivalence relations on the lifts and verify which quantities survive the change `f\mapsto l_0^n f`. Because several words in the final portion of this margin remain illegible, this note deliberately does not reconstruct a complete formal statement from it.

8. **Scan 154, (68 bis)–(69); kind: unpursued implication.** Applying `x\mapsto x\rho(x)\rho^2(x)` to the twisted commutator fixes the second sign, and the remaining equation is rewritten as `u=\alpha u_0` with `[u_0,\rho]=1`. This suggests organizing the remaining choices as a coset of a centralizer and then imposing the other conjugacy and determinant equations. The note concerns the structure made visible by the displayed calculations, not a claim that all remaining compatibility conditions have been solved here.

9. **Scan 154, paragraph below (69); kind: unproved claim recalled from earlier work.** “Nous avons déjà remarqué” introduces the assertion that the two conjugacy equations determine `u` up to an invertible scalar, with the determinant reducing the residual ambiguity to `\lambda^2=1`. The local proof is not repeated on this scan; it would require determining the simultaneous centralizer of the relevant matrices over `\widehat{\mathbb Z}` and checking possible exceptional components. The statement may have been justified on earlier pages outside this assignment.

10. **Scan 154, same paragraph; kind: conjecture / expectation.** The phrase “on espère néanmoins tomber sur un choix canonique” explicitly leaves open a preferred representative despite the prime-by-prime sign ambiguity. Subsequent formulae should be checked for what exactly canonically determines the representative, and whether the construction remains invariant under the choices in the preceding scans. This expectation is recorded even if a later page resolves it.

11. **Scan 154, (70); kind: own idea. Confidence: high as a direct algebraic check, conditional on the uncertain identity glyph.** The matrix family in (70) can be tested directly as the commutant of the displayed `\rho` by writing a general 2×2 matrix and comparing the four entries of the products. After resolving the overwritten identity symbol, its determinant also provides a concrete quadratic expression with which to check the subsequent norm-like formulae. This is a proposed verification of the written calculation, not an emendation of (70).

### Scans 155–159

All manuscript observations and quotations below refer to the supplied images of Grothendieck (1981), using filename scan numbers. A “conjecture” label includes the author's working expectations and doubts, including ones reconsidered within the next page; it does not assert that a question remains open elsewhere in the manuscript.

1. **Scan 155, paragraph after (73); kind: conjecture / working expectation.** Grothendieck recalls “de subodorer que l'on devrait avoir ε′ = +1 ssi p ≡ 1 (4)” after finding that an earlier universal positive-sign conclusion was not compatible “avec le corps des classes”. A careful study would have to identify the role of p and the relevant class-field-theoretic condition from the preceding context rather than assume that the symbol denotes an arbitrary prime.

2. **Scan 155, right annotation to (74); kind: conjecture / working expectation.** The brief note “sans doute, ε₂ = 1” connects the commuting case to the sign determined by μ. The following scans develop this distinction, so this is a record of the author's intermediate expectation rather than an independently unresolved claim.

3. **Scan 155, (71)–(73); kind: own idea. Confidence: medium.** The repeated expressions $p^2+pq+q^2$ and $c^2+cd+d^2$, with reciprocal μ factors, invite a norm-based organization of these calculations. One could test this by working directly in the two-dimensional algebra generated by the displayed ρ and computing the determinant of $c\rho+d$; the reason for the suggestion is the explicit recurrence of the same quadratic polynomial, not an appeal to an external identification.

4. **Scan 156, left margin beside the commutator calculation; kind: unpursued implication.** The note “On pourrait aussi appliquer les formules §43 (78)” points to an alternative calculation. Comparing that cited formula with the present expansion would require the actual earlier section, which is not supplied in this five-scan segment.

5. **Scan 156, final paragraph; kind: conjecture / working expectation.** Grothendieck wants to “trouver ‘au pif’ une expression” when ε₂ = −1 and says “je prévois que la matrice” involving τ∞ will work. Scan 157 tests this expectation, encounters a sign problem, and changes the placement of τ∞; both the failed trial and the repair should be kept when studying the argument.

6. **Scan 157, from the tentative commutator to t replaced by −t; kind: unpursued implication.** The trial equality leads to “2μut = 0”, followed by “décidément, ça déconne !”, and the next step replaces t by −t. This passage is suitable for a separate reconstruction of the sequence of sign conventions, with each intermediate matrix checked independently, because collapsing the calculation to its eventual answer would conceal why the left and right placements of the reflection matter.

7. **Scan 158, (75)–(78); kind: own idea. Confidence: high that a check is needed, not that a particular correction is established.** Recompute (77) in both ε₂ cases directly from (75), keeping the group commutator and the conjugation notation distinct. The reason is visible on the page: the left formula has $-\varepsilon_2\mathrm{id}$, whereas its adjacent “i.e.” statement has $+\varepsilon_2\sigma_\infty$; the diplomatic transcription deliberately leaves this discrepancy intact.

8. **Scan 158, corollary; kind: unproved claim in the local text.** The corollary says that the action “passe en une action dans le quotient” and is induced by an automorphism of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\widehat{\mathbb Z})$ defined by a matrix of determinant μ. A full proof of descent needs to establish preservation of the kernel of the relevant quotient map and the agreement of the induced action with the displayed conjugation; the preceding two-by-two computations alone do not explicitly state those steps on this page.

9. **Scan 159, upper-left margin; kind: unproved claim.** The margin says one is “ramené au cas où u commute à σ∞”, “quitte à conjuguer” by an inner automorphism; the end of the note is not fully legible. The corresponding reduction would need an explicit normalizing conjugation and a check that the hypotheses and multiplier used in the corollary survive it.

10. **Scan 159, second left marginal note; kind: unpursued implication.** “On a fait ceci, pour le moment, pour u commutant à σ∞” limits the scope of the calculation performed. This should be compared with the preceding corollary's exterior-commutation hypothesis before treating the passage as a proof for every representative.

11. **Scan 159, inserted “modulo signe” and (79); kind: unpursued implication.** The promised construction “canoniquement”, qualified by inserted “modulo signe”, rests on the fact that left multiplication by $\ell_0^n$ leaves the lower row (t,u) unchanged. To formalize the claim one should specify the quotient of choices for f, the remaining simultaneous sign ambiguity, and why no other ambiguity from the original automorphism remains.

12. **Scan 159, last paragraph; kind: own idea. Confidence: medium.** The analogous invariance of (c,d) suggests comparing the two lower-row expressions $t\sigma_\infty+u$ and $c\rho+d$ as parallel descriptions of the same action. The reason is the explicit transition from the f calculation to α₀ and then to $c\rho+d$; this is a proposed organization for further reading, not a claim of a new relation or a relation proved on this page.

### Scans 160–164

These are source-based working questions, not claims of established results or novelty. Formula readings carrying doubt marks remain provisional; the quoted words below are brief and only support the particular note. References identify the supplied scans, independently of the footer numbering.

1. **Scan160, (80) and following two lines — conjecture / question.** The question mark over the equality in (80) and “peut-être de corriger par un facteur” record a provisional comparison of the conjugating matrix with `\mu\alpha(c\rho+d)`. The marginal correction points to the factor `\delta=\varepsilon_3`, and scan161 subsequently writes it in (82), so the question is locally pursued rather than simply abandoned. A study of the derivation should keep the original question and the later scalar correction as distinct stages (Grothendieck, 1981, scans160–161, eqs. 80–82).

2. **Scan161, (83)–(84) — unpursued implication.** The reformulation culminates in `\varepsilon_2U=D` and `\varepsilon_2T=C`, called the “contenu essentiel” in the provisional reading of the accompanying sentence. This invites a precise comparison between the conjugating-matrix expression and the two scalar compatibility conditions, including an account of why the other matrix entries are redundant under the determinant relations. The dependence on the legibility of “contenu” is editorial, whereas the two displayed scalar identities are clear (Grothendieck, 1981, scan161, eqs. 83–84).

3. **Scans161–162, Remarque and opening continuation — conjecture / expectation.** “Sans doute sous des conditions beaucoup plus générales” expresses the expectation that the calculation is valid in a broader setting of matrix groups over arbitrary rings. The text then introduces fixed `\rho,\sigma`, a scalar, and a one-parameter subgroup rather than restricting itself to the original profinite situation. A proof must specify the base ring, determinant constraints, and invertibility assumptions instead of assuming that every displayed division remains valid (Grothendieck, 1981, scans161–162).

4. **Scan162, final paragraph — conjecture / expectation.** “Devraient pouvoir se développer” and the inserted “compléments substantiels” explicitly leave a more general treatment for possible later work. The closing admission “je ne sais si je vais expliciter” should be tracked against the continuation of the manuscript rather than treated as a promise of a completed argument. This note records both the expectation and the author's hesitation (Grothendieck, 1981, scan162, final paragraph).

5. **Scan162, (*) — own idea; confidence: medium.** A useful first reconstruction would define the solution functor of (*) with the determinant conditions stated explicitly, then ask on which open subsets a commutator equation is equivalent to a conjugacy equation. This is a proposed organizational step, not an asserted description of the manuscript's intended scheme. The reason for medium confidence is that the displayed matrix equation is explicit, but the base and fixed-versus-variable data are not all settled in this remark (Grothendieck, 1981, scan162, eq. *).

6. **Scan163, first paragraph — unproved claim.** The phrase “schéma relatif lisse de dim relative 4” proposes smoothness and a dimension for the scheme of solutions of (*), with `f,\alpha_0,\mu` variable. No proof is supplied at that point in these pages, and the base of the relative statement and the determinant restrictions must be identified before a Jacobian or deformation calculation can check it. The claim should therefore be examined in the general-ring framework of the preceding remark, not merely by counting displayed variables (Grothendieck, 1981, scans162–163).

7. **Scan163, first paragraph and (85) — own idea; confidence: medium.** A targeted test of the proposed smoothness would examine the relevant Jacobian in residue characteristics 2 and 3 before extrapolating from characteristic zero. The reason is that differentiating the visible quadratic expressions `t^2+u^2` and `c^2+cd+d^2` changes their behavior in these characteristics. This is a suggested check only; it does not assert that the stated solution scheme fails to be smooth (Grothendieck, 1981, scan163).

8. **Scan163, Proposition and (85) — unproved claim / proof obligation.** The proposition asserts a necessary and sufficient condition on the two lower rows through the equality, up to sign, of their quadratic expressions as units. A proof has to complete both lower rows to matrices satisfying the stated determinants and the compatibility relation, and then identify the freedom left in the upper rows. Scan164 begins this reconstruction, but its first detailed construction of the auxiliary matrix is crossed out, so canceled calculations should not be counted automatically as the final proof (Grothendieck, 1981, scans163–164, eqs. 85–88).

9. **Scan163, revised paragraph between (85) and (86) — own idea; confidence: medium.** Audit the intended sign involution before formalizing the parameter space: the inserted tuple contains `2\nu+1`, whereas the surviving displayed negation ends in `-\nu`. If the sign reversal is meant to send `\mu=2\nu+1` to `-\mu`, elementary algebra instead sends `\nu` to `-\nu-1`. This is an editorial hypothesis to be checked against later pages; the multiple revision layers prevent a confident statement of the intended correction, and the transcription preserves the ink (Grothendieck, 1981, scan163).

10. **Scan163, (86) — own idea; confidence: medium.** Compare the surviving `c^2+cd+u^2` in (86) with the preceding `c^2+cd+d^2` in (85) before deriving consequences from the proposition. The visible mismatch may be an unrevised intermediate slip, but the reason for checking it is the different last variable on the same page, not an assumption that the formulas must already be consistent. No correction has been made in the transcription (Grothendieck, 1981, scan163, eqs. 85–86).

11. **Scan164, existence assertion preceding (87) — unproved claim.** “Il y en a toujours” asserts existence of `r,s` with `ur-ts=1`, but the written parenthetical explanation invokes `r^2+s^2` and the components `r_p,s_p`. The variable scope therefore needs verification in any reconstructed proof: the available data of the proposition are the fixed lower-row entries. The statement and its written explanation should be distinguished (Grothendieck, 1981, scan164, upper half).

12. **Scan164, (87) — own idea; confidence: high, conditional on the unit hypothesis.** For fixed `t,u` with `q=t^2+u^2` invertible, the concrete choices `r_0=u/q` and `s_0=-t/q` satisfy `ur_0-ts_0=1`. One can then check directly the proposed affine family in the direction `(t,u)` and determine whether it gives every completion over the stated ring. This construction is elementary and motivated by the page, not claimed as new; it is kept in the notes and has not been used to choose the overwritten signs in (87) (Grothendieck, 1981, scans163–164).

13. **Scan164, canceled block containing (88) — unpursued implication.** The deleted calculation defines `A` using `(1+BC)/D` and reduces the remaining compatibility to the upper-left corner relation, described as the “coin sup. gauche.” It is worth determining why this route was abandoned and whether its reduction remains valid after the hypotheses are made explicit. The page itself does not state a reason for the cancellation, so the crossed-out argument is evidence of an attempted approach rather than an accepted conclusion (Grothendieck, 1981, scan164, canceled eq. 88 and following lines).

### Scan 165

- **Scan 165, after (88); unproved claim.** The determinant is said to be a unit, « ce qui assure une solution unique ! ». A verification should calculate the determinant of the displayed coefficient matrix with its written signs and recover the stated quadratic form, then use invertibility over the profinite coefficient ring.
- **Scan 165, middle; unpursued implication.** The preference to « partir du multiplicateur μ » suggests organizing the solutions by the multiplier and the two bottom rows. The isolated congruence `μ ≡ ε₂ (2)` needs comparison with the earlier and later congruences; modulo 2 alone cannot distinguish the two integer signs, and the transcription deliberately preserves the written modulus.
- **Scan 165, lower paragraph; conjecture / expectation.** Grothendieck says the pairs « dépendent de 1 paramètre » in a sense one could « préciser si on y tenait », with explicit parameters `σ,τ`. Making this precise would require specifying the parameter spaces and whether the parametrizations are global, local, or torsor descriptions, particularly at primes where the quadratic forms behave differently.

### Scan 166

- **Scan 166, (89) and following paragraph; unproved claim.** The system is said to have « rang 3 », and its solutions form an « espace affine de dim 1 » over `Ẑ`. A complete formulation over this ring should exhibit a split surjective coefficient map, identify its rank-one kernel, and establish that the affine fibre is nonempty.

The ensuing congruence computation is only part of the task: one should distinguish necessity, sufficiency for matrix lifting, and lifting to the original profinite groups.

This would make the claimed affine parameter and its reduction modulo 2 directly comparable with the additive action on scan 168; this is a proposed verification, not a claim that the manuscript has already supplied all steps.

### Scan 167

- **Scan 167, (90); unpursued implication.** The statement that `c mod 4` and the determinant sign determine the other sign is an explicit compression of the sign data: « permet de trouver le signe ε₂ ». It would be useful to track how this condition interacts with all the earlier independent sign choices, rather than assuming that the two signs remain free after congruences are imposed.

This isolates which part is formal from which part still depends on the matrix equations and their nonempty solution set.

### Scan 168

- **Scan 168, action formula labelled uncertain (93)/(94), and its following paragraph; unproved claim.** The displayed additive action is identified, up to the factor 2, with the ambiguity of solutions when the four bottom-row entries are fixed: « c'est justement l'indétermination ». A proof should verify preservation of (93) and compare its orbits with the full affine solution fibres, including the added mod-2 conditions.

The precise equivalence relation on these quantities, particularly the surviving signs and the prime in the group notation, deserves an explicit invariant formulation before treating them as canonical coordinates.

This might be an uncorrected slip or might depend on a specialization not visible here; the original subscript remains unchanged in the transcription.

The proposed normalization and its compatibility with the intrinsic data should be checked at that earlier reference and in the continuation; the current extract ends before the reservation beginning « mais il me semble peu rationnel » is completed.

# LM_C3-169-187 — cote 140-3, scans 169–187  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_C3-169-187\LM_C3-169-187_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English

These notes are separate from the transcription. Their source observations refer to the supplied manuscript (Grothendieck, 1981), using scan numbers and, where available, the author's page or equation numbers. “Unproved” means not proved in the cited local passage, not absent from the whole manuscript or later literature. Some questions are taken up on subsequent supplied pages and are still recorded at their first occurrence. “Conjecture” also covers an explicitly stated question, hope, or programme where identified as such; it does not convert an intention into a formal conjecture. Own ideas are proposed checks or investigations, with their confidence and reason, and carry no claim of novelty.

### Scans 169–173

#### R169.1 — Scan 169, lines 1–5 — Unpursued implication

Grothendieck deliberately leaves aside a “possibilité de normalisation” and emphasizes the “rôle joué par les quatre quantités” $c,d,t,u$. A worthwhile local question is what information that normalization would suppress and whether all four quantities can be recovered from the resulting matrix data. The preceding discussion is outside this package, so these lines alone do not determine the normalization or its admissibility (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 169, ms. p. 383).

#### R170.1 — Scan 170, lower body — Conjecture / explicit open problem

He writes, “je n'ai pas de caractérisation bien plausible à proposer” for $\Gamma_{\mathbb Q}$ as a subgroup of $\widetilde\Gamma$. This records a recognition problem rather than an asserted equality with a later named group. Any proposed characterization would have to give intrinsic necessary conditions and address whether they suffice (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 170, ms. p. 384).

#### R170.2 — Scan 170, last paragraph; scan 171, (3) — Unproved claim

The assertion “On a un scindage canonique” is followed by the subgroup defined through commutation with $\sigma_\infty$ and the displayed product decomposition. A proof would need to establish existence and uniqueness of the decomposition and the relevant intersection statement, using the precise automorphism and inner-action conventions. Those supporting details are not supplied in these two passages (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 170–171).

#### R171.1 — Scan 171, (5)–(7) — Unproved claim / dependency

The map is called an “application (continue)” before its homomorphism property is stated on the next scan. Verifying continuity requires the definitions and dependence of the coefficient functions in the previous section; well-definedness also depends on the primed quotient convention. The epsilon-like exponent in (5) should first be checked against the manuscript and those earlier definitions, without altering the diplomatic reading (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 171).

#### R172.1 — Scan 172, (9) and following paragraph — Unproved claim / prior proof cited

Grothendieck calls (9) “un fait déjà établi” and refers to (67), (68), and the corollary to theorem (77). The present package does not contain those referenced displays, so its proof is locally conditional on recovering their exact conjugation convention and hypotheses. This is not a claim that the full manuscript lacks a proof (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 172, ms. p. 385).

#### R172.2 — Scan 172, (10); scan 173, (11)–(12) — Unpursued implication

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

These are questions for further work, with source-local evidence and explicit limits. “Unproved claim” means that the indicated passage does not itself supply the full argument; references or later pages may supply it. “Unpursued implication” concerns an avenue not developed at that point, even when it is taken up later in this supplied extract. Items labelled **own idea** are proposals for investigation, with confidence and reasons, and make no claim of novelty or established truth. Paleographic uncertainties are not resolved by any of these suggestions.

1. **Scan 188, opening paragraph and (31)–(32). Kind: unproved claim.** The assertion “correspondance biunivoque” identifies pairs satisfying the earlier conditions (25) with pairs of coboundary representatives. Verifying the assertion requires the precise hypotheses of (25), an existence argument for the representatives in the indicated groups, and a check of their allowed ambiguity; those hypotheses are outside these five pages.

2. **Scan 188, paragraph after (34). Kind: unproved claim.** Grothendieck writes that ν is “uniquement déterminé” by α₀,β₀ through the possibility of finding f. A proof would need to exclude two different powers of the displayed lacet that admit the required relation for the same pair, taking account of the allowed left multiplication of f.

3. **Scan 189, left marginal note beside (36). Kind: unproved claim.** The note calls the ambiguity an “inconvénient mineur” and appears to promise that it will be removed “plus bas”; the final phrase is paleographically doubtful. What needs clarification is whether a later construction chooses representatives, or instead replaces the parameters by an invariant of the indicated simultaneous left action.

The necessity of those identities can be investigated by multiplying the defining coboundaries, but the converse requires a separate existence statement and a treatment of fibers of the two coboundary maps; the displayed norm identities alone do not explain those points.

The reduced dependence on the image of ξ, and the role of the sign determined by the cubic relation, deserve a separate proof; the precise quotient notation in the margin remains uncertain. A proof should specify whether it concerns an actual matrix, a class modulo ±1, or both.

28. **Scan 199, (78) and margin — unpursued implication.** The triangular expression « (μ, μB; 0, 1) » suggests that the information retained in u_{αβ} can be studied through the entries B and D, with μD=1. The margin itself points toward this reduction. These pages do not yet describe the image, fibres, or resulting composition law in these reduced coordinates.

29. **Scan 200, margin beside (80) — unproved claim.** The note begins « ceci implique que » and compares conjugation by u_{α,β,f} with the effect of an automorphism u after taking a quotient. The qualification « quand il y en a un » is significant: the marginal claim does not assert existence of such an automorphism for every matrix triple. A proof would require the exact source group and quotient morphism, whose notation in this margin is uncertain in the present scan.

30. **Scan 200, (80)–(83) — unpursued implication.** Grothendieck completes the two conjugation identities « de façon naturelle » with the ε₀ identity (82), then removes f to obtain (83). The calculation begun here and continued on the next scan makes the sign ε part of the compatibility with the product σ∞ρ. It would be useful to isolate exactly which identities hold for a matrix lift and which survive only after quotienting by the central sign.

31. **Scan 201, Remarque — unpursued implication.** The remark says « sans ambiguïté de signes » once α, β and f are chosen, and distinguishes changing the signs of α or β from changing the sign of f. This separates invariance of conjugation identities from dependence of an actual matrix representative on a central sign. The distinction is relevant to any subsequent attempt to package the data into a canonical object rather than a choice of lift.

32. **Scan 201, Remarque — own idea.** One can record the independent sign changes as a small central action on the triples (α,β,f) and check directly which expressions descend to the quotient. **Confidence: high as a finite algebraic check**, because the remark supplies the claimed effects and the scalar −1 is central. Such a check would clarify the bookkeeping without implying that every matrix triple comes from a manuscript automorphism.

33. **Scan 202, (84)–(87) — unpursued implication.** The calculation establishes that the simultaneous left changes of α, β and f preserve u_{α,β,f}; the text says « vérifier avec (79) que » before (87). Thus this expression is insensitive to at least the displayed family of choices. The calculation invites a precise descent statement, but on this page the ambient set of triples and the quotient realizing that descent have not yet been specified.

34. **Scan 202, Proposition, (88) — unproved claim.** Grothendieck states « il f. et s. qu'on ait » (88) for completing prescribed lower rows to α and β satisfying the determinant and loop relations. He then calls the set of solutions a « torseur » over Ẑ and refers back to an earlier proposition (page number uncertain, 383 or 384). A proof would have to establish both existence of the upper rows under (88) and freeness and transitivity of the announced action; that action continues on the next scan.

35. **Scan 202, left margin beside the Proposition — unproved claim.** The marginal assertion is « Pour μ fixé, on peut tjrs trouver c,d,t,u satisfaisant la relation (88) — heureusement ! ». No construction of those four entries is supplied on this page. A proof would need to handle the signed unit values of both quadratic expressions over Ẑ, including the primes 2 and 3 that determine the displayed signs.

36. **Scan 202, Proposition and (88) — own idea.** One could test the row-existence and completion statements over finite quotients, then study whether compatible solutions can be chosen through the inverse system defining Ẑ. **Confidence: medium as an approach**, because the conditions are polynomial and the torsor assertion should impose strong control on fibres, but finite existence alone would not identify the claimed action or prove its freeness. Such computations would investigate the stated proposition without supplying readings for any uncertain ink.

37. **Scan 203, corollary following (89) — unproved claim.** The assertion “il f. et s.” gives parity conditions for choosing the two matrices congruent to the identity modulo 2 and then calls the resulting solution set a “torseur sous” the profinite integers. A proof within these pages would need both the lifting argument preserving the loop relation and a check that the stated simultaneous left action is free and transitive; the previous page's proposition must be included in assessing how much is actually left unproved.

38. **Scan 203, Scholie around (90) — unpursued implication.** Grothendieck calls the five quantities “invariants adéliques” and says that this is “ce qu'on peut faire de mieux” in the current setting. This invites a precise account of what information the passage to these lower-row data retains, and what the omitted upper-row data can change, without treating the claim as a global optimality theorem.

39. **Scan 203, (90)–(91) — own idea.** Compare the fibres of the map to the five quantities with the diagonal equivalence on the additional matrix `f`; this may separate the loss caused by the linear representation from the loss caused by choosing representatives. **Confidence: medium**, because the page explicitly distinguishes the outer data from an effective automorphism and records the ambiguity in `f`, but it does not supply a completeness statement for these invariants.

40. **Scan 204, opening paragraph — unpursued implication.** The additional datum is said to be “un peu trop faible pour reconstituer” the associated matrix. The exact failure of reconstruction merits isolation as a statement about fibres: is the ambiguity precisely the one subsequently represented by the torsor, or is further information lost in the representation?

41. **Scan 204, middle display and right margin — unproved claim.** The quotient is identified with a twist by the opposite torsor, and the margin says “c'est un … torseur à droite.” A detailed verification would have to state the left and right actions, their commuting relation, and the resulting quotient convention; the uncertain placement of the contracted-product notation is a transcription issue, not a licence to choose the conventions silently.

42. **Scans 204–205, final and opening paragraphs — conjecture / expectation (programme, not a formal conjecture).** “Il faudra introduire” leads into the proposed study of the “groupe adélique” of triples satisfying the loop relation and the canonical homomorphism into it. These lines explicitly defer that construction; they do not on their own establish its image, kernel, or a universal property.

43. **Scans 204–205 — own idea.** Formulate the diagonal quotient as a precise moduli problem with its sign ambiguity retained, then ask whether the displayed reconstruction descends to an actual matrix or only to its class. **Confidence: medium**, because scan 204 explicitly discusses a right torsor and the change of sign under replacing `f` by `f(-1)`; the correct categorical formulation still requires checking against the rest of the manuscript.

44. **Scan 206, paragraph after (94) — unproved claim.** The normalization by an inner automorphism is asserted to exist “et un seul,” with the displayed choice `γ = β₀⁻¹`. Existence is linked to (49); uniqueness would require identifying the stabilizer of the chosen involution within the permitted conjugating group, rather than assuming that all inner representatives are automatically unique.

45. **Scan 206, (93)–(96) — unpursued implication.** The centralizing case `[u, σ∞] = 1` removes one variable and expresses the data through a pair satisfying a cyclic relation and the loop relation. This is a concrete place to compare the earlier three-variable presentation with a two-variable presentation while retaining the explicit condition `2ν + 1 ∈ Ẑ*`.

46. **Scan 206, (95)–(96) — own idea.** Examine the solution set for particular admissible values of `ν`, beginning with `ν = 0`, and determine which freedoms in `f` survive both relations and the allowed equivalences. **Confidence: medium**, because the equations display the necessary starting constraints, but neither sufficiency for reconstructing every relevant automorphism nor a classification of their fibres is established by this page alone.
