## 5. Research notes — separate from the transcription

These notes are in English and do not emend the diplomatic text. “Unproved claim” means that the cited passage does not give a complete proof there; an argument may occur earlier or later in the manuscript, and a recap may summarize an earlier result. “Conjecture” includes a written question or tentative expectation. Own ideas are explicitly labelled, with confidence and a reason; they are proposals for checking, not established conclusions or claims of novelty. Quotations are short extracts from the supplied manuscript; its scan numbering is used in the citations.

### Research note 1

**Scan606, margin beside (104) — unproved claim.** “On aura néc.ᵗ” introduces the necessary congruence \(\mu\equiv-1\pmod3\). A proof should reduce \(c^2+cd+d^2\) modulo 3 and use the unit hypothesis; this is separate from determining the ink in the marginal abbreviation (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 606).

### Research note 2

**Scan606, (104)–(106) — own idea; confidence high for the residue calculation, conditional on the displayed hypotheses.** The simultaneous conditions at 2 can be made explicit: for even \(c\) and odd \(d\), \(c^2+cd+d^2\equiv cd+1\pmod4\), so the written condition \(\mu\equiv1\pmod4\) forces \(c\equiv2\pmod4\). A prime-by-prime parameter check could clarify which pairs in the profinite integers satisfy the full unit condition; this is a suggested calculation, not a claim of novelty (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 606).

### Research note 3

**Scans606–607, (108)–(109) — unpursued implication.** The assertion that “le signe” does not depend on the choices is followed by an explicit reduction modulo 4. It would be useful to isolate which part of the argument establishes independence in the indicated quotient and which part only computes the residue; the subgroup definitions and earlier numbered relations lie outside the supplied block (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 606–607).

### Research note 4

**Scan607, diagonal margin and first matrix identities — own idea; confidence high, because the margin states the operation explicitly.** The superscript \(t\) is defined here by \({}^{t}u=(\mathrm{Tr}\,u)-u\), not by an instruction to transpose entries. Checking the subsequent products with this operation is a useful safeguard against a mathematically plausible but textually false reconstruction (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 607).

### Research note 5

**Scan608, alternative proof after the Corollaire — unpursued implication.** The phrase “le foncteur Ext” introduces an argument in the category of commutative extensions, after assuming commutativity. A careful reconstruction should specify the source object in Ext and check how the two indicated subgroup restrictions form a direct-sum decomposition; that categorical step must not be confused with an argument for arbitrary noncommutative extensions (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 608).

### Research note 6

**Scan608, last paragraph — unproved claim.** “les seuls élémts d'ordre4” are asserted to lie in the indicated cyclic subgroup. The next page uses this assertion to rule out a trivial action, so a complete proof should trace the order computation to the earlier presentations or supply it from the extension data (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 608–609).

### Research note 7

**Scan609, (111)–(114) — own idea; confidence medium, because the finite-group description is clear but some normalizations precede these scans.** The dihedral description suggests writing the central extension by an explicit normalized 2-cocycle in the basis of the two quotient characters. Such a calculation could test exactly which cup product, and whether any character-square terms, corresponds to the later arithmetic class; the statement that the abstract group is dihedral does not alone fix this identification (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 609–611).

### Research note 8

**Scan610, first (115) — unpursued implication.** The “sous-groupe des commutateurs” description identifies the kernel of the central extension with the derived subgroup. One can compare the resulting commutator pairing on the quotient with the cocycle suggested in the preceding note; this also offers a way to distinguish the finite extension from its arithmetic pullback (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 610).

### Research note 9

**Scan610, middle question — conjecture / question.** “mais qu'en est-il de son image inverse” asks whether the pulled-back extension splits. The manuscript immediately distinguishes nonexistence of a splitting extending the particular section \(A\) from nonexistence of any splitting, and a proof would have to address the latter additional step (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 610).

### Research note 10

**Scan610, lower middle — conjecture.** “Je présume” introduces the expected nontriviality of the restriction to the decorated double-prime group, and then to the displayed arithmetic subgroup. The successive restrictions should be separated when testing the claim; nontriviality before restriction does not itself establish nontriviality after restriction (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 610).

### Research note 11

**Scan610, last paragraph — conjecture / question.** “Il serait intéressant d'identifier” asks for an explicit description of the class \(c\) in the Brauer group. The next scan proposes a cup product, so this question should be tracked together with that tentative identification, rather than treated as resolved merely by the appearance of a formula (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 610–611).

### Research note 12

**Scan 611, upper and middle; unproved claim.**

The phrase “Sauf erreur on aura” qualifies the identification of \(c\) as the cup product of the two written classes, after which “Il doit être trivial” introduces the expectation that the resulting \(c\) is nonzero and remains nonsplit after passage to \(\mathbb Q(i)\). Checking this requires recovering the precise coefficient convention, the two character classes, and the map into the Brauer group, then testing the class and its restriction; the uncertain degree in (115) makes those identifications especially important (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 611).

### Research note 13

**Scan 611, (115) and following prose; own idea.**

**Own idea, conditional consistency check; confidence high conditional on the class identification, because it follows from a standard norm identity.** If the displayed fields really identify the two usual Kummer classes for \(-3\) and \(3\), and the cup product is the usual quaternion Brauer class, it would give \((-3,3)=0\): \(3\) is the norm of \(\sqrt{-3}\) from \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\), equivalently this is the identity \((a,-a)=0\). This would conflict with the written expectation “\(c\) ainsi explicité est \(\ne0\),” so the next step is to test the exact class, basis, and coefficient conventions rather than emend the manuscript; no novelty is claimed (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 611; Skorobogatov, 2007, pp. 9–10).

### Research note 14

**Scan 612, upper-left margin and (118)–(122); unproved claim.**

“Ceci mérite d'être explicité dans un théorème récapitulatif” requests a systematic statement of the construction. Such a statement would have to distinguish the two codomains, the sign ambiguity of the first map, the choices represented by \(\alpha,\beta\), and the congruence characterizations, with a proof of independence and homomorphism properties; the short doubtful symbols in (121)–(122) should be resolved from adjoining manuscript context before that reconstruction (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 612).

### Research note 15

**Scan 613, middle, (124)–(127); unpursued implication.**

“Il serait temps de rectifier la confusion” and the concluding limitation “c'est bien sur \(Z^!_{\rho,\sigma}\), non sur \(Z_{\rho,\sigma}\)” make the index-two distinction part of the domain of the maps. The exact-sequence diagram suggests that any extension of those maps to the larger group must be checked for compatibility with the enlarged procyclic kernel and its conjugation action, rather than inferred solely from the similar notation; the superscripts in the correction are still textually uncertain (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 613).

### Research note 16

**Scan 614, middle, before (128); unproved claim.**

The assertion that the conditions are “satisfaites évidemment par \(b=-1\)” provides the proposed value of the map on the indicated generator. To turn the subsequent factorization and square into a complete proof, one should verify that the preceding congruence characterization determines this value uniquely and that the generator and quotient conventions used in (127)–(129) agree (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 614).

### Research note 17

**Scan 615, after (131); own idea.**

**Own idea, elementary consistency check; confidence high conditional on the written quotient being exactly \(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\).** Since the automorphism group of a cyclic group of order two is trivial, the statement that the action on \(L_\sigma/\{\pm1\}\simeq\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\) is given by \(\varepsilon_2\) cannot distinguish the two signs on that quotient. It may be recording an action visible before taking the quotient, so comparing the action on \(L_\sigma\) itself would clarify what information survives; this observation does not justify changing the sentence (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 615).

### Research note 18

**Scan 615, lower, (132); unproved claim.**

“Se remonte de façon évidente” asserts a lift of the \(\sigma\)-map, with (132) pointing to the subgroup \(\mathcal M(0)\). A verification should establish that its identification with \(\widetilde\Gamma_{\mathbb Q}\) and its image in \(N_\sigma^*\) really give the displayed lift and that reduction modulo the central signs recovers the map (130) (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 615).

### Research note 19

**Scan 615, lower, comparison of the two maps; unpursued implication.**

“La symétrie de présentation des deux hom (130) est un peu” followed by the doubtful reading “bidon” marks an asymmetry that is not exhausted by their parallel display. Comparing the lifting obstruction for the \(\rho\)-map with the exhibited lift for the \(\sigma\)-map could connect the earlier central extension class to this difference; this is a question to check against later manuscript pages, not a claim that the issue is left unresolved in the whole work (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 615).

### Research note 20

**Scan 616, (132)–(135); unproved claim.** “Ainsi on a … un scindage” follows the assertion that the induced map is trivial on the indicated L-subgroup. A full verification should identify the quotient used in (132), prove that the proposed section respects its kernel, and check the resulting map and semidirect-product decomposition in the topology intended by the manuscript. The visibly different rho and sigma subscripts in (134) should be checked against surrounding pages before using the displayed image formulas (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 616).

### Research note 21

**Scan 617, (138)–(140); unproved claim.** “Et on trouve que” precedes the isomorphism defining the group denoted M(1/2), followed by several simultaneous decompositions. To reconstruct the proof, one should isolate the kernel and image of the indicated N-subgroup and then verify that a single chosen section yields each displayed decomposition. The claim is given together with earlier definitions, not as a detailed stand-alone argument on this page (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 617).

### Research note 22

**Scan 617, right margin beside (140); unpursued implication.** The warning that M-zero-exclamation is invariant in M-exclamation “mais non dans” the full ambient group limits how the chosen section can be transported. Any comparison of the decompositions under ambient conjugation must therefore distinguish invariance inside the smaller group from invariance in the whole group. The words “cf plus bas” explicitly defer further treatment (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 617).

### Research note 23

**Scans 617–618, (141) and Proposition; unproved claim.** The argument uses the image of rho in a finite quotient to force the epsilon-three character to be 1, and the Proposition says that the map “est injectif, et a pour image” the corresponding kernel. The sketch should be completed by verifying uniqueness of the correcting element and by proving that every element of that character kernel admits the prescribed correction. This is partly argued in the manuscript, rather than merely asserted without any indication (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 617–618).

### Research note 24

**Scan 618, (142)–(143); unpursued implication.** The rho-based subgroup M(-j-bar) gives a family of decompositions over a restricted quotient, whereas the preceding sigma-based subgroup M(1/2) maps to the full displayed quotient. Comparing these sections could clarify the role of the epsilon-three restriction and the distinction between the two stabilizer constructions. The uncertain primes and zigzag superscripts must be resolved before formulating an exact comparison statement (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 618).

### Research note 25

**Scan 618, cancelled final paragraph; own idea, low confidence.** The withdrawn assertion beginning “Notons maintenant que” suggests checking whether conjugation by the indicated involution preserves each intermediate subgroup, not only L-rho and its centralizer. Such a check might explain why the paragraph was abandoned, but a cancelled statement supplies no evidence that the proposed normalizing action is valid. Confidence is low because some of the relevant decorations are difficult to read and the author does not give a replacement argument here (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 618).

### Research note 26

**Scans 619–620, upper nonlifting discussion; conjecture / expectation.** Scan 619 states that the canonical map “ne se relève pas,” while scan 620 describes the extension as one whose nontriviality “on s'est convaincu plus ou moins.” This contrast makes the epistemic status worth checking against later pages: the block identifies the proposed obstruction but does not provide a complete independent proof of its nonvanishing. A proof would require a nontriviality criterion for the specific central extension, with continuity accounted for if the groups are profinite (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 619–620).

### Research note 27

**Scan 619, (144)–(145); unproved claim.** The manuscript says that the first diagram “montre” a diagram of “carrés cartésiens.” To make this implication explicit, each square needs a kernel-and-image or universal-property verification, including the added vertex labelled “sans !” and the quotients in the top row. This would also clarify exactly which pulled-back central extension is being compared with the extension of M(0) (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 619).

### Research note 28

**Scan 620, (146/145)–(148) and final two cases; unproved claim.** The displayed map is declared “épi,” followed by a correction argument dividing according to epsilon-three. A complete proof should verify membership of the corrected element in the intended intersection subgroup in both cases, not merely its action on rho, and should state precisely which quotient is used by “congru.” The last calculation supplies a substantial part of the second case, but several earlier facts are invoked implicitly (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 620).

### Research note 29

**Scans 619–620, central extension comparison; own idea, medium confidence.** One could express the proposed lifting obstruction as a continuous second-cohomology class with coefficients in the displayed central subgroup and compare its restrictions along the rho-based and sigma-based sections. This is a plausible organizing calculation because these pages already identify the relevant pullbacks and a nonlifting assertion, but the block alone does not establish either the class or a nonzero restriction. Any finite-quotient calculation would also require checking the relevant inflation map before concluding nontriviality upstairs (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 619–620).

### Research note 30

**Scan 621, upper half, after (149); unproved claim (identification left implicit here).** The manuscript says that the canonical map $\gamma_{\rho,\sigma}\simeq Z_\rho^{*!}/\mu\to N_\rho^*/\mu$ “n'est autre que le premier hom (130).” Checking this identification requires following the inclusions and quotient maps used in the construction of (130), rather than just comparing source and target; the assertion may have been justified in the preceding development (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 621).

### Research note 31

**Scan 621, heading 9° and (1)–(2); unpursued implication.** The stated purpose is to “récapituler ce qui me semble essentiel,” after an explicit worry about losing the thread. The simultaneous presentations of $Z_{\rho,\sigma}$ and its index-two subgroup give a useful audit point: the action and the inclusion must be checked together when comparing this recap with earlier semidirect-product constructions (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 621).

### Research note 32

**Scan 622, (4)–(4 bis); unproved claim (recapitulated).** “s'identifie au diagramme” asserts compatibility of the two entire extension diagrams, not merely isomorphism of the middle groups. A verification should check both inclusions of kernels and the induced identification of the common quotient; this is a recap, so the relevant proof may occur earlier (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 622).

### Research note 33

**Scan 622, (5 bis); own idea.** The displayed factorization of the two $\mu$-valued characters through $\chi:\widetilde\Gamma_{\mathbb Q}\to\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{*}$ suggests auditing the finite congruence quotient through which the pair factors, then comparing its pullback with the central extension discussed before the recap. **Confidence: medium:** the factorization itself is clearly drawn, but the intrinsic character labels in (5) remain uncertain and the construction must be checked against their definitions (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 622).

### Research note 34

**Scan 622, (6)–(7); unproved claim (recapitulated).** After the definition of $N_\sigma^*$, the four intersection statements in (7) are stated without a proof on this page. A direct check would use the action on $\sigma$, distinguish the involutions $\tau$ and $\tau'$, and verify the two different intersections with $\Pi$ and $\Pi_0$; the displayed isomorphism symbol in the second line has been retained (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 622).

### Research note 35

**Scan 623, (10)–(12); unproved claim (recapitulated).** The key assertion is that the indicated homomorphism “induit un iso” from $\mathcal M(1/2)=N_{\sigma0}^{*!}$ to $\gamma_{\rho,\sigma}$. The subsequent “scindages en produits $1/2$ directs” depend on both surjectivity and triviality of this subgroup's intersection with the geometric kernel, so those are the two proof obligations to trace in the earlier pages (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 623).

### Research note 36

**Scans 622–623, (7) and (14); own idea.** Compare the lifting problem for the two finite kernels recorded as $L_\sigma\simeq\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$ and $L_\rho\simeq\mathbb Z/6\mathbb Z$ after their common order-two subgroup is quotiented out. **Confidence: medium:** the orders and the intersections with $\Pi$ are explicitly displayed, but any identification of the resulting obstruction classes requires the actions and surrounding extension maps, not just the group orders (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 622–623).

### Research note 37

**Scan 624, (16)–(18); unproved claim (recapitulated).** “on trouve,” “on note aussi,” and “On voit” introduce the centralizer inclusion, the identification with $\mathcal M'(-\bar j)$, and the displayed isomorphism onto the subgroup cut out by $\varepsilon_3=1$. A verification must track that restriction of the quotient and the kernel calculation, not simply an abstract isomorphism of groups; the exact first centralizer subscript remains doubtful (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 624).

### Research note 38

**Scans 623–624, (10) and (18)–(19); own idea.** Compare the section denoted $\mathcal M(1/2)$ with $\mathcal M'(-\bar j)$ after restricting the former to the kernel of $\varepsilon_3$, and ask whether the two resulting sections are conjugate by the geometric kernel. **Confidence: medium-low:** the two constructions and their quotient groups are visibly juxtaposed, but conjugacy needs information about the induced actions and cannot follow from the displayed isomorphisms alone (Grothendieck, 1981, scans 623–624).

### Research note 39

**Scan 624, cancelled final paragraph; unpursued implication (abandoned on this page).** The cancelled passage begins “La correspondance entre” and then “est définie par l'application,” but its last arrow has no written target. This records an unfinished attempt to specify the correspondence between the two displayed presentations; no completed definition or valid comparison is asserted here (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 624).

# LM_C3-625-643 — cote 140-3, scans 625–643  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_C3-625-643\LM_C3-625-643_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes

These English notes concern questions, deferred arguments, and possible investigations suggested by the supplied passage (Grothendieck, 1981). They make no claim that a question remains open in the literature or later in the manuscript, and no claim of novelty. The short quotations identify the author's statements; doubtful quoted words remain identified as doubtful. Items explicitly labeled **own idea** are proposals for further checking, with their confidence and reason stated. They have not been used to change the transcription.

### Scans 625–630

1. **Scan 625, lines 13–19 — unproved claim.** “`μ_{τ′} ne normalise pas Z_{ρ,0}^!`” is the decisive warning against the displayed direct-product decomposition that follows as a rejected possibility. A proof or verification would need the conjugation action on the two factors and an explicit element or character detecting the failure of normality.

2. **Scan 625, (22) and final paragraph — unpursued implication.** “`une quasi-section de multiplicité 2`” identifies the extension by `μ` as the remaining discrepancy between the proposed quasi-section and a genuine section. It would be useful to track precisely which quotient and which finite-index restriction remove that discrepancy; the next scans begin doing this, but the warning on this page should not be lost in a simplified product notation.

3. **Scan 626, opening paragraph — unproved claim.** “`elle est sûrement`” precedes the heavily revised *non triviale / scindée* passage. The exact assertion depends on the cancellation scope; any mathematical commentary should first settle that textual issue, then supply the relevant splitting or nonsplitting argument rather than read the word *sûrement* as a proof.

4. **Scan 626, remark — conjecture.** “`il y a fort à parier que celui-ci est justement ε₂`” proposes a specific quadratic character for the extra component of the action. The calculation sought is explicit: extract the `μ` coordinate after conjugation, compare it with `ε₂`, and check the resulting invariance of the displayed intersection of the two subgroups of `Γ_\mathbb Q^{\sim}`.

5. **Scan 626, final paragraph — unpursued implication.** “`il y aurait lieu de reprendre l'étude de l'extension`” proposes revisiting the preceding construction from the viewpoint of the associated `α,β`. Since their definitions are not supplied in these six scans, this is a cross-reference to be checked against the earlier manuscript, not an invitation to reconstruct them from expected theory.

6. **Scan 627, opening — conjecture.** “`une autre section partielle`” over the displayed kernel of `ε₂ε₃` is proposed, together with the tentative notation `\mathcal M(\sqrt3)` or `\mathcal M(q)`. The three question marks and the adjoining marginal note indicate an unresolved identification; constructing the section and checking its field interpretation are distinct tasks.

7. **Scan 627, middle paragraph — unproved claim.** The passage says that sections correspond to points, with the quoted adverb read tentatively as “`inévitablement`”. The argument would need precise hypotheses and a statement of what is meant by correspondence, by the tilde qualification, and by a partial section over a finite extension; the wording on this page alone does not establish all those implications.

8. **Scan 627, about lines 20–26 — unpursued implication.** The section in b) is compared with the point `1/2`, while the section in c) is compared with `-\bar\jmath`; the passage then stresses that the other group is “`pas ⊂ \mathcal M_0^!`”. This shifts attention from the geometry of a point on `U_{0,3}` to the lifting problem after taking the quotient by `μ`, and provides the transition to the moduli discussion.

9. **Scan 628, middle — conjecture.** “`J'ai donc l'impression ... ne peut se remonter`” states an expectation of a failure to lift the section over the full `Γ_\mathbb Q^{\sim}`. The proposed connection with a nontrivial extension is followed by the question about a curve “`d'invariant 0`” and the author's immediate doubt, “`Alors que semble absurde`”; these are stages of the investigation, not a settled nonexistence claim.

10. **Scan 628, (26), continued on scan 629 — own idea.** Compare the obstruction for a fixed point of `M′_{1,1}` with the set of all points above its coarse-moduli image, keeping the two fibres separate throughout the calculation. **Confidence: high as a useful diagnostic**, because the next page explicitly says that the failure of the first lift “`ne signifie pas`” failure of a lift of its image; this is a proposal for organizing the calculation, not a claim of novelty.

11. **Scan 629, (27)–(30) — unproved claim.** The identifications of the two moduli objects with quotient descriptions lead to the assertion that the datum in (30) “`équivaut à la donnée de (29)`” after forming `T=\widetilde T/μ`. A full check should identify the action of the kernel on `U_{0,3}`, the equivariance conditions, and the equivalences between the indicated torsor groupoids rather than only their object sets.

12. **Scan 629, slanted margin — unpursued implication.** The margin contrasts a construction defined “`pour une courbe ... mod symétrie`” with one defined “`seulement pour une vraie courbe elliptique`”. Its two long technical nouns and the order condition are doubtful readings, so the intended interpretation through finite-level structures should be verified against the ink before it is used as an explanation of the torsor lift.

13. **Scan 630, obstruction paragraph — unproved claim.** “`l'obstruction est, comme il se doit`” identifies the obstruction with an extension by `μ₂` and then with an element of `H²(\mathbb Q,μ₂)≃ {}_2 Br(\mathbb Q)`. The passage states the identification but does not compute the class here; the concrete pullback extension associated with the chosen torsor is the object to calculate.

14. **Scan 630, underlined conclusion and margin — unproved claim.** The underlined assertion “`donc Γ_\mathbb Q→\mathcal G_3 est surjectif`” has the adjoining correction “`[erroné/corrigé], cf rectification plus bas`”. It must be recorded as a revised claim, and the later conclusion on this same page that the image has order 2 must be checked against the proposed argument from connectedness.

15. **Scan 630, final paragraph — own idea.** Compute the image of the torsor homomorphism first, then pull the finite extension back along that actual image, rather than use surjectivity inferred from the two-point image in `U_{0,3}`. **Confidence: high as a verification strategy**, because the handwritten correction and the subsequent order-2 conclusion already isolate the problematic step; the expected obstruction remains to be calculated.

### Scans 631–636

#### R631.1 — Conjecture / expectation: the middle extension is cyclic of order four

**Source:** Scan 631, paragraph before the first extension display and first marginal note. Grothendieck writes, “ça ne peut guère être que `Z/4Z` !”, then adds an argument using the order of the image of `σ=σ_∞`. A full verification would distinguish the two extensions of the displayed order-two group by `μ`, identify the indicated inverse image inside `\widetilde{\mathcal G}_3`, and check the claimed order of the chosen lift. The margin's “canoniquement” also raises the separate issue of which choice makes the identification canonical.

#### R631.2 — Unproved claim: the displayed lifting problem has no solution

**Source:** Scan 631, below the lifting triangle and the lower marginal note. The words “n'existe sûrement pas” concern a lift of the displayed Galois homomorphism through the middle extension. The marginal appeal to abelianization and `Z_3^*` appears to be a compressed justification, but several readings there remain weak; a proof should first reconstruct the precise character and quotient appearing in that note.

#### R631.3 — Own idea: make the pullback extension explicit

**Source:** Scan 631, phrase “image inverse de l'extension” and the lifting triangle. **Confidence: high as a proposed organization of the calculation; no vanishing or nonvanishing conclusion asserted.** One can write the pullback of the displayed extension along the Galois character and formulate the question as whether that pulled-back extension splits. This follows directly from the drawn square and provides a way to separate the group-extension data from the less legible marginal calculation.

#### R632.1 — Unproved claim left for explanation: behavior after adjoining `sqrt(3)`

**Source:** Scan 632, first three lines continuing scan 631's “Il faudrait regarder pourquoi, en termes classiques”. The manuscript says the obstruction is “scindée” after passing to the indicated subgroup corresponding to `Q(sqrt(3))`. The precise extension, action on its kernel, and meaning of this restriction should be reconstructed before giving the requested classical explanation; the field is transcribed without a minus sign.

#### R632.2 — Unpursued implication: compare a chosen point with its coarse image

**Source:** Scan 632, “ne se remonte pas” followed by “son image 0 … doit bien se remonter”. The argument distinguishes failure to lift one chosen rational point of `M_{1,1}'` from the expected existence of a lift of its coarse image. An explicit comparison of the corresponding torsors would clarify how those two statements coexist and which choices of torsor over the same reduced fiber are being varied.

#### R632.3 — Unproved claim: the reduced fiber and its action

**Source:** Scan 632, definition `P_0=Q_{red}` and “can.l isomorphe à Spec Q(-bar j)”. The text identifies the reduced fiber, describes its two points after extending the field, and says the `\mathcal G_3`-action factors through the sign map. A proof would calculate the fiber scheme, separate its reduced part from any multiplicity, and verify the action on those two geometric points.

#### R633.1 — Unproved claim: identify the kernel as a cyclic group of order six

**Source:** Scan 633, NB: “extension centrale”, “isom. à `Z/6Z`”, and “noyau engendré par `ρ`”. The margin compresses both a splitting assertion and a generator assertion. Checking the order of `ρ`, its image in the order-three quotient, and the central order-two subgroup would make the identification precise.

#### R633.2 — Unproved claim: the equivalence between point-lifting and torsor-lifting categories

**Source:** Scan 633, “la catégorie des relèvements … est équivalente à celle des … torseurs”. The statement includes the equivariant map to the underlying scheme, not only the abstract torsor. A detailed construction in both directions should also explain why isomorphism classes are described by conjugacy modulo the indicated kernels, as specified by the interline insertion.

#### R633.3 — Unpursued implication: failure for the preferred splitting does not settle all lifts

**Source:** Scan 633, “On avait choisi un `P=T`” and “mais le torseur `T` ne se remonte pas”. The chosen split image of the order-two group gives one torsor in the fiber, whose failure to lift leaves other torsors to be examined. The transition to considering the image of a general homomorphism is the beginning of that wider classification problem.

#### R634.1 — Unproved claim: a liftable homomorphism must have full image

**Source:** Scan 634, first paragraph: “il faut prendre un épi”. The argument excludes the order-two subgroup and its conjugates before passing to the full group. To make the reduction complete, one should verify that the subgroup list is exhaustive under the prescribed sign character and that nonlifting is unchanged under the stated conjugacies.

#### R634.2 — Conjecture / question explicitly deferred: existence and classification of full-image lifts

**Source:** Scan 634, “s'il existe un tel relèvement” and “comment les obtenir”. Grothendieck calls this an “exercice plaisant et délectable” in class field theory, then says he will not pursue it “pour le moment”. The existence problem and classification of all such lifts should be kept separate; neither is supplied on this page.

#### R634.3 — Unpursued implication: relate homomorphism lifts to sections of the larger extension

**Source:** Scan 634, final paragraph: “il me faudrait en m̄ temps expliciter la relation”. The requested comparison is between choices of lift of the Galois homomorphism and splittings of the displayed extension by the completed group. A precise comparison would need to preserve the relevant equivalence relations, especially conjugacy by the geometric kernel and any distinction between a chosen representative and its class.

#### R635.1 — Unproved claim left for later: normalization by `τ'`

**Source:** Scan 635, “Modulo une vérification que je vais faire plus bas, `τ'` normalise…”. This is explicitly a deferred verification on which the semidirect-product construction in (34) depends. A proof should compute the action on the defining kernel of `ε_2`, then check the intersection with the order-two factor and the stated index four.

#### R635.2 — Unproved claim: compare the two kernel descriptions

**Source:** Scan 635, (32)–(33). The manuscript gives both the pair-of-characters kernel and the kernel of the cyclotomic map followed by reduction modulo 12. Verifying their equality requires identifying the two displayed characters on that quotient; one should first resolve the changes of notation in the canceled right-hand side of (32), rather than silently identify its distinct prime and circle superscripts.

#### R635.3 — Unpursued implication: check the partial section after forming the semidirect product

**Source:** Scan 635, (35) and “c'est une section partielle”. The displayed isomorphism to `\widetilde\Gamma_Q'''` asserts more than the existence of a subgroup: it asserts the behavior of the projection on that subgroup. Once normalization is established, checking its kernel, image, and compatibility with the previously defined partial section would justify this step and the announced isomorphisms on the next page.

#### R636.1 — Own idea: use the canceled index diagram as a consistency check, not as a proved lattice

**Source:** Scan 636, canceled diagram (37). **Confidence: high for the numerical observation; low as evidence of any additional group structure.** The two visible routes from `\mathcal M^0(-\bar j)` to `\mathcal N_\rho^*` have products of indices `2·6·2` and `2·4·3`, both 24. This is a useful check on the transcribed labels, but equal products do not prove the indicated containments or normality, and the whole diagram is canceled.

#### R636.2 — Unproved claim in a canceled draft: the intended finite-quotient isomorphism

**Source:** Scan 636, “induit un isomorphisme d'” and incomplete (39). The canceled draft moves from the finite subgroup `\mathbb D_\rho` to an isomorphism whose target is written only as `\mathcal N_\rho^*/`. Its denominator and precise assertion must be obtained from subsequent reasoning if they are to be discussed mathematically; they cannot be supplied to this transcription.

#### R632.4 — Own idea: test the proposed splitting at a real place

**Source:** Scans 631–632, the cyclic order-four extension and the statement that the obstruction becomes “scindée” over `Q(sqrt(3))`. **Confidence: high in the conditional elementary group calculation, moderate in its applicability here because the full notation and coefficient action precede this extract.** If the extension is literally the constant cyclic extension `C4 → C2` and the prescribed quadratic character is nontrivial on complex conjugation, no homomorphism `C2 → C4` lifts that character: every element of order at most two in `C4` maps to the identity in `C2`. Restriction to the totally real field `Q(sqrt(3))` would preserve this real-place test, so the extension, coefficient action, and meaning of “scindée” should be checked before accepting that interpretation of the assertion. This is a diagnostic to apply to the manuscript's definitions, not a correction of the transcribed field or a conclusion about the intended construction.

### Scans 637–643

#### R637.1 — Scan 637, paragraph after (37)

**Kind: conjecture / stated program.** Grothendieck writes, “Je vais examiner la question d'invariance” and also mentions “la structure des groupes quotients”. The indicated problem is to determine which finite-index intermediate subgroups in the upper part of the diagram are normal in which larger groups, and then identify the resulting quotients. Subsequent pages in this fragment address parts of this program; the diagram itself should not be read as having already settled all normality assertions.

#### R638.1 — Scan 638, right marginal warning to (38)

**Kind: unproved claim at this point.** The warning says the candidate \(\mathcal M'(-\bar j)\mu_{\tau'}\) “n'est pas un sous-groupe”, because \(\mu_{\tau'}\) does not normalize \(\mathcal M'(-\bar j)\). To substantiate this statement independently, one needs the actual conjugation action and an element that leaves the subgroup under that action. Scan 641 returns to precisely this normalization issue through \(\varepsilon_2\).

#### R638.2 — Scan 638, question below (39)

**Kind: conjecture / question.** The explicit question is, “sont ils invariants dans \(Z_\rho\)?” for the four displayed subgroups. This question is answered affirmatively on scan 640, then distinguished from normality in the larger \(\mathcal N_\rho^{*}\) on scan 641. It is useful to keep those two ambient groups separate when reconstructing the argument.

#### R639.1 — Scan 639, upper paragraph

**Kind: unproved claim.** In reducing normalization to the action of \(\rho\), the text uses \(Z_\rho=L_\rho Z_\rho^{!}\) and comments, “c'est ± trivial”. A standalone proof would need the earlier definitions of \(L_\rho\), \(Z_\rho^{!}\), and their multiplication, rather than treating the diagram as a proof of that product description. No such earlier definitions have been reconstructed from this excerpt.

#### R639.2 — Scan 639, display (*)

**Kind: unproved claim recalled from elsewhere.** The introduction “or on sait que” invokes a congruence for \([x,u]\) modulo \(\Pi_0\), expressed using \(\operatorname{sg}(x)\) and an exponent read provisionally as \(\xi_2(u)\). The lemma depends on this relation, so an independent verification must first settle the definitions and the exponent's additive or multiplicative convention. The uncertainty between \(\xi_2\) and \(\varepsilon_2\) is a textual issue as well as a possible mathematical distinction.

#### R639.3 — Scan 639, display (*) and condition c)

**Kind: own idea. Confidence: medium.** Compare the inserted exponents with the final condition \(\varepsilon_2(u)=1\) and with the earlier definitions of these characters before trying to simplify the lemma. The reason for this suggestion is physical: the inserted exponent has a descending \(\xi\)-like stroke, whereas the condition has the clearer \(\varepsilon\)-like form. They could encode related characters with different value conventions, but that interpretation is not established by the visible notation alone.

#### R640.1 — Scan 640, corollaries and intersection argument

**Kind: unpursued implication within this local argument.** The conclusion “les quatre groupes (39) sont distingués dans \(Z_\rho\)” is obtained by combining normalization with subgroup intersections. This suggests documenting exactly which ambient normalizer is available for each intersection, rather than transferring a statement about \(Z_\rho\) to \(\mathcal N_\rho^{*}\) without a new check. The next page shows why the transfer matters: one of the four subgroups fails the stronger condition.

#### R641.1 — Scan 641, displays (42)–(43)

**Kind: own idea. Confidence: medium.** A careful reconstruction could isolate the obstruction to normalization by \(\tau'\) as the nontrivial value of the displayed \(\varepsilon_2\) character, then test it on an explicit element from the earlier presentation. This is suggested by “\(\tau'(x)\in Z_{\rho,0}^{!}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon_2(x)=1\)”, not by an externally supplied theorem. The unprimed \(\tau\) at the end of (42) should first be compared with the author’s earlier notation; it should not be silently corrected to \(\tau'\).

#### R641.2 — Scan 641, final corollary

**Kind: unpursued implication.** The assertion that \(\mathcal M'(-\bar j)\) is the sole exceptional subgroup among the four provides a way to organize the lattice by the conjugation action of the extra involution. One can ask whether adjoining \(\mu\) removes the obstruction in each case and how that operation is reflected in the finite quotient. The fragment makes the subgroup assertions but does not yet give a complete action table for that quotient.

#### R642.1 — Scan 642, display (44) and surrounding paragraph

**Kind: unproved identification used locally.** The text calls \(\mathbb D_\rho\) a normalizer in \(\operatorname{GL}(2,\mathbb Z)\), “groupe isomorphe à \(D_6\), et d'ordre 12”. The local injectivity argument uses its intersection with the kernel, but the normalizer identification itself is not derived on this page. A complete independent account would need generators, their action on \(L_\rho\), and the precise convention for \(D_6\).

#### R642.2 — Scans 642–643, page transition

**Kind: conjecture / expectation.** The words “Il serait tentant” lead to the queried isomorphism \(\mathcal N_\rho^{*}/\mathcal M^0(-\bar j)\overset{?}{\simeq}\mathcal G^{\wedge}/\Pi_0\), compatible with the embeddings of \(\mathbb D_\rho\). This is then promoted to a proposition using a concrete composite map on scan 643. The compatibility requirement is part of the proposed identification, not merely an equality of group orders.

#### R643.1 — Scan 643, Proposition, (45)–(46)

**Kind: claim whose proof is unfinished in the supplied pages.** The proposition says that the induced homomorphism “a comme noyau \(\mathcal M^0(-\bar j)\)” and hence gives the quotient isomorphism (46). Its proof starts by writing elements as \(\alpha^{-1}u\) with conditions on \(u(\rho)\), \(\alpha(\rho)\), \(\varepsilon_2(u)\), and \(\varepsilon_3(u)\), but the supplied fragment ends at “L'image de/des”. To check the proof one must obtain the continuation or independently verify both the stated kernel and the image; neither is completed in the transcription.

#### R643.2 — Scan 643, congruence quotient in (45)

**Kind: own idea. Confidence: medium.** Build the finite map in (45) explicitly, starting with the reduction to \(\operatorname{GL}(2,\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z)\), and compare the images of the subgroup generators from the diagrams. The reason is that (45) provides a concrete proposed route to the quotient rather than merely an abstract isomorphism claim. Such a check could clarify the degree-4 epimorphism and the compatibility with \(\mathbb D_\rho\), but it requires definitions and generators not supplied on these seven pages.

#### R643.3 — Scan 643, hats and the first right-hand superscript in (45)

**Kind: own idea. Confidence: low.** Before interpreting the completion symbols, compare this diagram with the preceding manuscript definitions of \(\mathcal G\), \(\mathcal G^{\wedge}\), and \(\Pi_0^{\wedge}\). The reason is that the top right-hand superscript in (45) is overwritten and star-like, whereas its lower equivalent quotient and the later canonical map visibly have hats. # LM_C3-644-662 — cote 140-3, scans 644–662  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_C3-644-662\LM_C3-644-662_notes.md]

## Research notes — English

These notes concern questions, tentative expectations, assertions left unproved here, and possible further checks suggested by this excerpt. The categories describe the status of the passage on these pages, not its status elsewhere in the manuscript or literature. Cancelled claims are identified as cancelled. Notes labelled **own idea** are proposed investigations with stated confidence and reasons, not amendments to the transcription.

### Scans 644–647

#### Research notes (English)

- **Scan 644, first diagram — unproved claim / question.** The bottom arrow is labelled “?”. The surrounding text reduces a kernel statement involving `M°(−j̄)` to the existence of a commutative factorization through `μ × μ`; checking the map requires the earlier definition (45), which is outside this package. The question mark is retained as a written uncertainty rather than interpreted as an asserted construction.
- **Scan 644, middle — unproved claim.** “n’est autre que ε₂” identifies the displayed composite with a sign character. A proof would need to compare that character with the reduction modulo 4 appearing in the diagram, keeping the overwritten stages distinct from the final arrows.
- **Scan 644, bottom — unproved claim.** “est donnée par ε₂(u)” refers the action computation to an earlier page. Checking the reference would require the earlier page, provisionally read as 554 (alternative 594), and the exact convention for the action induced by (45); these scans alone do not supply it.

##### Scan 645 research notes (English)

- **Scan 645, after the first diagram — conjecture / verification requested.** “il faudrait vérifier que cet hom … n’est autre que ε₃” explicitly leaves the identification to be checked. The inserted correction changes the proposed kernel, so the nearby canceled argument should not be used as an established proof of that identification.
- **Scan 645, insertion — unproved claim / deferred correction.** “le noyau n’est pas Ker(ε₃ | M″!) … mais M₀″!” is followed by “on va y revenir plus bas”. Establishing this correction would require the definitions of the decorated subgroups and a direct comparison of the homomorphism’s kernel with the sign character’s kernel. The exact lead-in and one canceled word are low-confidence readings.
- **Scan 645, canceled lower half — unproved claim in a discarded argument.** “il est donc 1, ou d’ordre 2” follows the trivial-intersection claim for the subgroup denoted Dρ. The canceled passage is worth checking as an index-two subgroup argument, but its canceled status and the correction above preclude treating it as a final assertion here.

##### Scan 646 research notes (English)

- **Scan 646, canceled proposition — unproved claim in a discarded formulation.** “induit … isomorphismes évidents sur les facteurs” asserts compatibility with two three-step filtrations. A proof would compare the maps on the two sign factors and the middle factor, then deduce the kernel; the diagonal cancellation and the revised kernel notation below must be respected when assessing the statement.
- **Scan 646, lower half — unproved claim.** “Admettant ce point” makes the ensuing kernel computation conditional on the preceding identification. The calculation intersects the corrected kernel with Nρ*; validating it requires the definitions of M₀″!, M₀!, and Zρ₀! from earlier pages.
- **Scan 646, last lines — unpursued implication.** “on a bien un hom injectif” uses the intersection computation to eliminate the residual kernel considered on the preceding page. The conclusion continues onto scan 647, where equal finite orders are invoked; the precise numbered reference is (46) or (45), not securely distinguished in the ink.

##### Scan 647 research notes (English)

- **Scan 647, opening continuation — unproved claim.** “ont même ordre 24” upgrades the preceding injective homomorphism to an isomorphism. The order count is not repeated here; checking it needs the preceding constructions and the exact group intended by the numbered map.
- **Scan 647, (49) and (52) — unproved claim.** The marked isomorphism from Zσ₀! to γρ,σ and the sequence labelled “exacte” summarize assertions cited at pages 615 and 616. A full proof would verify that the displayed homomorphisms have the stated image and kernel, using the original normalization and central-subgroup conventions.
- **Scan 647, (48)–(52) — own idea.** The displayed isomorphism and central extension suggest testing whether this fiber-product construction can be reconstructed as a pullback of the second sequence along the first map. **Confidence: medium**, because the fiber products and maps are visible, but the definitions of their common quotient and all structural maps are not given in full on this page. This is a proposed verification, not a claim of novelty or an established result.

### Scans 648–652

#### Research notes (English; separate from the transcription)

##### 648-R1 — Unproved claim — scan 648, lower quarter, before the second (55)

“Il est clair alors par (52)” introduces the asserted exact sequence with kernel `\mu_\rho`. A proof would need to check the kernel and surjectivity of the projection from the fibre-product subgroup defined in (53), with the exact maps of (52), rather than infer exactness merely from the displayed inclusions.

##### 648-R2 — Unpursued implication — scan 648, (54)–(55)

The phrase “plongement central” and the displayed intersection select two of the three central sign factors inside the distinguished subgroup. It is worth tracking how each of those two factors survives the later quotient by `\mu_\rho`; the intersection identity alone does not identify their subsequent roles.

No proposal is presented as established or as new, and none was used to repair the transcription.

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

The following notes distinguish authorial questions, assertions whose proof is absent or deferred at this point, unpursued consequences, and explicitly labelled proposed investigations. They are not corrections to the transcription, claims of novelty, or reports of a literature search. All quotations and scan-specific assertions refer to the supplied manuscript (Grothendieck, 1981). A later passage may settle an item recorded here.

A proof would have to establish that each of the four displayed requirements is stable under multiplication and inversion; the uncertainty in the stabilised object in (107)d should be resolved before formalising this particular formulation.

# LM_C4-001-019 — cote 140-4, scans 1–19  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_C4-001-019\LM_C4-001-019_notes.md]

## 4. Research notes — separate from the transcription

These items distinguish the author’s questions and unfinished claims from unpursued implications and the transcriber’s own ideas. A later treatment elsewhere in the manuscript is not presumed to resolve an item unless that treatment is actually within the supplied pages.

### Scans 1–4

#### R01 — Scan 3, §51.11–15 — unpursued implication

The contents advertise “position du problème,” “Scindages de l’extension,” “jacobiennes généralisées,” and “extensions Kummériennes.” These are leads for checking how the integral group-scheme constructions in §50 are used later; the present package does not contain the advertised arguments, so no conclusion about their validity or completion can be drawn from these entries.

#### R02 — Scan 4, revised §52 heading — unpursued implication

The replacement heading reads “Approximations de Lie des systèmes de Galois-Teichmüller,” while the cancelled heading concerns schematic envelopes of L- and Pi-groups. The revision motivates a later comparison of these constructions, but a contents-page change alone does not establish an equivalence between them.

#### R03 — Scan 4, §53.1 — unproved claim

The entry explicitly labels the announced action “énoncé provisoire.” Its actual hypotheses, formulation, and proof must be checked in the later section; none is supplied by this table of contents.

### Scans 5–9

These observations use the supplied scans only. They distinguish questions and provisional statements in the manuscript from proposed follow-up work; no claim of novelty or literature priority is intended.

1. **Scan 5, ll. 14–20 — unproved claim.** The assertion beginning “On voit que si \(S\) est quasi-compact” passes from a fiberwise quasi-unipotence condition to a single positive integer exponent over the base. A proof should identify precisely which finite-presentation or constructibility input makes the exponent uniform, rather than using quasi-compactness alone without an open-cover argument.

2. **Scan 5, canceled paragraph near the foot — unproved claim, canceled formulation.** A preliminary “Théorème” involving a group scheme locally of finite presentation over a quasi-compact base is struck out before the surviving sufficiency statement. The cancellation and the uncertain end of its wording matter: this passage should be tracked as an abandoned formulation, not quoted as a proved theorem.

3. **Scan 6, ll. 3–5 — conjecture/question.** “Je me demande si c'est aussi nécessaire” asks whether a fiberwise unipotent section must come from a global homomorphism \(\mathbb G_a\to G\) taking \(1\) to that section, at least in suitable “bons” cases. The following pages begin to separate the characteristic-zero field case from extension over an arithmetic base.

4. **Scan 6, ll. 6–12 — unproved claim.** The “résultat d'unicité pour \(\varphi\)” in characteristic zero is used to invoke descent. A complete argument needs both uniqueness after base change and the resulting compatibility on the double overlap; it should also specify the class of group schemes for which the uniqueness statement holds.

5. **Scan 6, ll. 13–18 — unpursued implication.** The displayed example \(x\mapsto x^p-x\) shows why evaluation at \(1\) cannot by itself determine an additive-group homomorphism in positive characteristic. The proposed restriction to maps that are “mono” shifts the problem toward uniqueness of the embedded subgroup, a logically different question from uniqueness of its parameterization.

6. **Scan 6, ll. 19–24 — conjecture/question.** The manuscript asks whether a subgroup isomorphic to \(\mathbb G_a\) is determined by “une section partout non triviale,” and then whether this holds over a field. The quantifier on the base and the distinction between a fixed section and a full infinitesimal parameter should be preserved in any comparison with later results.

7. **Scan 6, after the subgroup question — own idea.** A candidate test in characteristic \(p\) is to compare the two graphs \(t\mapsto(t,0)\) and \(t\mapsto(t,t^p-t)\) inside \(\mathbb G_a^2\); both contain the nonzero section \((1,0)\), and the first projection supplies their parameterization. **Confidence: high as an algebraic test**, because Frobenius makes the second coordinate additive and the graph polynomials differ; this is proposed for checking the exact formulation, not as a novelty claim.

8. **Scan 7, ll. 4–13 — unproved claim.** The statement “il existe un ouvert \(U\) non vide” and the subsequent largest open of definition use spreading out and gluing by uniqueness. A proof should explain how finite presentation produces a homomorphism over an open, and why its homomorphism identity and prescribed value at \(1\) also spread out.

9. **Scan 7, ll. 14–22 — unproved claim.** “quitte à localiser en un pt maximal” reduces the extension problem to a local base, and regularity in dimension one then yields a trait. The reduction is worth checking separately from the later trait calculation, since generalization to higher-dimensional or nonregular bases would require additional arguments.

10. **Scan 8, ll. 4–8 — unproved claim.** The schematic closure of the generic one-parameter subgroup is described as “un sous-schém. en groupes réduit.” A detailed treatment should verify the group law on the closure, the role of the trait hypothesis, and the relationship between reducedness of the closure and reducedness of its special fiber.

11. **Scan 8, ll. 8–10 — conjecture/expectation.** The proposed sufficient route is to show \(L^0\simeq\mathbb G_{aS}\), immediately accompanied by doubt that the special neutral component is reduced. This identifies a geometric obstacle to a naive closure argument, before the manuscript switches to the matrix calculation.

12. **Scan 8, ll. 11–18 — conjecture/expectation.** The possibility that a generic parameterization specializes to a nonmonomorphism, or even “l'hom trivial,” is explicitly left open. Consequently the existence of an extending homomorphism and the assertion that the neutral component of its image is an additive-group model should not be treated as equivalent without proof.

13. **Scan 8, discussion of a trivial special-fiber map — own idea.** The scaling map \(t\mapsto\pi t\) on \(\mathbb G_a\) over a trait is a simple example to test against the statement about degeneration of a parameterization: it is nonzero on the generic fiber and zero on the special fiber. **Confidence: high for this test**, because additivity and reduction modulo \(\pi\) are explicit; it illustrates the proposed distinction without claiming to settle every hypothesis used for \(L\).

14. **Scan 9, equations (8)–(10) — unproved claim.** The extension problem for the linear group is reformulated as integrality of the individual divided-power coefficients \(X^i/i!\). A proof should compare polynomial matrix coefficients and preserve the distinction between coefficientwise integrality and merely having both \(\exp(X)\) and \(\exp(-X)\) integral.

15. **Scan 9, ll. 14–19 — unproved claim.** The discussion treats the cases \(n=2\) and \(n=3\) as elementary before moving to \(n=4\); the tiny underlined word after \(n=3\) is itself uncertain. Any verification must retain the original fiberwise hypothesis from scan 5 in addition to the displayed matrix conditions, rather than replacing the manuscript's problem by a weaker integrality-only problem.

16. **Scan 9, equations (11)–(12) — conjecture/question.** “on se demande s'il en résulte” asks whether integrality of the two indicated combinations forces integrality of their individual summands. The text then singles out the case where \(2\) is invertible, leaving the residue-characteristic-two difficulty for the continuation.

17. **Scan 9, equations (9)–(12) — own idea.** As a diagnostic step, derive the odd and even parts of the truncated exponential directly from \(\exp(X)\) and \(\exp(-X)\), and compare every retained term with (11). **Confidence: high that this is a useful check**, because addition and subtraction isolate the two parities; the calculation belongs in the research apparatus and must not silently supply or remove terms in the transcription.

### Scans 10–14

1. **Scan10, (11 bis)–(12 bis) and paragraph beginning “Pour en avoir le coeur net” — conjecture.** Grothendieck asks whether the integrality of two signed combinations of divided powers forces the separate integrality conditions he writes in (12 bis), and says that one needs “un contreexemple … ou un théorème !”. The residual-characteristic-two, nilpotence-order-four case remains a question at this point. The second coefficient in the written (12 bis) is 1/2 and must be checked as part of the mathematical question, independently of what an edited statement might become.

### Additional editorial research notes (English)

These items are the transcriber's mathematical observations, separate from the diplomatic text. They are not attributed to Grothendieck and make no claim of novelty. All of their source locations refer to the supplied scans; the two modern bibliographic leads below were consulted only for the notes.

#### E01 — Scan 5, definition before (1); scan 9, conditions (8)–(10) — own idea

The wording “est unipotent, i.e. s'il existe un hom de groupes” should be compared carefully with the usual linear-group definition: in characteristic $p$, an element in the image of $\mathbb G_a$ has order dividing $p$, whereas a unipotent Jordan block can have larger $p$-power order (compare Milne, 2022, §14.27). Thus the displayed parameterization is a substantive extra condition in positive characteristic, unless a special convention is intended here. In testing the subsequent matrix reductions, retain this fiberwise condition in addition to integrality of $\exp(X)$ and $\exp(-X)$. **Confidence: high**, because the additive group of a field of characteristic $p$ is killed by $p$; the interpretation of Grothendieck's terminology remains a question for the wider manuscript.

#### E02 — Scan 6, question about monomorphisms and a nontrivial section — own idea

For the question beginning “Un sous-groupe de $G$”, test $G=\mathbb G_a^2$ over a field of characteristic $p>0$: the two homomorphisms $t\mapsto(t,0)$ and $t\mapsto(t,t^p-t)$ are distinct closed immersions and both take $1$ to the nonzero point $(1,0)$. Their images are different copies of $\mathbb G_a$, so specifying that point does not determine the subgroup, even over a field. **Confidence: high**, since $t^p-t$ is additive and the first coordinate gives an inverse from each image to $\mathbb G_a$; this is an explicit test of the proposed uniqueness route, not a claim about what Grothendieck proves later.

#### E03 — Scans 6–10, necessity without taking a power — own idea

For “Je me demande si c'est aussi nécessaire”, try the ramified discrete valuation ring $A=\mathbb Z_2[\pi]$, $\pi^2=2$, and $g=I+N\in\mathrm{Gl}_3(A)$ with $N=E_{12}+\pi E_{23}$: its generic fiber has the usual exponential parameterization, and its special fiber is $I+E_{12}$, hence also is the value at $1$ of a $\mathbb G_a$-homomorphism. However, $\log(g)=N-(\pi/2)E_{13}$ has a nonintegral entry, so the uniqueness of the generic-fiber parameterization $t\mapsto\exp(t\log g)$ prevents it from extending over $A$ with value $g$ at $1$ (Milne, 2022, §14.29). This does not obstruct the power statement: $\exp(2t\log g)=I+t(2N-\pi E_{13})+2\pi t^2E_{13}$ has integral coefficients and takes $1$ to $g^2$. **Confidence: high for this explicit calculation**, because $N^2=\pi E_{13}$, $N^3=0$, and $\pi/2=1/\pi$; the example is offered for checking against the rest of the manuscript, with no novelty claim.

#### E04 — Scan 13, (18)–(19), and scans 14–16, scaling argument — own idea

An explicit bound may supplement “il existe un entier $d>0$”: if $X^r=0$ and an integer $D>0$ satisfies $DX\in M_n(A)$, then $d=D(r-1)!$ gives $d^iX^i/i!\in M_n(A)$ for $0\le i<r$. If $X=\log(g)$ for an integral unipotent matrix $g$ in characteristic zero with $(g-I)^r=0$, one may take $D=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,r-1)$. **Confidence: high under these stated matrix hypotheses**, because the logarithm is a finite polynomial and $i!$ divides $(r-1)!$; this does not supply the manuscript's deferred reduction for arbitrary group schemes or nonreduced bases.

## 5. Research notes — separate from the transcription

These notes record questions or obligations visible at the point where they arise, even when a subsequent page begins to address them. Quotations reproduce the proposed reading and inherit its uncertainty marks where applicable. The notes do not settle uncertain manuscript readings. Items labelled **own idea** are suggestions for checking or further work, with confidence and reasons; they are not claims of established results or novelty. Cross-references to sections outside the supplied scans have not been verified.

Manuscript wording: “localement de la forme” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 39).

The locality of the two displayed expressions deserves separate attention: replacing local choices of alpha_0 and beta_0 by global parameters may introduce gluing or torsor data. These pages should be checked for the topology intended by “localement” before identifying sectionwise images with sheaf images.

The middle product in the displayed computation of eta appears without the inverse on sigma(beta_0) that occurs in the definition of eta_0. Compare the same computation elsewhere in the manuscript; the transcription retains the visible absence rather than resolving it algebraically. (Source location: Grothendieck, 1981, scan 39.)

Manuscript wording: “groupe (si possible...)” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 40).

The parenthetical “si possible...” explicitly leaves the existence of a group structure on the proposed systems open at this point. Later formulas in this packet should be checked as a possible answer, particularly their dependence on characteristics 2 and 3.

Keeping the equality between the two half-parameters separate may retain data lost by multiplying it by 2. This is an interpretive question, not a correction to the written relations or to (67)b.

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** The first equality for mu is twice the displayed half-parameter equality, while the construction retains formal N[lambda] notation.


### Scan 52

**R32 — unproved claim; paragraph immediately after (68).**

Manuscript wording: “on vérifie que c’est” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 52).

Compatibility with (67)b, biadditivity, commutativity, associativity and the stated unit are asserted without the calculations being written here. The final lambda product in (68) is uncertain, and no extra N is visible before it; the transcription therefore preserves the visible expression rather than repairing it.

**Confidence:** high. **Reason:** The prose explicitly lists properties to verify; the displayed multiplication is the only local formula offered.

**R33 — unpursued implication; generalization after (68) and diagrams (69)–(70).**

Manuscript wording: “Soit plus généralement” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 52).

The revisions replace a principal ideal NA by a two-sided ideal J free of finite type over Z. This suggests a general construction of an algebra object from the extension 0→J→A→B→0. Its functoriality with respect to maps of pairs (A,J), and its behaviour when base change introduces torsion, are not developed on this page.

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** The crossed principal-ideal wording and added bilatère/finite-type conditions make the widening of scope visible; later pages must be checked before classifying the question as globally unpursued.

**R34 — own idea; (68) compared with previous (67)b.**

Manuscript wording: “N[nλ′+n′λ+λλ′]” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 52).

Check the multiplication against the map represented in (67)b by n+N[lambda]↦n+Nlambda. Literal multiplication of the scalar images produces an N-squared cross term, whereas the visible (68) has only the outer N. This may reflect an omitted factor or a convention not supplied locally; it must remain an audit question, not an emendation.

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** The comparison is an elementary symbolic calculation, but the last handwritten factor and the intended formal-bracket convention remain uncertain.


### Scan 53

**R35 — unproved claim; (72)–(73).**

Manuscript wording: “on trouve une suite exacte” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 53).

The passage from the exact sequence of ring schemes (71) to the exact sequence of unit groups (72) is stated without a local lifting argument here. A proof would have to specify the topology in which the rightmost map is surjective and verify the scheme-theoretic identification of its kernel with the invertible elements of 1+J.

**R36 — unpursued implication; (73).**

Manuscript wording: “λ+λ′+λλ′=0” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 53).

The displayed inverse-pair equation gives a concrete model for the kernel and suggests an explicit representability check. Its relation to the ring multiplication and its behaviour under base change can be tested directly from the preceding construction, without presuming that J is nilpotent.


### Scan 54

**R37 — unpursued implication; lines 9–15.**

Manuscript wording: “ni examiner les limites projectives” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 54).

Grothendieck explicitly postpones the structure of the projective systems and their projective limits, including the corresponding construction for a general A. The transition maps, the topology for taking the limit, and representability of the resulting object are therefore points to check beyond these pages.

**R38 — unproved claim; (76), following text.**

Manuscript wording: “n’est ni épi, ni mono” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 54).

The canonical map to G_m is asserted to fail in general to be both an epimorphism and a monomorphism. A proof or counterexample analysis must make the chosen sheaf topology explicit, and separate the functor-of-points kernel from any failure of local surjectivity.

**R39 — unproved claim; (77).**

Manuscript wording: “en tant que schéma (sans structure de groupe)” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 54).

The kernel is identified as a scheme with the N-torsion of G_a, while the parenthesis deliberately withholds identification of the group laws. Checking the coordinate map and computing the induced multiplication would clarify exactly what survives as a group-scheme statement.


### Scan 55

**R40 — unproved claim; lines 1–4.**

Manuscript wording: “non plat si N≠1” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 55).

The N-torsion additive scheme is said to vanish after inverting N and to have G_a fibres at primes dividing N, hence to be nonflat for N≠1. The coordinate-ring verification is not supplied here; it would also need the previously stated range of N and the precise base S_0.

**R41 — unpursued implication; lines 5–8.**

Manuscript wording: “une maladresse de sortir du groupe” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 55).

Grothendieck reconsiders replacing the constructed unit group by G_m and elects to retain the N-dependent group. The comment suggests that the residue and kernel data are part of the intended structure; “parfait en son genre” should not be read as an assertion that the group is perfect in the algebraic sense.

**R42 — own idea; (79)–(81).**

Clarify the nature of μ before comparing these character maps in characteristic 2: the constant group of two signs and the group scheme of square roots of unity have different fibres there. The displayed conversion to {0,1}_S0 makes this a useful notation audit, rather than an identification to assume. (Source location: Grothendieck, 1981, scan 55.)

**Confidence:** high. **Reason:** The page explicitly passes from the unit group of a finite ring to a constant two-element scheme, while μ itself is not redefined on this page.


### Scan 56

**R43 — own idea; (82)–(83).**

Audit the off-diagonal entries in table (82) against (83). With ε2 as the column label and ε3 as the row label, the visible table gives +5 at (ν2,ν3)=(1,0), whereas the visible formula (−5)^ν2(+5)^ν3 gives −5; the opposite off-diagonal is reversed too. Both readings have been retained without correction. (Source location: Grothendieck, 1981, scan 56.)

**Confidence:** high. **Reason:** The diagonal heading labels, off-diagonal signs, exponents, and mod 4/mod 6 congruences are individually visible in enlarged inspection.

**R44 — unproved claim; below (82), before (83).**

Manuscript wording: “une section ensembliste de (79)” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 56).

The proposed section is explicitly only a section of underlying sets/schemes, not asserted to respect the group law. Verifying it requires reconciling its residue characters with the preceding table and checking the intended functorial interpretation of the idempotent sign coordinates.

**R45 — own idea; (83)–(85).**

Compute the multiplication defect of the chosen representatives μ0 to describe the extension in (79) by an explicit cocycle. The canceled simpler representative μ0′ differs from the final expression by a multiple of 12, suggesting a change of kernel coordinate rather than a new residue choice. (Source location: Grothendieck, 1981, scan 56.)

**Confidence:** medium. **Reason:** The page supplies a set-theoretic section and an explicit correction coordinate, but neither a group-law calculation nor a claim that the section is multiplicative appears here.

**R46 — unpursued implication; margin NB; power calculations.**

Manuscript wording: “ν2=ν2²” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 56).

The idempotence remark makes the polynomial expansions meaningful for locally varying sign coordinates. A later verification should retain the distinction between a binary constant-scheme section and an arbitrary element of the base ring, especially on disconnected bases.


### Scan 57

**R47 — own idea; initial display; (86)–(87); equality before proposition; (89).**

Check the mixed-term coefficients before using these displayed formulas in a reconstructed proof. The initial expression and (89) give a −24ν2ν3 term, whereas the visible 3ν2ν3 and 2ν2ν3 terms in (86)–(87) yield different coefficients after multiplication by 4 and 6; the following two-row equality uses −6ν2ν3 on both sides. The overwritten sign in (86) is separately uncertain, and no coefficient has been corrected in the transcription. (Source location: Grothendieck, 1981, scan 57.)

**Confidence:** high. **Reason:** The coefficients 3, 2, 4, 6, and the final 12(ν0−2ν2ν3) are visible; the observation is a direct comparison of the printed algebra, not a proposed emendation.

**R48 — unpursued implication; paragraph below (87).**

Manuscript wording: “le souligné dans μ désigne la section” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 57).

The author explicitly distinguishes a section of the constructed unit group from its image in G_m by underlining. A functor-of-points account should preserve this distinction, since earlier pages note that the map to G_m is not generally a monomorphism; replacing all underlined sections by scalar units can lose information.

**R49 — unproved claim; insertion before proposition.**

Manuscript wording: “le schéma en groupe lisse” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 57).

The proposition refers to the constructed O_12* as smooth. A proof should identify its components and coordinate charts over the stated base, rather than infer smoothness only from its scalar image or from the two residue characters.

**R50 — unproved claim; (88)–(89), last line.**

Manuscript wording: “une section ν0 bien déterminée” (Grothendieck, 1981, scan 57).

The final normal form asserts uniqueness of the additive correction coordinate ν0. Verification must use the constructed ring scheme, where 12[ν0] is a structural coordinate, rather than cancel 12 in an arbitrary base ring; existence must also respect the sign-coordinate conditions and the displayed unit condition.

These research notes are separate from the transcription and the reading apparatus. They identify questions, unfinished verifications, implications, and explicitly labelled suggestions prompted by these leaves. They do not assert that an issue remains open elsewhere in the manuscript or literature, or that a suggested direction is new.
