## 5. Research notes — English

These notes are separate from the diplomatic text. Each scan reference cites the supplied manuscript (Grothendieck, 1981); short quotations anchor comments to the visible wording. “Unproved claim” means that the indicated step is not proved at that location in the supplied passage, even when it may follow from earlier work or be addressed later. Proposed investigations and conditional calculations are not assertions of novelty or corrections to the transcription.

1. **Scan 229, proposition — unpursued implication.** The assertion « homéomorphe à R³ » would imply contractibility, and hence vanishing of all positive-dimensional homotopy groups, of the displayed covering group. This is a consequence to check against the precise covering construction, not an alteration of the proposition.

2. **Scan 229, (13) — own idea.** The extension over the group with determinant ±1 should be examined as an extension with a possibly nontrivial action on its infinite cyclic kernel. Confidence: high as a question to investigate, because the disconnected group and the later reflection formulas make the coefficient action consequential; this note does not assert centrality.

3. **Scan 230, proof of the proposition — unproved claim.** « s'identifie topologiquement à l'inclusion » of the unit circle into its product with R² is used without a construction on this page. One would want an explicit parametrization of Sl(2,R), a check of the embedded circle, and then an application of the lifting classification.

4. **Scan 230, Cor. 1 — unproved claim.** The assertion “est ≃ Z” for the inverse image of a finite cyclic subgroup includes a uniquely normalized generator. The next scan develops a closely related claim, but on this page the conjugacy-to-rotations and normalization steps have not yet been written out.

5. **Scan 230, Cor. 2 — unproved claim.** « L'action d'un g » of determinant −1 is asserted to invert the kernel generator and the central generator. A proof needs a lift of a reflection and a computation of its action on a full turn; extending from one reflection to every determinant −1 element also requires an argument.

6. **Scan 230, last exponential condition — own idea.** Compare the written membership sign with the intended typing of u as a point of the unit circle, while keeping the original sign in the transcription. Confidence: high that a typographical/handwriting issue warrants review, because the immediately preceding display identifies u with the complex number u(1); no correction is asserted.

7. **Scan 231, “Je voudrais décrire” — conjecture / question.** « Je voudrais décrire ... par générateurs et relations » states the aim of obtaining a presentation of the lifted integral matrix group. Later pages in this packet address that aim; its occurrence here is retained as a research item.

8. **Scan 231, last paragraph — unproved claim.** « par conjugaison SPS » suppresses the justification that a finite cyclic subgroup of Sl(2,R) can be placed in the displayed rotation subgroup. A proof would need a conjugating real basis, with attention to the determinant of the change of basis and the chosen orientation.

9. **Scan 231, proposition — unpursued implication.** The assertion “est isomorphe à Z” about the inverse images of the order-six and order-four subgroups supplies candidates for an amalgamated presentation. The actual amalgamation and compatibility of central generators need the subsequent relations; they do not follow solely from the cyclicity assertion.

10. **Scan 232, (17)–(18) — own idea.** The displayed operation uses exponents +2n and +3n, whereas (17) equates rho-tilde cubed with sigma-tilde to the power −2. Under a central infinite-order omega-prime, the two sides acquire factors omega-prime to +6n and −6n respectively; a sign check is therefore necessary before using this as a torsor action. Confidence: high in the conditional calculation; the transcript retains both positive exponents as written.

11. **Scan 232, lower-right margin — conjecture / question.** « Faire la vérification » explicitly leaves a verification to be performed near the normalization formulas (20). A verification should establish existence and uniqueness of the indicated lifts and compatibility with the chosen omega_0, rather than infer them from a preferred presentation.

12. **Scan 232, “il vaut mieux dire” margin — unproved claim.** The note asserts a unique generator of each cyclic inverse image lying above the selected rho or sigma, followed by relations (20). Proving this requires knowing how each integral matrix sits in its finite cyclic subgroup and which sign of the infinite cyclic generator projects to it.

13. **Scan 232, (19)–(20) — own idea.** Track omega_0, which lies over the central order-two subgroup, separately from omega-prime_0, the kernel generator, throughout the later group presentations. Confidence: high as a useful consistency check, because (19) explicitly makes the former a square root of the latter and changing their roles changes the extension.

14. **Scan 233, “cette extension est scindée” — unpursued implication.** The order-two lift constructed in (21) gives a splitting over the chosen reflection subgroup. Together with the inversion action from the preceding corollary, this invites an explicit semidirect-product description of that preimage; the extension's multiplication should be checked before carrying the description to the full integral group.

15. **Scan 233, (22)–(23) — own idea.** Verify the formulas against the stated parametrization z = exp(2iπt), keeping the manuscript's written expressions separate from the check. For a reflection z ↦ i times the conjugate of z, this parametrization gives the candidate lift t ↦ 1/4 − t modulo integers; the fixed parameter is 1/8, which may help explain—but does not resolve—the overwritten fraction and the extra 2iπ in (23). Confidence: high in this conditional calculation, low in any claim about the author's intended correction.

16. **Scan 233, beginning “Ceci résulte” — unproved claim.** « Ceci résulte ... aussitôt de la prop. précédente » leaves the passage from cyclic inverse images to the unique normalized rho- and sigma-lifts implicit. A proof should separate uniqueness of a generator with specified projection from compatibility of its powers with the selected central generator.

17. **Scan 234, theorem (25); kind: unpursued implication.** The displayed relation “$\widetilde\rho^3\cdot\widetilde\sigma^2=1$” gives a natural route to comparison with a two-generator one-relator group of type $(3,2)$. Any such identification must track the inverse on one generator and distinguish the kernel of the map to $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb Z)$ from the larger kernel of the map to its quotient by $\{\pm1\}$. This is a question for a separate algebraic comparison; no normalization has been made in the transcription.

18. **Scan 234, proof after (24); kind: unproved claim.** “il suffit de montrer que les premiers mbs satisfont les relations caractéristiques (20)” invokes uniqueness of lifts characterized by their powers. A full verification would identify the discrete central kernel and show that the relevant power constraints determine the lift uniquely.

19. **Scan 235, proof between (27) and Corollaire 1; kind: unproved claim.** “en induisant des iso identiques sur les facteurs extrêmes” is the decisive step of the comparison of exact sequences. Because the first displayed sequence does not explicitly begin with an injection, a detailed proof should verify infinite order of the abstract central element, or derive injectivity from its image in the second sequence, before invoking the comparison argument.

20. **Scan 235, final paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** “Je vais essayer de présenter le … groupe … avec trois générateurs involutifs” announces a second presentation to be constructed on the following pages. The algebraic task is to verify that the proposed involutions generate and that substituting them into (28) introduces neither extra relations nor an unintended quotient.

21. **Scan 236, opening paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** “engendrent un groupe isomorphe à $D_\infty$” is asserted for three pairs of elements. A verification must show that the rotation-like generator in each pair has infinite order and that conjugation by the indicated involution reverses it; the second property follows from the preceding formulas, whereas the first depends on the covering-group construction.

22. **Scan 236, (31)–(32); kind: unpursued implication.** The displayed “somme amalgamée de groupes” gives a route to normal forms and to an action on the tree associated with an amalgam. One could use that action to compare finite subgroups and involutions of the extended covering group; this is a research direction, not a classification established in these pages.

23. **Scan 236, (33); kind: unproved claim.** “Or on peut prendre … les générateurs involutifs” introduces the substitutions needed for the next corollary. A complete derivation should check that each proposed product squares to the identity and express the former generators back in terms of the new ones before transforming the defining relation.

24. **Scan 237, Corollaire 2 and (34); kind: unproved claim.** “admet une présentation (à trois générateurs involutifs …)” states the final presentation without a new proof on this sheet. Its proof is the elimination/substitution argument suggested by (33); an independent check should confirm the order of the factors in both products, since switching either pair replaces the associated element by its inverse.

25. **Scan 237, (34); kind: own idea. Confidence: medium.** Treat the product relation as a relation among three reflections and compare it with quotients obtained by separately setting the cubic and square factors equal to the identity. The reason to explore this is that the manuscript retains only their product as a relation, so those quotients may clarify precisely which central information the covering group keeps; no novelty or established identification is claimed.

26. **Scan 238, (37) and the sentence immediately following; kind: unproved claim.** “dont on sait que c’est un isomorphisme” invokes the identification of the mapping-class group of the once-punctured torus with the integral linear group. A complete argument should separate surjectivity, obtained from explicit mapping classes, from injectivity of the homology representation and should state whether orientation-reversing homeomorphisms are included.

27. **Scan 238, final paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** “l’action sur l’espace tangent s’identifie à l’action tautologique” is used to compare two extension constructions. The required verification is that the tangent action at the fixed origin, with its chosen orientation convention, induces the same action on the covering of directions as the linear representation; the announced conclusion continues on the next scan.

28. **Scan 238, notation between (36) and (37); kind: own idea. Confidence: high.** Audit the occurrence U_{1,0} against the surrounding definition U_{1,1}=X_1 minus {0} before using the argument in a later proof. The reason is the explicit mismatch on this page, not an assumption about which expression the author intended; the transcription deliberately leaves U_{1,0} unchanged.

29. **Scan 239, lines 6–10 — unproved claim.** The theorem states that the inverse image of the extension “s'identifie canoniquement” with `Gl(2,Z)^~`, referring back to the proposition on manuscript page 761. On this page the identification is asserted through that earlier reference; checking it would require tracking the extension kernel, its chosen generator, and the orientation convention in the preceding paragraph.

30. **Scan 239, lines 15–17 — conjecture / author question.** The parenthetical “(judicieusement ?)” explicitly questions the choice of a base point for computing the fundamental group. The subsequent lattice construction should be checked to see which choices make the actions of the displayed generators easiest to express.

31. **Scan 239, (39) — unproved claim.** The displayed identification involving “Aut ext” is stated without an argument on this page. A verification would need a precise interpretation of the handwritten `loc` subscript and a proof that the relevant peripheral structure is exactly the one preserved by the indicated automorphisms.

32. **Scan 239, presentations a), b) — own idea.** **Confidence: medium.** Once the cancellations have been resolved paleographically, compare the two presentations by substituting the involution products into the first presentation and checking each relation directly. This would detect a sign or inverse mismatch without allowing the algebra to dictate what the manuscript says; the reason for the suggestion is the dense overstriking in both displayed relations.

33. **Scan 240, (41) — unproved claim.** The statement “on aura” identifies `S T_{1,1}` with a normalizer of the cyclic subgroup generated by the boundary loop. A proof must specify whether the subgroup itself or its conjugacy class is fixed, and check the corresponding change from outer automorphisms to actual automorphisms.

34. **Scan 240, lines 6–16 — unproved claim / deferred calculation.** “Donc il faudrait expliciter l'action” announces a calculation of the displayed generators on `x` and `y`; no such formulas are supplied on this page. The required check is that the resulting automorphisms satisfy the presentations and carry the peripheral generator to itself or its inverse according to the stated cases.

35. **Scan 240, lines 10–13 — unproved claim.** The requirement “transformer” the peripheral generator into itself or its inverse is stated for the indicated generators: preserve `l′_0` for `rho~` and `sigma~`, and invert it for the involutions. Establishing this requires following the orientation of the peripheral loop through each geometric representative, including the paths used to return the base point.

36. **Scan 240, last paragraph — unpursued implication.** The “revêtement principal” with group `Z^2` offers a way to represent noncommutativity of the punctured-torus group as winding around deleted lattice points. The next page begins the relative-path description, but a full generator-action calculation remains to be extracted from that model.

37. **Scan 241, (42)–(44) — unproved claim.** The “iso. can.” and the exact sequence are stated through a mixed fundamental-group construction, and the path-pair calculation is credited to Jean Malgoire. A detailed verification should define the equivalence relation on pairs, the group multiplication and the injection of the fundamental group of the lattice complement.

38. **Scan 241, after (44) — unpursued implication.** The convention “compose comme les fonctions” fixes the order of multiplication for the path-pair model. This matters for every subsequent commutator and generator-action formula; a derivation must translate the geometric concatenation order into that convention explicitly.

39. **Scan 241, final paragraph and drawing — unproved claim.** The commutator loop is called “visiblement opposé” to the displayed peripheral loop. Its sign is argued pictorially here; a proof would compare the orientation of the square boundary with that of the radial loop while retaining the chosen multiplication convention.

40. **Scan 241, drawing — own idea.** **Confidence: high.** Independently compute the four endpoint displacements using `a=(1/2,1/2)` and compare them with every vertex label in the sketch. The visible `a-e_1` at the upper left and `a-e_0` at the lower right may reflect a local index interchange, because the nearby e_1 and e_0 lattice labels and the x/y arrows indicate the opposite coordinate displacements; this is an editorial check, not a correction to the transcription.

41. **Scan 241, (43) — own idea.** **Confidence: medium.** Use the plane with lattice points removed to construct generators for the kernel of the map to `Z^2`, then examine how deck translations move those generators. The reason is that (43) identifies the quotient with the abelianization and the sketch supplies a loop around one deleted point; extending the construction to every lattice point could make the kernel action explicit.

42. **Scan 242, after (46), unproved claim.** Grothendieck writes, “La composition des morphismes de germes est évidente.” A proof should show that representatives can be restricted so that they compose, and that the resulting germ is independent of those representatives and restrictions; the filter-compatibility condition is the relevant ingredient.

43. **Scan 242, (47) and final paragraph, conjecture / expectation.** The phrases “sans doute” and “au moins dans les ‘bons cas’” qualify the proposed interpretation of these coverings as coverings of a suitable limiting topos. The sentence continues on the next page; at this point the precise choice of topos and the hypotheses making the interpretation valid remain open.

44. **Scan 242, (47), own idea — medium confidence.** Clarify whether the displayed limit of categories is intended as a filtered 2-colimit and identify its objects and morphisms by eventual restriction. This is suggested by the analogous explicit limit of sets of morphisms in (46), but the categorical coherence data are not spelled out here.

45. **Scan 242, upper-left margin, own idea — medium confidence.** Work out the categorical role of the germ associated with the improper filter, which the note explicitly allows and calls “germe d’espace vide”. Domains can be shrunk to the empty set in that case; checking the resulting Hom sets would test the conventions against the proposed topos interpretation.

46. **Scan 243, upper-left margin; kind: conjecture/question.** The marginal question is tentatively read as “cela ne fait pas aller loin ?”; both substantive words remain doubtful. The point of the question cannot safely be identified more specifically than its position beside the proposed projective-limit description, and its wording should be settled before using it as evidence of a mathematical reservation.

47. **Scan 243, first paragraph; kind: unproved claim/expectation.** The category “dans les bons cas” “a tendance à être multigaloisienne, voire galoisienne.” A precise investigation would need to specify those good cases and establish the categorical axioms for the filtered category of coverings; the phrase itself supplies no hypotheses or proof.

48. **Scan 243, conditions 1° and 2°; kind: unproved claim.** The asserted reformulation beginning “Ce foncteur est pl. fidèle” uses eventual constancy on components and eventual triviality of induced exterior fundamental-group maps. A proof should state the local hypotheses under which coverings are classified by these groups and track the quantifier order; the inserted nonemptiness and containment conditions are part of the claim.

49. **Scan 243, condition 2°; kind: own idea.** Compare the condition with pro-triviality of a system of fundamental groups without interchanging the quantifiers over neighborhoods and coverings. **Confidence: medium**: the written condition requires one smaller neighborhood to kill the whole induced group map, whereas an individual covering might trivialize only after a smaller neighborhood depending on that covering; whether the two formulations agree needs checking in the intended category.

50. **Scan 244, first paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** The category of topological spaces “peut être considérée comme sous-catégorie pleine” of the category of germs by using the trivial filter. The associated assertion that the category of coverings restricts correctly to ordinary topological coverings needs an explicit comparison of the morphisms and pullback functors.

51. **Scan 244, (49)–(50); kind: unproved claim.** A morphism from a `1`-connected germ is used to produce a “foncteur fibre” and then `π_1` relative to it. The categorical construction should specify the needed exactness and detection properties of this functor in the multigaloisienne case, and the additional connectedness condition used for the subsequent equivalence of categories.

52. **Scan 244, bottom paragraph; kind: unpursued implication.** The explicit condition “Si X est 0-connexe” distinguishes recovery of the whole covering category from a base germ that selects a component. One can investigate how the construction varies between components without treating the single associated group as a description of the whole disconnected case.

53. **Scan 245, first paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** The assertion that the fundamental group “dépend fonctoriellement du triple” involves the morphism from the `1`-connected germ, not only its source and target objects. A proof should formulate morphisms between such triples and verify that the resulting homomorphisms are compatible with composition and with the chosen equivalence for constant coverings.

54. **Scan 245, residual-germ definition; kind: unproved claim.** “Il est vide ssi Y est ouvert” identifies when the residual filter becomes empty. The proof can be sought directly in the neighborhood-filter definition; it should keep the convention for an empty or improper filter explicit.

55. **Scan 245, NB sentence; kind: unpursued implication.** The assertion that the germ at a point is “tjrs 1-connexe” whereas the residual germ need not be isolates local punctured-neighborhood monodromy as the information retained by the latter. This suggests comparing local covering categories of ordinary and residual germs in concrete spaces, without inferring that the residual germ is always nontrivial.

56. **Scan 245, last assertion; kind: unproved claim.** “Tout germe d'espaces (S,Φ) peut s'interpréter” as a residual germ in `X=S∪{ω}` is stated without constructing the topology. A proof should specify neighborhoods of the added point and verify that their traces on `S` recover exactly the original filter up to germ equivalence.

57. **Scan 245, last assertion; kind: own idea.** Try adjoining `ω` with neighborhoods generated by `{ω}∪U`, where `U` runs through an open cofinal basis of `Φ`, while retaining the original open sets of `S`. **Confidence: high as a construction to check**, because it directly encodes the written filter; separation properties of the resulting space and any requirement of a proper filter must still be examined.

58. **Scan 246, middle paragraph; kind: unpursued implication.** “Je m'intéresse au choix d'un rev. universel” of the residual germ of a surface point identifies the local object motivating the digression. The role of a *choice* of universal covering, and the transformations between such choices, deserves comparison with the earlier lifted-group constructions without inserting that comparison into the transcription.

59. **Scan 246, lower paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** A covering represented over some `S_i∈Φ` defines a germ over the original germ that “ne dépend pas du choix” of representatives. A proof should pass to common refinements, construct the comparison morphisms, and establish their compatibility before obtaining the stated canonical functor.

60. **Scan 246, isomorphism parenthesis; kind: own idea.** Test the scope of “à isom unique près”: the intended uniqueness may concern the comparison induced by a *fixed* covering object and its refinements, rather than every isomorphism of the resulting germs. **Confidence: medium**, because coverings can have automorphisms, so an unqualified reading of uniqueness would need further structure; the inserted “au dessus de” may be relevant but by itself should not be treated as a proof.

61. **Scan 247, (54) and first paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** The canonical functor from coverings to germs over the base “est pleinement fidèle,” and its essential image defines an étale covering of the germ. A proof should check that every morphism of the resulting germs over the base descends to a morphism between covering representatives after a common refinement, not merely that covering morphisms induce germ morphisms.

62. **Scan 247, second paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** The `1`-connected objects are called universal coverings, and “ils forment un groupoïde, connexe ssi” the covering category is galoisienne. Establishing this requires both that morphisms between such objects are invertible and that the asserted connectedness criterion follows from the stated multigaloisienne hypothesis.

63. **Scan 247, bottom paragraph and formula; kind: unproved claim.** A universal covering “est bel et bien un germe d'espaces” that is `1`-connected, and the written formula identifies its associated fundamental group with its covering automorphism group. The comparison should be derived from the fiber functor and the full-faithfulness assertion, including the dependence on the chosen universal covering.

64. **Scan 247, vertical marginal note; kind: unpursued implication.** The note interprets the displayed group as the fundamental group of the “cat. multigaloisienne ‘abstraite’,” “calculé” at a `1`-connected object. This explicitly invites comparison of the geometric base-germ construction with the purely categorical one and of their behavior when several connected components are present.

65. **Scan 247, bottom formula; kind: own idea.** Audit the action and composition conventions in the comparison with the automorphism group of a universal covering; a representation by `Hom` can introduce an opposite-group convention. **Confidence: high that the convention must be checked, not that the written formula is wrong**, because the variance of the representing functor and the chosen left/right action determine the precise comparison.

### Literature checkpoints

66. **Scans 230–231, covering arguments; 243, conditions 1°–2° — own idea, literature checkpoint.** Compare the uses of covering classification with the hypotheses of Hatcher’s Theorem 1.38, which assumes path connectedness, local path connectedness, and semilocal simple connectedness (Hatcher, 2002, p. 67). **Confidence: high in the need for this check**, because a passage to germs or a filtered system does not by itself supply those hypotheses for every representative; this comparison is proposed only for the research argument.

67. **Scans 234–240, lifted presentations and peripheral automorphisms — own idea, literature checkpoint.** Use the braid-group and Dehn–Nielsen–Baer treatments in Farb and Margalit (2012) as comparison points for the presentation and for the distinction between outer automorphisms and automorphisms preserving a specified peripheral subgroup. **Confidence: medium**, because these pages also include orientation-reversing elements and a chosen lift, so any identification requires explicit choices of generators, action conventions, and central element.

68. **Scans 243–247, categorical reconstruction and final automorphism formula — own idea, literature checkpoint.** Compare the reconstruction discussion with SGA 1, Exposé V, §§4–5 and §9, while keeping its finite-set/profinite framework distinct from the category of coverings under consideration here (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 1971/2004). Section 5.1 explicitly discusses the opposite-group relationship between automorphisms of a fiber functor and of its representing pro-object. **Confidence: high that a variance check is required**, because the last formula on scan 247 identifies a fundamental group with a covering automorphism group; the citation supplies a convention to compare, not a correction of that formula.

## 5. Research notes — separate from the transcription

These observations are in English and do not amend the French transcription. “Unproved claim” identifies a proof obligation or an assertion whose full verification is not given at the cited location; it does not claim that Grothendieck never proves it elsewhere. Later construction within this excerpt may address an earlier announcement. Own ideas are proposed checks, not established results or claims of novelty. Brief quotations and scan/equation references refer throughout to Grothendieck (1981).

### Scans 248–252

These notes distinguish the source's assertions and expectations from proposed checks of my own. They are observations about these five pages only, not claims of priority or claims that the matters are unresolved elsewhere in the manuscript or literature. Citations refer to the supplied manuscript scans.

1. **Scan 248, equation (56) and the following paragraph — unproved claim.** The identification with the orientation module is supported by the sketch that the punctured disks' fundamental groups “forment un syst. projectif constant”. A full proof should specify a cofinal system of representative disks, verify the transition isomorphisms, and show that the identification with the orientation module is independent of the disk and respects reversal of orientation. The word transcribed as “canoniquement” remains a paleographical doubt.

2. **Scan 248, final complete paragraph — unproved claim.** The universal covers are said to “forment un groupoïde connexe”. To make this precise in the setting of germs, one would need existence of these covers, comparison isomorphisms after restriction, and the identification of the automorphism groups with the local orientation module; the source's phrase immediately before “fondamental” is itself uncertain between “groupoïde” and “groupe”.

3. **Scans 249–250, (60)–(61) and the section-functor formula — unproved claim.** Grothendieck announces “je vais définir un hom canonique”, then describes an action on sections of the pullback of a cover. A detailed verification should check naturality in the cover, compatibility with restriction of representatives of the germ, and the left/right action conventions that determine the direction of the induced homomorphism.

4. **Scans 250–251, (62)–(65) — unproved claim.** The chosen comparison of universal covers gives a homomorphism, while the source asserts that its choice-free result is “un hom ext. bien déterminé”. A proof should explicitly calculate how changing the comparison (62) changes the induced isomorphism (63) by conjugation, and then identify the resulting outer homomorphism with that induced by the inclusion of the punctured local germ into `U`.

5. **Scan 252, upper-left marginal note — conjecture (methodological expectation, not an asserted theorem).** The phrase “il serait plus commode pour la suite” proposes replacing the parameterized interval description by a germ of a subset of `X`, “satisfaisant à certaines propriétés”. The properties are not supplied in this note; recovering the intended restrictions and comparing the two descriptions is a concrete task left open here.

6. **Scan 252, (66)–(69), especially the final paragraph — unproved claim.** The text proposes to use the arc-germ morphism “pour définir un foncteur fibre”. A full argument should identify the interval-germ covering category with sets, prove that truncating the interval does not change the functor, and check that the passage from a continuous representative to its germ preserves the stated construction. The arrow in (69) from sets toward interval covers is part of the source and should be retained in such an account.

7. **Scan 251, (65) — own idea; confidence: high.** A useful check would compare `X = R², U = R² \ {0}` with `X = S², U = S² \ {x}`: the same cyclic local group should map very differently into the two global groups. This tests the important distinction between a canonical outer homomorphism and an asserted embedded peripheral subgroup; these pages assert the former and do not establish injectivity. The reason for high confidence is that the proposed examples reduce to elementary contractions of the corresponding punctured surfaces.

8. **Scan 252, marginal proposal and conditions (68) — own idea; confidence: medium.** Before replacing parameterized germs by subset germs, I would test continuous arcs with self-intersections or repeated excursions accumulating at the initial point, and compare them with embedded regular arcs. The displayed conditions require departure from `x` but do not visibly impose injectivity, so the image germ may omit order or multiplicity information carried by a parameterization. This is a proposed obstruction to investigate, not a claim that the constructions fail or that Grothendieck intended to include all such examples.

### Scan 253

- **Scan 253, equations (70)–(72) — unproved claim.** The words “on aura une factorisation” and “un iso can.” assert that an outgoing interval germ factors through its associated universal cover and that the two resulting based universal-cover constructions agree canonically. A proof would have to specify the category of germs and verify the universal properties, including independence from shortening the interval.
- **Scan 253, final paragraph — unpursued implication.** The definition beginning “un germe de courbe … est différentiable” introduces differentiability of the germ rather than a globally fixed representative. A check of invariance under changing representatives is needed before the construction can be used as a categorical source; the subsequent page supplies an additional tangency condition.

### Scan 254

- **Scan 254, equation (73) and following paragraph — unpursued implication.** The condition that the tangent map “est injective” assigns a nonzero tangent ray to the differentiable outgoing arc germ. The text does not here discuss invariance under orientation-preserving reparametrisation, which would be necessary if one later treats such germs as unparametrised arcs.
- **Scan 254, equations (74)–(75) — unproved claim.** After defining morphisms by isomorphisms of associated universal covers, the manuscript says “On trouve donc … une équivalence de … groupoïdes connexes.” Full faithfulness is built into (74), but essential surjectivity still requires every relevant universal cover to be represented by an outgoing arc germ, together with the local hypotheses guaranteeing connectedness.
- **Scan 254, equation (74) — own idea (confidence: medium).** Check separately the role of parametrisation by comparing two germs with identical images but different rates of approach to x. The definition through universal covers may identify more objects than a geometric equivalence of parametrised germs would; this is a proposed diagnostic, not an established defect or a novelty claim.

### Scan 255

- **Scan 255, equations (77)–(79) — unproved claim.** “Je vais définir une équivalence de catégories” promises a functor from differentiable arc germs to the fundamental groupoid of tangent directions, whose object map assigns the “demi-tangente.” Beyond the stated object map, a proof requires canonical compatible bijections on morphisms and the essential surjectivity of the tangent-ray assignment.
- **Scan 255, final paragraph — unpursued implication.** The required “bijection canonique” between arc-germ morphisms and tangent-direction morphisms makes the passage from a surface germ to its tangent circle stronger than an abstract isomorphism of local fundamental groups. Its dependence on the differentiable structure, and the precise naturality required under differentiable maps, remain to be specified on this page.
- **Scan 255, equation (79) — own idea (confidence: medium).** Test the claimed functor against curves sharing the same nonzero tangent ray but approaching it with different higher-order terms. The object map makes them identical in the tangent groupoid, so the construction should provide a coherent comparison of their universal-cover objects; this is a useful check of canonicity, not a claim of a new result.

### Scan 256

- **Scan 256, equations (80)–(81) — unproved claim.** “Je vais définir plutôt un foncteur” replaces a proposed family of morphism bijections by a functor from the direction-circle groupoid to universal covers of the punctured germ. The parenthesis “qui sera une équivalence de catégories” still requires functoriality, full faithfulness and essential surjectivity; defining the displayed object correspondence alone would not establish them.
- **Scan 256, equation (82) and final paragraph — unproved claim.** The assertion “on sait que le groupoïde enveloppant … est canoniquement équivalent” to the circle’s fundamental groupoid depends on localising the inclusion category of closed simply connected arcs. A proof can be sought by subdivision of paths and comparison of subdivisions, with special attention to degenerate arcs and exclusion of the whole circle, both written into (82).
- **Scan 256, equation (82) — own idea (confidence: medium).** Compare the localisation of the closed-arc poset with that of a small collection of overlapping arcs that still covers the circle. This could provide a concrete test of which relations recover the fundamental loop; the proposal is motivated by the explicit inclusion-category presentation and is not a claim that the reduction has already been proved.

### Scan 257

- **Scan 257, equations (83)–(84) — unproved claim.** The “équivalence canonique” is now described on point objects and on the zigzag a → A ← b. Establishing it requires showing that these arc zigzags generate all morphisms and that their relations match homotopy classes of paths, including the circle’s nontrivial winding relation.
- **Scan 257, final paragraph and equation (85) — unpursued implication.** “La donnée d’un foncteur … équivaut à la donnée d’un foncteur” starts a universal-property reformulation, whose target is supplied on the next page. The text as shown leaves open whether the equivalence is meant as a bijection of functor data, an equivalence of functor categories, or an equivalence up to specified natural isomorphism.
- **Scan 257, equation (84) — own idea (confidence: medium).** Track a concatenated sequence of small arcs that winds once around the circle and verify its image under the proposed functor. This tests whether the localisation sends the elementary zigzags to the expected fundamental-group generator and whether changing the subdivision introduces unwanted relations; it follows directly from the displayed description but is not carried out here.

### Scans 258–262

These notes are separate from the transcription. They identify tasks suggested by the local excerpt and do not certify novelty or claim that a proof is absent from the rest of the manuscript. No explicit conjecture or question has been securely identified in these five scans. References below are to the supplied scan numbers and the author’s equation numbers.

#### 1. Scan 258, after (86), condition involving (86bis)

**Kind:** unproved claim.

The criterion that (85) be an equivalence is stated in terms of connectedness, a fundamental group isomorphic to Z, and the image of the two-arc circuit being a ‘générateur’. A proof needs to show that this circuit generates the source vertex group and that sending it to a generator gives full faithfulness; the excerpt does not supply those checks here.

#### 2. Scan 258, (87)–(88)

**Kind:** unproved claim.

‘il suffit de définir un foncteur’ into 1-connected germs over D_x^* asserts a passage from such germs to universal covers. A proof must state the relevant category of germs and show that its universal-cover assignment is functorial with the required equivalence criterion.

#### 3. Scan 259, after (89)

**Kind:** unproved claim.

The revised text proposes a ‘filtre sur X-x tendant vers x’ in place of a germ of a subspace. The construction needs a precise germ-of-filter equivalence relation and a proof that the associated 1-connected germ is independent of representatives.

#### 4. Scan 259, cone paragraph and (90)

**Kind:** unproved claim.

The assertion that the elements of A_x ‘s'identifient évidemment’ with the specified closed cones is not proved here. Its verification must handle singleton arcs, excluded zero and whole-space cones, and the relation between arc inclusion and cone inclusion.

#### 5. Scan 259, last paragraph, strict containing cones

**Kind:** unpursued implication.

Replacing a single chart-image of a cone by a filter of strictly containing cones is designed to remove chart dependence, which the text explicitly notes as ‘dépend du choix de l'iso. local’. A systematic comparison with neighbourhood filters on the circle of directions would clarify which parts depend only on first-order data; the independence claim continues on the following scan.

#### 6. Scan 260, upper paragraph, image-filter construction

**Kind:** unproved claim.

The filter is said to be one ‘qui ne dépend pas du choix de f’. Proving this needs a uniform comparison of a chart change tangent to the identity with strictly enlarged cones near the origin; pointwise convergence of directions alone does not state the needed filter inclusion.

#### 7. Scan 260, middle paragraph, contractibility

**Kind:** unproved claim.

The text takes V ‘convexes fermés’ and the intersections V∩(C'−{0}) as ‘contractibles’, then concludes that the germ is 1-connected. A proof must verify the contractibility for all admitted directional arcs and justify the passage from this neighbourhood basis to covering theory of the germ.

#### 8. Scan 260, last paragraph, (88), (87), (81)

**Kind:** unproved claim.

‘on vérifie que ce dernier est bien une équivalence’ refers back to the two-arc criterion ((86bis)) without carrying out the verification on this page. The missing check is that the constructed local covers send the circuit to a generator of the relevant automorphism group.

#### 9. Scan 260, middle contractibility argument

**Kind:** own idea.

A direct polar-coordinate proof could contract an admitted sector intersection by moving its direction inside the proper arc and adjusting its positive radius inside a convex neighbourhood. Confidence: medium, because the surrounding argument is two-dimensional and the arcs are proper, but the exact class of allowed closed neighbourhoods and the treatment of endpoints must be checked; this is a proposed verification, not a claim of novelty.

#### 10. Scan 261, (91)

**Kind:** unproved claim.

The ‘morphismes d'inclusion canoniques’ from the differentiable arc germ to the germ attached to its half-tangent are asserted directly. Their construction needs the first-order control of the arc and the strict-cone filter used on the preceding pages; it is not a literal inclusion of the curved arc into a straight ray.

#### 11. Scan 261, (92) and the following Isom diagram

**Kind:** unpursued implication.

For two differentiable arcs with the same half-tangent, both displayed covers are compared with the same object Θ(Δ). This suggests a canonical comparison between their corresponding fibre functors, but the naturality and compatibility of that comparison must be checked rather than inferred from the equality of the direction alone.

#### 12. Scan 261, end of page, essentially commutative diagram

**Kind:** own idea.

One could formulate the naturality requirement as a specified natural isomorphism between the two routes around (93), rather than merely the existence of equivalent categories. Confidence: high as a bookkeeping proposal, since the text explicitly says ‘ess. comm.’ and the displayed cover comparisons supply candidate components; the coherence conditions still require verification.

#### 13. Scan 262, left marginal note beside (93)

**Kind:** unpursued implication.

The note identifies the earlier difficulty as the lack of a ‘morphisme direct entre le germe D_x^*, et l'espace S_x’. This distinguishes the equivalence of covering groupoids from an explicitly given map of the underlying germ to the circle; a direct realization would require an additional construction and its invariance properties.

#### 14. Scan 262, (94) and its following line

**Kind:** unproved claim.

The equivalence is ‘défini comme composé de Θ^{-1} avec le foncteur can.’. Interpreting the inverse as a quasi-inverse of an equivalence requires recording its dependence on choices, or the canonical natural-isomorphism class of the resulting functor; that coherence is not detailed in this paragraph.

#### 15. Scan 262, final paragraph around repeated (90)

**Kind:** unpursued implication.

The passage says the construction can be made explicit as ‘une construction canonique dans un espace vectoriel V’. Comparing that explicit local model across changes of coordinates with the same differential is a concrete way to test the earlier assertion that the strict-cone filter is independent of the chosen local isomorphism; the paragraph begins that model but continues beyond this page.

### Scan 263

- **Scan 263, lines 5–10; unproved claim.** “Il faut voir comment … dépend ‘continûment’ de Δ” is followed by “tout à fait standard”. A proof would need to specify the parameter space of rays, the category in which the universal coverings vary, and the precise meaning of continuity; the adjective does not itself provide these definitions.
- **Scan 263, lines 11–end; unpursued implication.** An automorphism fixing x and differentiable there induces automorphisms of the punctured germ and of the circle of tangent rays. The following comparison must track both actions on lift torsors, rather than merely compare abstract fundamental groups.
- **Scan 263, first paragraph; own idea; medium confidence.** A useful model to test is a real oriented two-dimensional vector space with the covering of its nonzero vectors parameterized by a real angular coordinate. This may make the dependence on Δ explicit, but an angular coordinate requires an auxiliary choice, so it would not alone establish the claimed invariant construction.

### Scan 264

- **Scan 264, (96) and adjacent upper-left margin; unproved claim.** The “bijection canonique” between the two sets of lifts is asserted to be an isomorphism of orientation-module torsors. The marginal note says the construction “sera faite dans les pages qui suivent” and points to (122), p. 783; those later pages are outside the present attachment range.
- **Scan 264, paragraph before 1); question / expectation.** “J'ai envie de donner une description axiomatique de (94) et (96)” announces an intended axiomatization. The following pages should be read as specifying the data and compatibility conditions of this comparison, not as a completed proof of every assertion in (96).
- **Scan 264, 1), cone and arc definitions; unpursued implication.** The correspondence between arcs of the tangent circle and proper closed cones permits a local construction indexed by an ordered family of subsets. A rigorous treatment must specify exactly which degenerate arcs are included and how the germ associated with a cone is defined independently of a chart.
- **Scan 264, (96); own idea; medium confidence.** Test the asserted torsor isomorphism separately on a linear orientation-preserving map and a reflection. The reflection is especially useful because its action changes the sign on the orientation module, so it can expose a hidden equivariance convention that a positive rotation would not reveal.

### Scan 265

- **Scan 265, (97)–(98); unproved claim.** The two sets of sections are said to be “l'un et l'autre Torseurs” over the same orientation module, and H(A) is said to be a torsor as well. This requires nonemptiness of the section sets and simple transitivity of the stated actions, including at singleton arcs and for the germ Ep(A).
- **Scan 265, (99)–(101); unproved claim.** Restriction along A⊂A′ is asserted to give “des isom. de … torseurs”, hence a canonical map H(A)→H(A′). A proof should establish that the restriction maps are bijections and verify the identity and composition laws, with the variance in (99) distinguished from that in (100).

The diagram isolates a useful universal-property step, but the subsequent claim that the resulting torsor-valued functor has trivial transport requires additional geometric input on the next page.
- **Scan 265, (98)–(102); own idea; medium confidence.** H can be viewed as a system of comparison torsors for two systems of local sections. This suggests checking whether its monodromy is the difference of the two section monodromies, but the signs and left/right action conventions must be fixed before this becomes a proof.

### Scan 266

- **Scan 266, opening and (103)–(105) — unproved claim.** « On sait que » introduces the assertion that the enveloping groupoid is a T_x-groupoid and that the functor to universal coverings is an equivalence. A full verification would identify its objects and all morphism torsors, including how the diagonal marginal reformulation of (105) compares with the overwritten main formula.
- **Scan 266, middle paragraph — unproved claim.** « je dis que le foncteur … est essentiellement constant » is followed by the explicit zero homomorphism on fundamental groups. The argument on this page does not prove that zero-monodromy assertion; a proof must compute the transport of the comparison torsor around a generator, rather than infer constancy merely from the existence of isomorphisms between its values.
- **Scan 266, final paragraph and (106) — unpursued implication.** The stated « système transitif d'isomorphismes » is used to define a common value H of the two chosen universal coverings. The compatibility required of the maps i_A is therefore part of the construction's content; the sentence stating that compatibility continues beyond the supplied excerpt.
- **Scan 266, essential constancy — own idea.** Compare the monodromy of the two section torsors around a pair of complementary arcs in the direction circle, then compute the induced monodromy on their Isom torsor. # LM_C4-267-280 — cote 140-4, scans 267–280  [source: answers\unzipped\LM_C4-267-280\LM_C4-267-280_notes.md]

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

Locations refer to the supplied scans and equation numbers (Grothendieck, 1981). “Unproved claim” means that the indicated verification is not supplied at that location, not that the claim is unknown or absent from the wider manuscript. Own ideas are labelled with their confidence and reason; none is presented as new or established.

1. **Scan 267, text around (108)–(109); kind: unproved claim.** The functors are said to “se factorisent en des équivalences.” A proof at this point would need to establish the asserted passage to the groupoid completion, full faithfulness, and essential surjectivity for both covering categories; these checks are not supplied on this page. The remark that the functors are independent of the chosen universal covers should also be distinguished from independence of any chosen natural identifications.

2. **Scan 267, final paragraph; kind: unpursued implication.** The words “par la propriété univ.” reduce the particular geometric construction to a comparison of functors on connected `T`-groupoids. This suggests that the geometric independence statement may be isolated as an abstract lemma about torsor-valued functors; the following pages need to be checked for the extent to which they complete that reduction.

3. **Scan 267, (110) and final paragraph; kind: own idea; confidence: medium.** One could audit the claimed naturality by evaluating every displayed isomorphism on a chosen object and then on its automorphism group, keeping the side of the `T`-action explicit. The reason for this suggestion is that a representable torsor comparison can conceal an inverse or an opposite-action convention; it is a proposed verification procedure, not an assertion that an error occurs here.

4. **Scan 268, (113)–(116); kind: unpursued implication.** The assertion that the comparison functor is “essᵗ. constant” is given an argument through quasi-inverses and the torsor isomorphism in (116), rather than left as an unsupported claim. What remains worth checking separately is the precise meaning of essential constancy and the dependence of the resulting identification on the selected quasi-inverses; the text only needs an essentially constant functor at this step.

5. **Scan 268, (114)–(116); kind: own idea; confidence: high for the proposed check.** A careful rederivation should give distinct names to the two quasi-inverses and track them through both representable functors. This is prompted by the visible `G_1` / `F_2` switch, and is an editorial verification proposal, not a correction to the transcription or a claim that the underlying result fails.

6. **Scan 269, paragraph after the definition; kind: unproved claim.** The statement “Cette identification est compatible” with inclusions of arcs invokes compatibility of the `H(A)` descriptions across `A ⊂ A'`. A complete verification would compare the restriction maps on both section torsors and check that the comparison isomorphism commutes with them; this page asserts the compatibility without displaying that square.

7. **Scan 269, torsor sentence; kind: unproved claim.** The correlations are said to “forment un torseur sous `T_x`.” To make the claim explicit one must specify the action and verify nonemptiness, freeness, and transitivity, including how the identification of the deck groups is used. The result may rely on the preceding construction of `H`, so it should not be interpreted as an independent conjecture.

8. **Scan 269, (117); kind: unproved claim.** The two forgetful functors are asserted to be “des équivalences de catégories.” Their proof requires existence of a compatible partner cover and unique lifting of a morphism once a correlation is fixed; the statement compresses these categorical checks into the diagram.

9. **Scan 269, (117); kind: own idea; confidence: medium.** Treat the category of correlated triples as a common comparison category and verify the two projections directly, rather than selecting a universal cover globally. This may provide a convenient way to organize later functoriality checks, because both forgetful functors and their morphisms are retained in one object of study; no novelty claim is intended.

10. **Scan 270, opening paragraph; kind: unproved claim.** “Toutes ces constructions” are said to have been made intrinsically enough to pass to isomorphisms of differentiable surface germs. To verify that assertion one must check independence of representatives and compatibility with shrinking neighbourhoods for the induced circle, punctured-disc, and deck-group maps in (118); these checks are not expanded here.

11. **Scan 270, (119)–(120); kind: unproved claim.** The lift sets are asserted to be `T_x`-torsors and to admit “un iso. can.” between them. The page begins a justification by “transport de structure” and continues onto the next scan, so the local proof should be read across that page boundary rather than judged complete here.

12. **Scan 270, (120); kind: own idea; confidence: medium.** After verifying the lift-set bijection for one germ isomorphism, test its compatibility with identity maps and composition of two germ isomorphisms. This is a necessary check if the construction is to produce a group of compatible lifts later, and follows from the intended functorial setting without being asserted here as an established additional result.

The nontrivial check would be independence from the auxiliary section and open set, so this is a proposed reconstruction, not an asserted result or a claim of novelty.

A detailed proof needs the precise definition of that family and a chain of inclusions joining any two of its members; the page states this connectivity assertion without constructing such chains.

Whether that reformulation adds anything useful depends on the exact definition of the indexing family on earlier pages; it is not asserted here as an established or novel theorem.

An explicit construction should give the composition law, show that composition and inversion preserve the specified lifting relation, and verify the projection; the written assignment in the final line has a visible tilde on its output and must be checked rather than editorially repaired.

This is an announced construction to be checked, rather than a completed existence proof on this page; one must specify the topology on the lift group, verify the group operations, and compare the subspace and quotient topologies with the proposed kernel and quotient.

A direct proof should identify a global lift with independent local lifts having the same element of G below them, and verify that this identification respects multiplication; after topologies are introduced, its topological compatibility must also be established.

One can test that reading by computing conjugation on each T_x and checking whether it yields a sign character at each fixed point; this interpretation is an inference from the cancelled bound, not a claim that the manuscript completes that argument.

## 5. Research notes

These notes are separate from the transcription. A claim described as unproved is unproved in the indicated local passage of this supplied extract, not necessarily elsewhere in the manuscript or literature. Questions and possible implications are recorded even when later pages may address them. All items labelled **own idea** are proposed checks or interpretations, with confidence and reasons; none is asserted to be new.

### Scan 2

### R02.1 — Scan 2, bottom left — conjecture (question)

Grothendieck writes a question mark over the equality in `det a = delta_alpha^{-1} mu`. This is a local computational question, not a conjecture about a named theory. A check would first require establishing exactly which matrix is denoted by `alpha`, whether `delta_alpha` is its determinant, and the readings of the overwritten triangular matrix entries; those definitions are not made explicit on this sheet.

### R02.2 — Scan 2, lower-right box — unpursued implication

The boxed expression `a = (mu/delta_alpha)(-c/v rho+d)` suggests an expression for `a` in the algebra generated by `rho`. The relevant denominators and the sign in the box require verification before one can formulate the domain on which such an expression is valid. The unfinished calculation of its determinant is a natural continuation, but any completed identity belongs in commentary and must not replace the draft.

### R02.3 — Scan 2, determinant formulas — own idea

One could compare the two determinant computations using a purely symbolic calculation with separate variables for every ambiguous coefficient, then inspect which alternatives are compatible with the written matrix product. Confidence: high that this would be a useful diagnostic, because it would expose consequences of each reading without choosing one from context. It would not establish what the ink says, and consistency must not be used as a silent emendation.

### Scans 4, 6, and 8

1. **Scan 4, top and middle — unpursued implication.** The presentation `\{\tilde\rho,\tilde\sigma\mid\tilde\rho^n=\tilde\sigma^2\}` and the displayed product `\tilde\rho_{n-1}\cdots\tilde\rho_0=\tilde\omega_0^2` suggest comparing the central generator of the ambient extension with the product of peripheral lifts. The calculation on the page is directed at the displayed product in its notation, but the consequences for the extension class are not developed here.
2. **Scan 4, lower third — unproved claim.** The page writes an exact sequence involving the presentation with the relation “central i.e.” and then an identification involving `\mathbb Z\bar\omega` and `\mathbb Z\omega`. A proof of that presentation and identification would need to establish the kernel and the absence of further relations, rather than only the displayed product relation.
3. **Scan 4, final lines — own idea.** It may be useful to formulate the final identification as a change of central kernel along the displayed map `\bar\omega_0\to\omega_0^2`, and to check it directly from the two presentations. **Confidence: medium:** the map and the two cyclic central groups are visible, but the final binary operation and some decorations are uncertain; this is a proposed verification, not an assertion about the intended construction or its novelty.
4. **Scan 6, top — conjecture (question).** The explicit question is “est-il invariant dans” the decorated ambient group, followed by another question “par” `\tilde\sigma` “?”. The page contrasts the clear action of `\tilde\rho` with the action of `\tilde\sigma`, whose effect is then calculated on peripheral generators.
5. **Scan 6, top and parity paragraph — unproved claim.** The parenthesis “ss-groupe d'indice 2” and the condition that the central exponents be congruent to zero modulo 2 are stated without a separate proof on this page. Verification would require a precise characterization of the subgroup in terms of the parity of the central coordinate and justification that checking the displayed generators is sufficient.
6. **Scan 6, middle to bottom — unpursued implication.** The intention “On va essayer de les calculer au moins” `z_0,z_1` is followed by two products ending in 1, then the start of a general-index calculation. The displayed special calculations suggest checking whether all correction factors vanish, while the unfinished general product leaves that broader verification open on this page.
7. **Scan 6, parity paragraph — own idea.** A useful independent check would be to reduce the central correction exponents modulo 2 and test whether the resulting obstruction to invariance is a homomorphism or a cocycle for the visible action. **Confidence: medium:** the text explicitly supplies central powers and a parity condition, but the action convention and some superscripts remain uncertain, so this is a research procedure rather than an established interpretation.
8. **Scan 8, upper-right margin — unproved claim.** “Cette extension n'est pas scindée” is asserted next to the presentation of `\mathbb D'_3` and the central extension by `\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z`, with a short parenthetical explanation about orders. A careful proof should compare the orders of lifts of the quotient generators; the parenthetical generator and numeral readings are not secure enough to use as an unquestioned proof.
9. **Scan 8, large diagram and right-hand sequences — unpursued implication.** The nested central groups and the arrows labelled `\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z`, `\Pi_{0,3}`, and `\mathbb D_3` invite checking that the successive quotient descriptions yield the same finite-group and matrix-group extensions. The sheet supplies the diagrams but no separate verification of exactness and commutativity for every displayed path.
10. **Scan 8, last identification — unproved claim.** The matrix-group quotient is identified with a fundamental group written `\Pi_1(\ldots;P_+)`. To verify this identification, one would need to settle the object and action in the partly overwritten argument, specify the base point, and match the presentations or monodromy maps; none of those details is supplied in the adjacent diagram.
11. **Scan 8, marginal order explanation — own idea.** If the small parenthesis really says that both lifts of rho have order 6, it should be tested directly by multiplying a lift by the central element in the displayed presentation. **Confidence: medium for the proposed check, low for the exact premise:** the parenthesis may instead name another generator or different numerals, so a possible algebraic discrepancy must remain separate from the diplomatic reading and must not be used to change it.

### Scans 10, 12, 14, and 15

### Grothendieck's questions, provisional claims, and implications

1. **Scan 10, upper right; kind: conjecture (question).** The quotient annotation explicitly leaves a “sous-groupe d'ordre 2” “à déterminer.” The immediate task is to identify which subgroup, ambient group, and map the annotation is intended to describe, then check the kernel and the surrounding cyclic projections. The nearby order 36 is visible, but the crowded arrows should be resolved before attributing a final quotient claim to the author.

2. **Scan 10, middle presentation of E; kind: unproved claim.** The draft labels the group 36 and writes that the indicated relator is “invariant” and “d'ordre |3.” These lines do not contain a complete finite-order proof. An explicit model and mutually inverse presentation maps, or a normal-form argument with a matching lower bound, would be needed to establish the order and verify the listed images of rho, sigma, and omega.

3. **Scan 10, upper and lower diagrams; kind: unpursued implication.** The same order-18 fibre product is displayed together with a tentative finite-field product description and maps to D3 and Z/6Z. An explicit comparison of those descriptions would determine which order-two action is intended on the two three-element factors and which factor is detected by each projection. The transcription leaves the action/product sign uncertain, so that comparison should be reported independently of the palaeographic reading.

4. **Scan 12, diagonal proposition and lower calculations; kind: unproved claim.** The proposition begins “Il existe des relèvements” and ends with a presentation after the assertion of uniqueness. The accompanying equations give part of the arithmetic construction, and scan 14 continues the parity calculation, but a full argument would also need to justify how the chosen central extension is identified by those lift relations and how the claimed uniqueness depends on the chosen exponent. Several words in the proposition are uncertain, so its exact scope must be fixed before treating it as a theorem statement.

5. **Scan 14, final two-value set; kind: unpursued implication.** The concluding condition is “nu impair” for the two values -(n-1)/2 and (n+1)/2. For odd n, their parity selects the positive representative when n is 1 modulo 4 and the negative representative when n is 3 modulo 4. This reformulation would make the dependence on n transparent without changing the manuscript's calculation or the surviving notation.

6. **Scan 15, quotient display under diagonal cancellation; kind: unproved claim.** The cancelled display places the numbers 72, 6, and 24 under the quotient and its two factors. An independent verification would require the reduction map modulo 6, its relation to the two reductions modulo 2 and modulo 3, and the exact identification of the central sign quotient. Because the block is crossed, it should be recorded as a draft calculation rather than an endorsed final statement.

### Own ideas and proposed checks

7. **Scan 10 upper diagram, compared with scan 15 quotient display; kind: own idea. Confidence: high as a consistency check, not as a reading correction.** Explicitly compare the adjacent order-36 label and “d'ordre 2” annotation with the factor orders 6 and 24 written on scan 15. Counting those factors and the proposed kernel would test whether the annotations belong to the same quotient or to different stages of the diagram. This is a reason to investigate the maps, not to replace the printed order or subgroup size in the transcription.

8. **Scans 12 and 14, lift adjustments; kind: own idea. Confidence: high.** Revisit what changes when n is even, rather than formally substituting an even n into alpha=(n-1)/2. The homogeneous relation 2 gamma=n beta has integral solutions generated by (2/d,n/d), where d=gcd(2,n); the author's beta=2x, gamma=nx uses the odd case. This elementary distinction offers a precise test of which existence or uniqueness statements actually require the initial “n impair.”

9. **Scan 15, mod-3 tensor line; kind: own idea. Confidence: medium.** Investigate the permutation action on F3^3/F3, where the denominator denotes the diagonal line in the most direct reading. In characteristic 3 that diagonal line lies in the sum-zero subspace, so the latter yields a one-dimensional subquotient. This could clarify the crossed or blotted superscript in the neighbouring expression and the role of the three peripheral generators, but the proposed interpretation must not be substituted for the uncertain exponent 0|1.

10. **Scan 15, cancelled commutator expansion; kind: own idea. Confidence: medium.** Check the displayed word in a concrete matrix or finite-group model using the relations actually written on that page, then compare intermediate reductions with each surviving cancellation. Such a calculation may expose which assumption the author was testing or rejecting. It cannot settle an invisible inverse exponent or prove what an obliterated relator originally said.

These research notes are observations and possible verification tasks grounded in the four supplied scans. They make no claim of priority or novelty and have not been used to amend the transcription.

### Scans 16–19

These are working research prompts, not corrections to the diplomatic text. No external transcription has been used to settle a reading. A claim noted here may be proved elsewhere in the manuscript; these notes record only what is left open in the supplied local passage.

### Scan 16, upper-left margin — unproved claim / explicit verification marker

The words “à vérifier” and the later-looking “OK” occur together beside the initial construction. The object of the verification is not attached by an unambiguous insertion sign, so it should not automatically be restricted to either the pullback square or the asserted identification of `M_{1,1}`. The local pages do not supply the check that the `OK` may record.

### Scan 16, upper square and paragraph — unproved claim

The text calls `D'_3` an extension “non triviale” and specifies an action through `D_3`, followed by a compressed statement about the central kernel acting trivially. A proof should first fix the actual group in the square and the meaning of the pair `(U_{0,3},D'_3)`, then establish the pullback and the claimed kernel action. The ambiguous final subscripts in the prose must be resolved independently of this expected construction.

### Scan 16, upper square — own idea

If the diagram is the fiber product of `D_3 → Z/2Z` and `Z/4Z → Z/2Z`, restrict it to an order-two subgroup mapping nontrivially to `Z/2Z`; its inverse image should be cyclic of order four, providing a direct test of non-splitting. **Confidence: high for this conditional group calculation, medium for its applicability to the uncertain local notation.** This is a verification route, not a claim of a new result.

### Scan 16, middle identification — unproved claim

The equation identifying `T_{11}` with the pointed fundamental group of `(U_{0,3},D'_3)` is accompanied by a choice of a point in the Poincaré half-plane over `P_+`. A proof should state the fundamental-group convention for an action with ineffective kernel, construct the covering or groupoid model, and track the point choice. The note “dépend du choix” is material: a bare unpointed abstract isomorphism would not reproduce all that is asserted here.

### Scan 16, right slanted margin — unproved claim

“On vérifie alors aisément que” introduces a presentation identified with `SL(2,Z)`. Once the clipped exponents are securely recovered, one could verify the proposed lifts by matrices and check that the displayed relations give the whole group, not just relations satisfied in a quotient. The note's wording is more legible than its final presentation, so the precise proposition should remain provisional.

### Scan 16, lower squares — unpursued implication

The factorization “via `D_3`” appears to retain an order-two ineffective central action when forming the group-theoretic extension. It is worth checking explicitly how this kernel survives in the pointed action-groupoid fundamental group and what is lost by replacing the action-groupoid quotient by its coarse orbit space. This consequence is conditional on the reading of the kernel paragraph; it is not an additional assertion inserted into the manuscript.

### Scan 17, upper third, cancelled block — unproved claim

The three pairwise stabilizer-intersection equations are followed by injections into products of quotient sets. The group-theoretic implication from a trivial intersection to the corresponding injection is straightforward once the coset conventions are fixed; the geometric assertion requiring proof is that the chosen stabilizers have those intersections. The third written quotient repeats `H_A`, so its intended geometric role must not be reconstructed by silently changing that denominator.

### Scan 17, middle, cancelled block — unproved claim

The formula `R ≃ A_1 ×_A A_2` and the three image formulas appear to package incidence data or flags. A proof needs the precise definitions of `S,A,F` and the incidence objects, together with the conditions ensuring that the fiber product gives exactly the intended triples. The uncertain first inequality in the inserted description matters for that formulation.

### Scan 17, orientation display and final line — unproved claim

The cancelled identifications after passage to `Omega` are followed by an uncancelled-looking equivalence involving `Pol_tau^or` and `Pol_tau` with a corrected `/Omega` suffix. It is necessary first to determine whether that suffix denotes a slice, another fiber construction, or a quotient, and then construct the proposed equivalence with its morphisms. An interpretation based solely on objects would not establish the categorical statement.

### Scan 17, incidence reconstruction — own idea

Test the written incidence reconstruction on a small explicit polyhedron, keeping separately the unoriented flags and choices of orientation, and enumerate the resulting fiber products and images. **Confidence: medium**, because this is a useful consistency test but the precise categorical conventions and two handwritten labels remain unresolved. The test should preserve the manuscript's repeated denominator as a separate case rather than repair it beforehand.

### Scan 18, top presentation — unproved claim

The statement “image inverse” identifies `ST_{1,1}` with a subgroup of a covering group, followed by the presentation `rho^3=sigma^2`. A proof would need a precise choice of the ambient covering group and lifts of generators, then an identification of the central element represented by the common power. The overwritten ambient initials are therefore a substantive palaeographic issue, not cosmetic notation.

### Scan 18, central square — unproved claim

The margin says that `ST_{11}` “se déduit” from `T_{11}` by inverse image of the canonical extension of `Z/12Z` by `Z`. To verify this, show that the homomorphism to `Z` has the displayed values on generators and identifies the kernel map with multiplication by 12, then prove the square is a pullback. The word “cartésien” is itself cancelled in the drawing, while the marginal prose states the inverse-image construction; both states of the draft should be kept in view.

### Scan 18, two abelianization headings — own idea

Compare the two literal headings `(T_{11})_ab` with the presentation and quotient line before making any editorial decision: the displayed target groups are `Z` and `Z/12Z`. Computing the abelianization of the group presented by `rho^3=sigma^2` and of the indicated central quotient may identify the intended distinction, but it cannot establish that an unseen `S` was written. **Confidence: high that this is a useful conditional algebraic check; low that it resolves the handwriting without another witness.**

The words “Mais attention” and an underlined negative occur in a qualification about the preceding normalization-like construction. The technical noun, the adjective beginning `stricte...`, and the sentence's exact restriction are too uncertain to state as a theorem or counterexample. The first research step is to recover those words and the object `(K,...)`; no mathematical completion has been proposed in the transcription.

“On montrera” announces a relation between topological and algebraic construction after the title about groups and fundamental groupoids. The supplied passage gives an outline, not the comparison construction or its hypotheses. A future check should determine the intended categories and the precise comparison morphisms before importing a standard comparison theorem.

The replacements of the lifted generators by powers of the central element culminate in `1+2s=(1-n)/2` and “OK si” that last quantity is odd. This suggests a parity obstruction to making the two altered powers coincide with the chosen central power. The conclusion must remain conditional on the ambiguous exponent in the sigma line and on the relation between barred and unbarred omega.

For integer `n`, the literal condition that `(1-n)/2` be odd is equivalent to `n ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, and the written linear equation would give `s=-(n+1)/4`. **Confidence: high for this arithmetic consequence of the displayed equation; medium for its intended role**, because the altered-generator calculation has two uncertain symbols. Testing `n=3` and `n=7` is a useful check of the signs before attempting a general interpretation.

Reconstruct a combinatorial description of the sphere routes and the distinguished-path field, including basepoints, directions and labels, before identifying an action of the two named generators. The tentative caption reading “sentiers distingués” is compatible with that route, but must not decide the uncertain labels or the role of the two long diagonals. **Confidence: low**, because several overwritten labels and the caption ending are unresolved; this is a proposed investigation, not an established geometric interpretation.

## 5. Research notes — English, separate from the transcription

These items identify questions for subsequent checking against the surrounding manuscript and the literature. They do not establish novelty, complete the author’s proofs, or alter the transcription. All scan-specific quotations and claims refer to the supplied primary images (Grothendieck, 1981, indicated scan); the year is the task’s catalogue designation. “Unproved claim” means that a complete proof is not given on these supplied pages, even where a sketch or calculation is present. Items labelled “own idea” are editorial proposals with their confidence and reason stated.
